items.title: Last Warthog Departs Nellis as Base’s A-10 Era Comes to a Close
items.author: Steve Losey
items.summary: Nellis Air Force Base, Nev.—a longtime hub for A-10 Thunderbolt II tactical training, operational testing and maintenance—ended nearly a half-century of flying the venerable Warthog on Sept. 22. The post Last Warthog Departs Nellis as Base’s A-10 Era Comes to a Close appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
Nellis Air Force Base, Nev.—a longtime hub for A-10 Thunderbolt II tactical training, operational testing and maintenance—ended nearly a half-century of flying the venerable Warthog on Sept. 22.

The Air Force said in a Sept. 23 statement that nearly 70 Airmen lined up on the flightline at Nellis for a final salute as the last Warthog there took off.

Nellis has flown A-10s since 1977. The base has been the Air Force’s primary proving ground for A-10 tactical employment, and units have worked to refine its software, avionics and precision weapons, the Air Force said.

The 66th Weapons Squadron at Nellis’ U.S. Air Force Weapons School has also trained more than 300 A-10 weapons officers in 100 classes, the Air Force said.

With its heavy armor and withering GAU-8 30mm cannon, the A-10 was originally built to be a Soviet tank killer and played a central role in the Gulf War against Saddam Hussein’s army. But in the Global War on Terror, the A-10 became best known as a reliable close air support platform to defend U.S. and partner nations’ ground troops when they were besieged by insurgents.

The A-10 also carries out a close air support mission dubbed Sandy during combat search and rescue operations, most recently in April during the successful rescue of two F-15E air crew who were shot down in Iran.

For years, though, the Air Force has tried to retire its A-10 fleet amid concerns that it would not be survivable against an advanced enemy. Congressional opposition has thwarted those plans before, but that has softened in recent years.

The service had pressed to retire all 162 of its remaining A-10s by the end of fiscal 2026, but after the Iran war began and the rescue of the F-15E crew, the Pentagon announced it would delay at least some Warthogs’ retirement until at least 2030.

Still, the fleet and its accompanying enterprise are slowly winding down. Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Arizona, another longtime A-10 hub, graduated its last class of new Warthog pilots in April and held its farewell flights for its last aircraft in July. The maintenance depot for the A-10, at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, also closed this year.

The Air Force stressed that while the A-10 is retiring, the service will not let its close air support capability fade.

“Foundational tactical expertise, operational roles and personnel are transitioning to multirole and advanced fighter platforms across the service,” the Air Force said in its statement.

The F-35, for example, is taking on CAS and combat search-and-rescue roles, the service said, taking advantage of its fifth-generation stealth capabilities, advanced sensor suites, and secure data-sharing networks to carry out precision ground support missions in contested environments.

The 66th is working to teach pilots of other fighters how to take on the Warthog’s traditional missions, squadron commander Lt. Col. Ridge Flick said. The unit will also keep training combat rescue officers, pararescue Airmen, special tactics officers, and combat controllers, he said.

“We are maintaining the culture of the A-10 by involving as many other fighter communities involved in the close air support mission,” Flick said in the statement. “We are also training F-15 Eagle, F-35 Lightning II and F-16 Fighting Falcon pilots to take on some roles we have had in combat search and rescue.”

Airmen who used to repair and sustain A-10s at Nellos as part of the 757th Aircraft Maintenance Squadron’s Thunder Aircraft Maintenance Unit are being reassigned to other squadrons and airframes like the F-35 and F-16, the statement said.

“The discipline that A-10 maintainers developed over 50 years of managing airframe fatigue, wing replacements and depot-level overhauls is being integrated into those newer flight line programs,” the Air Force said.
zhParas: 内利斯空军基地（Nellis Air Force Base）位于内华达州，长期以来是A-10 Thunderbolt II战术训练、作战测试与维护的中心，该基地于9月22日结束了近半个世纪飞行这款久负盛名的“疣猪”的历史。
空军在9月23日的一份声明中说，当最后一架“疣猪”从内利斯起飞时，近70名空军人员在停机坪列队，向它致以最后的敬礼。
内利斯自1977年起就一直在飞A-10。空军说，该基地一直是空军A-10战术运用的主要试验场，各部队一直致力于改进其软件、航电设备和精确制导武器。
空军说，内利斯美国空军武器学校的第66武器中队还在100期培训班中培训了300多名A-10武器官。
凭借厚重装甲和威力惊人的GAU-8 30毫米机炮，A-10最初被设计为对付苏联坦克的“坦克杀手”，并在针对萨达姆·侯赛因（Saddam Hussein）军队的海湾战争中发挥了核心作用。但在全球反恐战争中，A-10最为人所知的是作为可靠的近距空中支援平台，在美国及伙伴国地面部队遭叛乱分子围困时为其提供防护。
A-10还在战斗搜救行动中执行代号“桑迪”（Sandy）的近距空中支援任务，最近一次是在4月，成功救援了两名在伊朗上空被击落的F-15E机组人员。
不过，多年来空军一直试图让A-10机队退役，原因是担心它在面对先进对手时难以生存。国会的反对此前曾使这些计划受挫，但近年来这种反对已有所缓和。
空军曾力推在2026财年结束前将其剩余的162架A-10全部退役，但在伊朗战争爆发以及F-15E机组获救之后，五角大楼宣布将至少部分“疣猪”的退役时间至少推迟到2030年。
尽管如此，这支机队及其配套体系仍在缓慢收尾。位于亚利桑那州的戴维斯-蒙森空军基地是另一个长期以来的 A-10 中心，该基地于 4 月送走了最后一批新“疣猪”飞行员，并于 7 月为其最后一批飞机举行了告别飞行。位于犹他州希尔空军基地的 A-10 维修站也在今年关闭。
美国空军强调，尽管 A-10 正在退役，但空军不会让其近距离空中支援能力消退。
“基础战术专长、作战角色和人员正在整个空军范围内向多用途和先进战斗机平台过渡，”空军在声明中说。
空军表示，例如 F-35 正在承担近距离空中支援和战斗搜救任务，利用其第五代隐身能力、先进传感器套件和安全数据共享网络，在争议环境中执行精确地面支援任务。
中队指挥官 Lt. Col. 里奇·弗利克（Ridge Flick）说，第66中队正在教导其他战斗机的飞行员如何承担“疣猪”的传统任务。他说，该部队还将继续训练战斗救援军官、伞降救援空军人员、特种战术军官和战斗控制员。
“通过让尽可能多的其他战斗机群体参与近距离空中支援任务，我们正在延续 A-10 的文化，”弗利克在声明中说。“我们还在训练 F-15 Eagle、F-35 Lightning II 和 F-16 Fighting Falcon 飞行员，以承担我们在战斗搜救中曾承担的一些角色。”
声明称，过去作为第757飞机维修中队“雷霆”飞机维修分队的一部分，在内利斯维修和保障 A-10 的空军人员，正被重新分配到其他中队以及 F-35 和 F-16 等机型。
“A-10 维护人员在 50 年里管理机体疲劳、更换机翼和进行基地级大修所养成的纪律，正被融入那些较新的外场项目，”空军说。

items.summary: The final Officer of the Deck watch stander departs the Whidbey Island-class dock landing ship USS Germantown (LSD 42) during the ship’s decommissioning ceremony, Sept. 24, 2026. Commissioned on Feb. 8, 1986 in Seattle, Germantown completes its service after more than 40 years of service. Modern U.S. Dock Landing Ships perform multiple missions including Amphibious Warfare, Air Warfare (AW), and Surface Warfare (SUW). They are surface combatants capable of supporting expeditionary strike groups,
items.body:
The final Officer of the Deck watch stander departs the Whidbey Island-class dock landing ship USS Germantown (LSD 42) during the ship’s decommissioning ceremony, Sept.

Commissioned on Feb.

8, 1986 in Seattle, Germantown completes its service after more than 40 years of service.

Dock Landing Ships perform multiple missions including Amphibious Warfare, Air Warfare (AW), and Surface Warfare (SUW).

They are surface combatants capable of supporting expeditionary strike groups, amphibious forces or operating independently.

Commander, Naval Surface Force, U.

Pacific Fleet ensures fleet commanders are equipped with personnel, materiel and training required to project credible naval power at sea, ashore, at home and abroad.

Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 3rd Class Nate Jordan)
zhParas: 在9月举行的惠德贝岛级船坞登陆舰“日耳曼敦”号（USS Germantown，LSD 42）退役仪式上，最后一名担任舰上值班军官（Officer of the Deck）的值班人员离开该舰。
于2月
8日，1986年，在西雅图服役，“日耳曼敦”号在服役40多年后结束服役。
船坞登陆舰执行多种任务，包括两栖作战、空战（AW）和水面战（SUW）。
它们是水面战斗舰艇，能够支援远征打击群、两栖部队或独立作战。
美国海军水面部队司令部司令，U.
太平洋舰队确保舰队指挥官拥有在海上、岸上、国内和国外投射可信海军力量所需的人员、物资和训练。
美国海军照片，由海军三等大众传播专家内特·乔丹（Nate Jordan）拍摄）

items.title: NPS Graduate Applies Virtual Modeling Research to Strengthen Military Energy Resilience
items.author: SN Katherine Eldridge
items.summary: U.S. Marine Corps Capt. Dylan Bruns will graduate from the Naval Postgraduate School (NPS), Sept. 25, after completing the Electronics Systems Engineering program, where his research explored how virtual models can help engineers better understand and test military power systems before units rely on them in the field.
items.body:
MONTEREY, Calif. – U.S. Marine Corps Capt. Dylan Bruns will graduate from the Naval Postgraduate School (NPS), Sept. 25, after completing the Electronics Systems Engineering program, where his research explored how virtual models can help engineers better understand and test military power systems before units rely on them in the field.

Bruns moved frequently growing up and claims Greenwood, Indiana, as his hometown, where he graduated high school.

At NPS, Bruns built a digital twin of a microgrid, a compact power system that provides electricity to specific areas or facilities. He compared the digital model with measurements from a working microgrid to see how closely the virtual system reflected the real one.

“A better ability to model and test these systems can help engineers understand how they will perform before relying on them in operational environments,” Bruns said.

NPS gave Bruns the resources to take his research beyond a computer model and test whether it could reflect the behavior of a real power system. With access to a laboratory, equipment, and faculty expertise, he was able to connect the virtual side of his research with the kind of equipment engineers would work with on the field. Through that work, Bruns saw how microgrids could address power challenges well beyond the military.

“Power demand is increasing while much of our electrical infrastructure is aging,” Bruns said. “Microgrids provide an actionable path toward integrating technologies such as renewable energy while also localizing power production for critical infrastructure, whether that is a military installation, a hospital or another facility that cannot afford to lose power.”

Following graduation, Bruns will report to Marine Corps Systems Command in Quantico, Virginia, where he will work with mid-range intercept capabilities.

“I expect I will have a great deal to learn when I arrive, but NPS has given me a strong enough technical foundation to understand the systems, ask better questions, and speak the same language as the experts I will be working with,” Bruns said.

Located in Monterey, California, NPS is a naval command and graduate university that provides defense-focused education and research, preparing students to return to the fleet and force with knowledge they can apply to military challenges.

For more information about the Naval Postgraduate School, visit https://nps.edu/ .
zhParas: 加利福尼亚州蒙特雷——美国海军陆战队 Capt. 迪伦·布伦斯（Dylan Bruns）将于9月25日从美国海军研究生院（NPS）毕业，此前他完成了电子系统工程专业的学习。他的研究探讨了虚拟模型如何帮助工程师在部队于实地依赖军用电力系统之前，更好地理解和测试这些系统。
布伦斯在成长过程中经常搬家，自称家乡是印第安纳州格林伍德，并在那里高中毕业。
在NPS，布伦斯构建了一个微电网的数字孪生体。微电网是一种紧凑型电力系统，为特定区域或设施供电。他将该数字模型与一个运行中的微电网的测量数据进行比较，以了解虚拟系统对真实系统的反映程度。
布伦斯说：“更好地建模和测试这些系统的能力，可以帮助工程师在作战环境中依赖它们之前，了解它们的性能表现。”
NPS为布伦斯提供了资源，使他的研究不止于计算机模型，并能测试该模型能否反映真实电力系统的行为。借助实验室、设备和教员的专业知识，他得以将研究的虚拟部分与工程师在实地会使用的设备类型联系起来。通过这项工作，布伦斯看到了微电网如何能够解决远超军事领域的电力挑战。
布伦斯说：“电力需求不断增长，而我们的许多电力基础设施正在老化。微电网提供了一条可行的路径，既能整合可再生能源等技术，又能为关键基础设施实现电力生产本地化，无论该设施是军事基地、医院，还是其他不能承受断电的设施。”
毕业后，布伦斯将前往弗吉尼亚州匡蒂科的美国海军陆战队系统司令部报到，在那里从事中程拦截能力相关工作。
布伦斯说：“我预计到任后会有很多东西要学，但NPS给了我足够扎实的技术基础，使我能够理解这些系统、提出更好的问题，并与我将共事的专家说同一种语言。”
NPS位于加利福尼亚州蒙特雷，是一所海军指挥机构兼研究生大学，提供以国防为重点的教育和研究，培养学生返回舰队和部队时掌握可应用于军事挑战的知识。
如需了解有关海军研究生院的更多信息，请访问 https://nps.edu/ 。

items.title: Washington National Guard builds on Malaysia partnership during Pacific Partnership 2026
items.author: Joseph Siemandel
items.summary: Nine Washington Army National Guard soldiers from Bravo Company, 181st Light Support Battalion, joined Malaysian military and civilian partners in Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, Sept. 2–14, 2026, during the U.S. Navy-led Pacific Partnership mission.
items.body:
Nine Washington Army National Guard soldiers from Bravo Company, 181st Light Support Battalion, worked with Malaysian military and civilian partners during Pacific Partnership 2026, Sept. 2-14, 2026, sharing medical expertise and training for disaster response.

The U.S. Navy-led mission brought together personnel from nine nations for engagements in Kota Kinabalu and surrounding areas of Sabah. The Malaysia visit was Pacific Partnership’s fourth stop in 2026 and its first in Kota Kinabalu.

During a four-day symposium, the Washington soldiers presented on mass casualty operations, including triage, casualty collection points, rapid trauma assessments and cultural considerations in caring for injured people and the deceased.

“We were asked to support the U.S. Navy during Pacific Partnership 2026 in Kota Kinabalu. The mission brought people together across four areas—medical care, disaster management, engineering and community outreach—and our team worked primarily on disaster management,” said 1st Sgt. Jonathan W. Wentlandt, 1st Sgt. for Bravo Company, 181st Light Support Battalion. “We integrated primarily with the disaster management group and were originally tasked with teaching a mass casualty class with cultural considerations of wounded and deceased.”

As divers recovered simulated patients and bodies from the water, the Washington soldiers introduced patients with simulated injuries at a naval hospital, giving emergency department staff practice managing an influx of casualties.

The team also developed and led hands-on training for staff at the Malaysian Armed Forces Hospital. Soldiers exchanged expertise with dental and nursing counterparts at medical symposiums and joined community health engagements around Sabah.

“Outside of our assigned role, members from our team worked with the medical line of effort in symposiums. We also worked with host nation outreach and events and visited religious and cultural areas. And our three assigned officers were a part of a panel regarding Army Officer ROTC,” said Wentlandt.

The soldiers discussed the Washington Army National Guard’s State Partnership Program relationship with Malaysia during the disaster management symposium and a reserve officer engagement. Washington and Malaysia have been partners since 2017. Their work in Kota Kinabalu followed a September 2025 exchange in Spokane, where Washington Guard members and local responders trained alongside members of Malaysia’s Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team.

“Working with members of the Malaysian Armed Forces and the local community was a highly rewarding experience. They were actively engaged in our discussion on triage, casualty collection points, and rapid trauma assessment techniques,” said Wentlandt. “The Malaysians demonstrated a strong willingness to share their protocols, practices, and perspectives. In addition to the valuable professional exchange, they enthusiastically shared their cultural experiences and insights, fostering meaningful cross-cultural understanding and collaboration. The latter was particularly true when it came to learning about treatment of injured and deceased Muslim and Kadazan Dusun people.”

在为期四天的研讨会上，华盛顿州士兵就大规模伤亡行动进行了介绍，内容包括检伤分类、伤员收集点、快速创伤评估，以及在救治伤员和处理遗体时的文化考量。

当潜水员从水中打捞出模拟伤员和遗体时，华盛顿州士兵在一所海军医院引入了模拟伤情伤员，让急诊科工作人员练习应对大量伤亡人员涌入。

“与马来西亚武装部队成员及当地社区合作是一次非常有收获的经历。他们积极参与了我们关于检伤分类、伤员收集点和快速创伤评估技术的讨论，”温特兰特（Wentlandt）说。“马来西亚人表现出强烈的意愿，分享他们的规程、做法和观点。除了宝贵的专业交流外，他们还热情地分享了自身文化经历和见解，促进了有意义的跨文化理解与合作。在了解受伤和死亡的穆斯林及卡达山杜顺人（Kadazan Dusun）的处理方式时，后者尤其如此。”

items.title: Bravo Company Marine recognized for initiative, service to others
items.author: LCpl Landon Heredia
items.summary: WASHINGTON — Lance Cpl. Daniel Capes, a Marine assigned to Bravo Company, Marine Barracks Washington, received a Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal for his actions following a motor vehicle collision and his leadership in preparing 14 newly assigned Marines for duty at the “Oldest Post of the Corps.”
items.body:
WASHINGTON — Lance Cpl. Daniel Capes, a Marine assigned to Bravo Company, Marine Barracks Washington, received a Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal for his actions following a motor vehicle collision and his leadership in preparing 14 newly assigned Marines for duty at the “Oldest Post of the Corps.”

On Sept. 6, Capes witnessed a vehicle strike a deer near Leesburg Pike and Lewisville Road in Virginia. Recognizing the danger posed by the damaged vehicle and surrounding traffic, Capes stopped to assist the elderly driver. When she was unable to exit through the driver’s side or move across the vehicle without assistance, Capes entered through the passenger side, helped her out and moved her away from the active roadway. He remained with her and monitored her condition until law enforcement arrived.

Capes, a company clerk with Bravo Company, demonstrated the same initiative throughout September when he assumed responsibility for receiving and integrating 14 Marines newly assigned to the company. He coordinated their billeting, uniforms and tactical equipment, verified their medical readiness and served as a mentor and primary point of contact until they joined their respective platoons. His personal investment ensured the Marines arrived prepared, supported and ready to contribute to the Barracks’ mission.

Capt. Hayden Brown, commanding officer of Bravo Company, presented Capes with the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal during an awards ceremony at Marine Barracks Washington, Sept. 23. The award recognized his initiative, sound judgment and commitment to the welfare of others both on and off duty.

Capes’ actions reflected the ironclad discipline, steady character and resilient mind expected of Barracks Marines. Whether responding to someone in need or investing in the development of fellow Marines, he demonstrated how individual initiative and a commitment to others strengthen the force and prepare Marines to accomplish the mission.
zhParas: 华盛顿——华盛顿海军陆战队军营 Bravo 连的海军陆战队员 Lance Cpl. 丹尼尔·凯普斯（Daniel Capes），因在一起机动车碰撞事故后的救援行动，以及为 14 名新分配的海军陆战队员做好在陆战队“最古老哨所”执勤准备中所展现的领导力，获颁海军与海军陆战队成就奖章。
9 月 6 日，凯普斯在弗吉尼亚州莱斯堡派克与刘易斯维尔路附近目击一辆汽车撞上一头鹿。意识到受损车辆及周边车流带来的危险，凯普斯停车协助这位年长的驾车人。当她无法从驾驶座一侧下车，也无法在没有帮助的情况下从车内穿过时，凯普斯从副驾驶一侧进入车内，帮她下车，并将她转移到远离行车道路的地方。他一直陪伴在她身边并观察她的状况，直到执法部门赶到。
凯普斯是 Bravo 连的连部文书，9 月里他承担起接收并整合 14 名新分配至该连的海军陆战队员的职责，同样展现出这种主动性。他协调他们的住宿、制服和战术装备，核实他们的医疗战备情况，并担任导师和主要联系人，直到他们加入各自的排。他的个人投入确保这些海军陆战队员抵达时已做好准备、得到支持，随时能为军营的任务作出贡献。
9 月 23 日，Bravo 连连长 Capt. 海登·布朗（Hayden Brown）在华盛顿海军陆战队军营举行的颁奖仪式上向凯普斯颁发海军与海军陆战队成就奖章。该奖项表彰了他在执勤和下班期间的主动性、良好判断力以及为他人福祉所作的奉献。
凯普斯的行动体现了军营海军陆战队员应有的铁一般纪律、沉稳品格和坚韧意志。无论是救助需要帮助的人，还是投身于培养战友，他都展现出个人的主动性以及对他人负责的精神如何增强部队实力，并使海军陆战队员为完成任务做好准备。

items.title: MCTO pilots inaugural DoW SkillBridge preparation course for a fall 2026 launch
items.author: Anthony Small
items.summary: ALEXANDRIA, VA — The Department of War’s (DoW) Military-Civilian Transition Office (MCTO) completed the final pilot of its inaugural DoW SkillBridge Preparation Training course on September 14, 2026 in Norfolk, Virginia. This concluded a series of Navy, Marine Corps and Army sessions designed to gather service member feedback on the SkillBridge curriculum before its planned fall 2026 launch for the Total Force.
items.body:
ALEXANDRIA, VA — The Department of War’s (DoW) Military-Civilian Transition Office (MCTO) completed the final pilot of its inaugural DoW SkillBridge Preparation Training course on September 14, 2026 in Norfolk, Virginia. This concluded a series of Navy, Marine Corps and Army sessions designed to gather service member feedback on the SkillBridge curriculum before its planned fall 2026 launch for the Total Force.

MCTO developed the course to give service members a stronger foundation on the DoW SkillBridge eligibility, active duty ethical considerations while training with civilian employers, new initiatives like the DoW Project Patriot Pipeline that tie into SkillBridge, and how to identify approved opportunities that align with their post-transition civilian career goals.

The pilot series commenced between August 24 and September 1, spanning sessions at Naval Base San Diego, Marine Corps Recruit Depot San Diego, a virtual Army session, Marine Corps Base Quantico, and Naval Station Norfolk.

The curriculum is organized into three modules of content: SkillBridge orientation and ethics, technical and nontechnical competencies, and finding the right SkillBridge fit. The training includes a participant guidebook, facilitator guidebook and presentation slide deck.

“Behind this launch are months of intensive design, iterative drafting, and meticulous attention to detail,” said Alison Patz, MCTO course developer. “We deliberately moved away from dense, text-heavy content to build clean, intuitive, and visually engaging training materials. It was a big undertaking, but translating complex guidelines into accessible, attractive material is critical to ensuring our service members can easily absorb and benefit from this training.”

For MCTO, conducting pilots across multiple Military Services provided an opportunity to validate the curriculum directly with the service members who will use it and assess whether the training clearly explains the information they need before beginning their SkillBridge process.

“The pilot visits highlighted the importance of piloting the new curriculum and validating SkillBridge’s training products, which have been designed to streamline and connect transitioning service members with civilian and federal companies for on-the-job training, employment skill training, pre-apprenticeships, apprenticeships or internships during the final phase of active duty,” said Frank Lencz, MCTO strategic plans and initiatives analyst.

At Naval Base San Diego, 34 Sailors from multiple commands participated in the first Navy pilot. Participants ranged from E-4 petty officers to O-3 junior officers with between four and 18 years of military service. Participants responded positively to the course materials, including the participant guidebook, knowledge checks and activities.

The Norfolk pilot reinforced one of the course’s central messages: service members can begin preparing for SkillBridge well before they are eligible to participate. The training shows participants how to use the official SkillBridge website, research approved providers and opportunities, identify potential prerequisites and understand how SkillBridge fits into their broader military-to-civilian transition plan.

“I definitely learned a lot just from this hour-long course that I didn’t know beforehand,” one Sailor said during the Norfolk pilot.

“Hearing directly from the 170 active-duty personnel who attended our pilots was not just beneficial—it was essential,” Patz added. “Their candid suggestions, thoughts, and firsthand feedback directly shaped and refined the SkillBridge Preparation Training. By listening to those on the ground, the Department will deliver a high-impact product that is truly built by the force, for the Total Force.”

The course also helps service members understand that finding the right SkillBridge fit may depend on career goals, location, training format, qualifications and family circumstances. Approved opportunities can help service members build on military experience or prepare for a different civilian career.

SkillBridge opportunities also support workforce needs across the Defense Industrial Base and broader national security missions, including maritime and shipbuilding, aviation and aerospace, cybersecurity and information technology, engineering, logistics, advanced manufacturing and skilled trades.

With the pilot series complete, MCTO will use the results to finalize the SkillBridge Preparation Training course ahead of the fall 2026 launch to the Total Force.

DoW SkillBridge provides eligible service members opportunities to gain civilian work experience through approved industry training, apprenticeships and internships during their final 180 days of military service, subject to service-specific requirements and command approval.

Explore DoW SkillBridge at: https://skillbridge.mil .
zhParas: 弗吉尼亚州亚历山德里亚——战争部（DoW）军民过渡办公室（MCTO）于2026年9月14日在弗吉尼亚州诺福克完成了其首期DoW SkillBridge准备培训课程的最终试点。这结束了海军、海军陆战队和陆军的一系列课程，这些课程旨在在计划于2026年秋季面向全军种启动之前，收集军人对SkillBridge课程的反馈。
MCTO开发该课程，旨在让军人更扎实地掌握DoW SkillBridge资格条件、在民间雇主处培训期间的现役伦理考量、与SkillBridge相关的新举措（如DoW Project Patriot Pipeline），以及如何识别符合其过渡后平民职业目标的获批机会。
试点系列活动于8月24日至9月1日期间启动，涵盖在圣迭戈海军基地、圣迭戈海军陆战队新兵训练基地、一场陆军线上课程、匡蒂科海军陆战队基地和诺福克海军基地举行的多场课程。
课程内容分为三个模块：SkillBridge入门与伦理、技术与非技术能力，以及找到合适的SkillBridge匹配机会。培训材料包括学员手册、培训师手册和演示幻灯片。
“此次启动的背后是数月的高强度设计、反复起草和对细节的一丝不苟，”MCTO课程开发人员艾莉森·帕茨（Alison Patz）表示。“我们有意摒弃了密集、文字繁多的内容，转而打造简洁、直观且具有视觉吸引力的培训材料。这是一项艰巨的任务，但将复杂的指南转化为易于理解、具有吸引力的材料，对于确保我们的军人能够轻松吸收并受益于这项培训至关重要。”
对MCTO而言，在多个军种开展试点提供了一个机会，可以直接与将使用该课程的军人一起验证课程，并评估该培训是否清楚地解释了他们在开始SkillBridge流程前所需的信息。
“试点走访凸显了试运行新课程和验证SkillBridge培训产品的重要性，这些产品旨在简化流程，并将即将过渡的军人与民用和联邦公司联系起来，以便其在现役最后阶段获得在职培训、就业技能培训、预学徒、学徒或实习机会，”MCTO战略计划与倡议分析师弗兰克·伦茨（Frank Lencz）表示。
在圣迭戈海军基地，来自多个指挥部的34名水兵参加了首次海军试点。参与者从E-4军士到O-3初级军官不等，军龄在4至18年之间。参与者对课程材料反应积极，包括学员手册、知识测试和活动。
诺福克试点强化了该课程的核心信息之一：服役人员可以在符合参与资格之前就早早开始为SkillBridge做准备。培训向参与者展示如何使用官方SkillBridge网站、调研经批准的提供方和机会、识别潜在先决条件，并理解SkillBridge如何融入其更广泛的军转民过渡计划。
“仅仅通过这个一小时的课程，我就确实学到了很多之前不知道的东西，”一名水兵在诺福克试点期间说。
“直接听取参加我们试点的170名现役人员意见，不仅有益——而且至关重要，”帕茨（Patz）补充说。“他们坦诚的建议、想法和第一手反馈直接塑造并完善了SkillBridge准备培训。通过倾听一线人员的声音，该部门将提供一款真正由部队打造、服务全军的高影响力产品。”
该课程还帮助服役人员理解，找到合适的SkillBridge机会可能取决于职业目标、地点、培训形式、资质和家庭情况。经批准的机会可以帮助服役人员在军旅经验基础上继续发展，或为从事不同的文职职业做准备。
SkillBridge机会还支持国防工业基础及更广泛国家安全任务领域的人才队伍需求，包括海事与造船、航空与航天、网络安全与信息技术、工程、后勤、先进制造和技术工种。
随着试点系列完成，MCTO将利用结果在2026年秋季向全军推出之前，最终确定SkillBridge准备培训课程。
DoW SkillBridge为符合条件的服役人员提供机会，使其在服役最后180天内通过经批准的行业培训、学徒和实习获得民用工作经验，但须满足各军种的具体要求并获得指挥层批准。
请访问 https://skillbridge.mil 了解 DoW SkillBridge。

items.title: Trout Falls: A century-old scenic destination at Fort McCoy
items.author: Courtesy
items.summary: Long before Pine View Campground, before Fort McCoy became the home of a modern four-season outdoor recreation area, and before the surrounding land became part of an Army installation, people were making their way to a scenic place along the La Crosse River known as Trout Falls.
items.body:
Long before Pine View Campground, before Fort McCoy became the home of a modern four-season outdoor recreation area, and before the surrounding land became part of an Army installation, people were making their way to a scenic place along the La Crosse River known as Trout Falls.

Today, Trout Falls remains one of the distinctive natural features of Fort McCoy’s Pine View Recreation Area. Surrounded by wooded hills and trails and fed by the La Crosse River, the falls offer visitors a place to experience the landscape in every season — from the colorful foliage of autumn to the snow and ice of winter.

And unlike many places on an active military installation, Trout Falls is part of a recreation area that is open to the public.

The history of the falls, however, reaches back more than a century before today's visitors arrive at Pine View.

Trout Falls before Fort McCoy

Historical photographs and newspaper accounts show that Trout Falls was already a recognized scenic attraction in the early 20th century.

The Wisconsin Historical Society preserves a postcard of the falls dated 1906. The image shows Trout Falls on the La Crosse River, with a group of women standing along the left bank. The postcard’s caption identifies the location as “Trout Falls, La Crosse River, La Crosse, Wis.” The hand-colored postcard provides an early photographic record of the falls and demonstrates that the site was being photographed and shared as a scenic destination more than 120 years ago. Another Wisconsin Historical Society postcard, produced in 1929 by the E.C. Kropp Co., provides an even more detailed look at the historic site.

The postcard is labeled “Trout Falls, Near Sparta, Wis.” It shows an elevated view of the river and falls surrounded by trees. At the base of the falls on the left bank is an open-sided structure elevated above the ground on supports. A partially obscured sign inside the structure appears to read “SHOE.” Two women can also be seen sitting on the riverbank and viewing the falls. The Historical Society identifies the location as approximately 7.7 miles northeast of Sparta on the La Crosse River in Monroe County.

The photograph is more than an attractive old image. It provides evidence that the area around Trout Falls was already being used and visited by people nearly a century ago.

The historic structure visible in the 1929 photograph also raises questions for future research. Its exact purpose has not been established from the available historical record, but its presence demonstrates that visitors were using and gathering at the falls during the period.

A place familiar to Sparta residents

A 2025 “Looking Back” feature published by the Monroe County Herald provides another important piece of Trout Falls history.

The newspaper looked back to 1910, when Sparta businessman Gustav Kollertz had his ice cream parlor decorated with painted scenes. One of those scenes was Trout Falls — a location the newspaper described as one that “every Spartan will immediately recognize.”

The reference is significant because it shows that Trout Falls was not merely an obscure geographic feature. By 1910, it was sufficiently familiar to the people of Sparta that an image of the falls could be used as recognizable local scenery in a downtown business.

The Monroe County Herald’s historical note also states that the area around Trout Falls was not part of Fort McCoy before the 1940s and was more readily accessible to the public at that time. Thus, long before the Army developed Pine View Recreation Area, Trout Falls was already part of the recreational and visual landscape of the Sparta area.

The river that gives Trout Falls its character

Trout Falls is located on the La Crosse River, a waterway that remains an important natural feature of Pine View Recreation Area.

The river also provides an explanation for the name Trout Falls.

Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources records identify a 12.7-mile section of the La Crosse River upstream from Trout Falls as Class I trout water. The DNR describes that portion of the river as a high-quality trout stream with enough natural reproduction to sustain wild trout populations at or near carrying capacity. The classification identifies Trout Falls near the confluence with Suukjak Sep Creek as the downstream reference point for that high-quality trout-water section.

The trout-rich river and the falls have therefore been connected not only by geography but by the character of the landscape itself.

Visitors today can still see the La Crosse River flowing through Pine View Recreation Area and over Trout Falls.

From training land to recreation area

The next major chapter in Trout Falls history began after the land became part of the military reservation. Fort McCoy's modern Pine View Recreation Area was conceived during the mid-1960s as an effort to provide a community recreation area on post.

In 1969, approximately 200 acres of training land were rezoned for development of the Trout Falls-Squaw Lake area. Most construction took place during the summer of 1971, with the original project including a five-acre picnic area and a 50-unit camping area.

The transformation brought a new chapter to a landscape that had already been known to area residents for generations. On June 24, 1972, Pine View Campground officially opened as the Trout Falls-Squaw Lake Recreation Area. The original recreation development was much smaller than today's Pine View complex, but its name is historically important. The Army was not simply creating a campground near a scenic feature. Trout Falls was part of the name of the original recreation area itself.

Over the decades, the recreation area expanded and developed into today's Pine View Recreation Area. The area eventually became known as Pine View, but Trout Falls remained an important natural landmark within it.

From Trout Falls-Squaw Lake to Pine View

The recreation area that opened in 1972 continued to develop over the following decades.

The campground eventually grew far beyond its original 50-unit design. A 2014 Fort McCoy publication noted that the campground had expanded to 176 campsites, including 38 nonelectric tent sites, along with cabins, yurts, travel trailers and other amenities.

That same historical account emphasized something that remains true today: the campground and recreation area are available not only to military Families but also to the general public. At the time, approximately 65,000 people were using the area annually.

The transformation from the original Trout Falls-Squaw Lake Recreation Area to today's Pine View Recreation Area illustrates how a natural feature that had attracted visitors long before Fort McCoy became an installation was incorporated into a modern outdoor recreation destination.

Trout Falls today

Today, Trout Falls is part of a much larger recreation landscape.

Pine View Recreation Area encompasses hundreds of acres and includes the La Crosse River, Trout Falls, Suukjak Sep Lake and Suukjak Sep Creek, Pine View Campground, hiking trails, and Whitetail Ridge Ski Area. Fort McCoy describes the area as offering four-season, year-round recreation, including camping, hiking and fishing.

The current Fort McCoy camping information specifically states that members of the Fort McCoy community and the public may use Pine View Recreation Area and that Pine View is fully operational year-round.

Two miles of nature and hiking trails are maintained in the recreation area, and the trail to Trout Falls starts at the Pine View picnic area. That makes the falls particularly accessible for visitors who want to experience the area on foot.

The public should remember, however, that Fort McCoy is an active military installation and installation access is controlled. Visitors should check current access requirements, recreation-area rules, hours and seasonal conditions before traveling to the area. Fort McCoy’s current information identifies Pine View as one of the installation's recreational facilities available to the public.

Autumn brings a different Trout Falls For many visitors, autumn may be the most spectacular time to experience Trout Falls. As the leaves surrounding the La Crosse River change from green to the reds, oranges and yellows of Wisconsin autumn, the falls become part of a larger landscape of color.

Fort McCoy Public Affairs photographs from Sept. 25, 2023, document Trout Falls surrounded by fall foliage. Similar photographs taken Oct. 10, 2024, show the La Crosse River flowing over the falls while the surrounding woods display the colors of the season.

Fort McCoy recreation officials have specifically encouraged visitors to experience Trout Falls during autumn.

Alex Karis, supervisory recreation specialist and facility manager with Fort McCoy's Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation, has described Trout Falls as an especially scenic destination during the fall season.

The attraction is not limited to sightseeing. Visitors can hike the trails through the recreation area, view the river, enjoy the changing foliage and combine a visit to the falls with other Pine View activities.

The combination of water, rock, forest and changing leaves gives Trout Falls a different appearance from the one seen in the historic postcards of the early 1900s.

Yet the basic scene remains remarkably recognizable. The river still runs through the same landscape. The falls still draw visitors. And the surrounding woods remain an important part of the experience.

Winter transforms the falls again

When autumn ends and snow arrives, Trout Falls takes on another character. Fort McCoy has specifically promoted winter visits to the falls, noting that the river, trails and surrounding landscape can provide a scenic winter destination even after the main camping season has ended.

Karis has encouraged visitors to see Trout Falls after snowfall, saying the falls are particularly beautiful in winter. When snow conditions permit, visitors can use snowshoes or cross-country skis on the area's trails. The trails follow the La Crosse River both above and below the falls, and bridges provide crossings over the river.

A Nov. 28, 2023, Fort McCoy Public Affairs photograph provides a modern winter record of the falls, showing the river and falls in a snow-covered landscape.

Winter also provides something historical photographs cannot: an opportunity to see how dramatically the falls change when snow and ice become part of the scene.

The sound and movement of the river continue beneath the winter landscape, while snow and ice can build along the rocks and surrounding vegetation.

For visitors interested in photography, the seasonal contrast is particularly striking.

A natural landmark with a military history Trout Falls represents an unusual intersection of Wisconsin natural history, local community history and Fort McCoy history. The falls were known to area residents before the Army acquired the surrounding land.

They appeared in early 20th-century postcards. They were familiar enough to Sparta residents in 1910 to be used as a recognizable scene in a local ice cream parlor. A 1929 postcard documented visitors at the falls and a structure beside the river. Then, decades later, the Army incorporated the falls into a recreation project that became the Trout Falls-Squaw Lake Recreation Area in 1972.

That recreation area eventually evolved into today’s Pine View Recreation Area. The name changed, the campground grew, facilities were added and the surrounding military installation continued to evolve. But Trout Falls remained.

A place to experience Fort McCoy beyond the training mission Fort McCoy is best known for its role as a military training installation, but places such as Trout Falls offer visitors a different perspective on the installation.

The Pine View Recreation Area provides an opportunity to experience the natural landscape of western Wisconsin while remaining within the boundaries of an active Army installation.

The area includes hiking, camping, fishing and other outdoor recreation opportunities. Fort McCoy's current information lists Pine View as a public recreation destination, while installation regulations continue to govern access and activities.

For someone visiting Fort McCoy for the first time, Trout Falls can therefore serve as a reminder that the installation is more than its training areas and military facilities.

It is also a place where a river flows through wooded hills, where trout inhabit the La Crosse River, where hikers can follow trails through the landscape, and where a natural feature photographed more than a century ago can still be visited today.

A century of visitors — and counting

The historical record of Trout Falls provides a remarkable continuity. In 1906, a group of women stood beside the falls for a photograph that became a postcard. In 1910, residents of Sparta recognized Trout Falls as a familiar local scene.

In 1929, visitors were photographed sitting beside the river while the falls flowed nearby. In 1969, the Army designated approximately 200 acres for development of the Trout Falls-Squaw Lake recreation area.

In 1972, the recreation area officially opened. In 2022, Pine View marked 50 years of recreation use. In 2023 and 2024, Fort McCoy photographers documented the falls in autumn and winter.

And today, the public can still follow the trail to Trout Falls and stand beside the same river that attracted visitors generations ago.

The scenery changes with the seasons, but the attraction remains. For those looking for a place to experience Wisconsin's autumn colors, take a winter hike, photograph a historic natural landmark or simply spend time outdoors, Trout Falls offers something that is increasingly rare: a living landscape with a documented history stretching back more than a century.

The falls are not simply a feature of Pine View Recreation Area. They are part of the history of the land itself. And after more than 100 years of being photographed, visited and remembered, Trout Falls remains one of Fort McCoy's most distinctive places to experience the outdoors.

People can learn more about the recreation area and all it has to offer the public by visiting https://mccoy.armymwr.com.

如今，鳟鱼瀑布仍是麦科伊堡松景休闲区独特的自然景观之一。瀑布四周环绕着林木覆盖的丘陵和步道，水源来自拉克罗斯河，为游客提供了一个体验四季风光的地方——从秋日斑斓的树叶到冬季的冰雪。
与现役军事设施内的许多地方不同，鳟鱼瀑布属于一个向公众开放的休闲区。
然而，这座瀑布的历史可以追溯到今天游客来到松景的一个多世纪之前。
麦科伊堡之前的鳟鱼瀑布
历史照片和报纸报道显示，早在20世纪初，鳟鱼瀑布就已经是一处公认的风景胜地。
威斯康星州历史学会保存着一张标注日期为1906年的该瀑布明信片。画面显示拉克罗斯河上的鳟鱼瀑布，一群女性站在左岸。明信片说明文字将地点标为“鳟鱼瀑布，拉克罗斯河，威斯康星州拉克罗斯”。这张手工上色明信片提供了该瀑布的早期照片记录，并表明早在120多年前，这里就作为风景目的地被拍摄和传播。威斯康星州历史学会保存的另一张明信片由E.C. Kropp公司于1929年制作，更详细地展现了这处历史遗址。
这张明信片上标注着“鳟鱼瀑布，威斯康星州斯巴达附近”。它展示了河流和瀑布的俯瞰景象，四周树木环绕。在左岸瀑布底部，有一座由支柱架空、侧面敞开的建筑。建筑内一块部分被遮挡的标牌看似写着“鞋”。还可以看到两名女性坐在河岸上观赏瀑布。历史学会确认该地点位于门罗县拉克罗斯河上，斯巴达东北约7.7 miles处。
这张照片不仅仅是一幅颇有吸引力的老照片。它提供了证据，表明早在近一个世纪前，特劳特瀑布周边地区就已经有人使用和到访。
1929年照片中可见的那座历史性建筑也为未来研究提出了问题。从现有历史记录来看，其确切用途尚未确定，但它的存在表明，当时游客正在使用这处瀑布并在此聚集。
为斯巴达居民所熟悉的地方
《门罗县先驱报》2025年刊登的一篇“回顾”专题文章，提供了关于特劳特瀑布历史的另一项重要资料。
该报回顾了1910年，当时斯巴达商人古斯塔夫·科勒茨（Gustav Kollertz）让人用彩绘场景装饰了他的冰淇淋店。其中一个场景就是特劳特瀑布——该报将其描述为一个“每个斯巴达居民都会立刻认出的”地点。
这一提及意义重大，因为它表明特劳特瀑布并不仅仅是一个鲜为人知的地理特征。到1910年，它已为斯巴达民众所足够熟悉，以至于瀑布的图像可以被用作市中心一家商铺中可辨识的本地景致。
《门罗县先驱报》的历史注释还指出，特劳特瀑布周边地区在20世纪40年代之前并不属于麦科伊堡，而且在当时更容易为公众所进入。因此，早在陆军开发派恩维尤休闲区之前，特劳特瀑布就已经是斯巴达地区休闲与视觉景观的一部分。
造就特劳特瀑布特色的河流
特劳特瀑布位于拉克罗斯河上，这条水道至今仍是松景休闲区的重要自然特征。
这条河也为“特劳特瀑布”这一名称提供了解释。
威斯康星州自然资源部的记录将拉克罗斯河在特劳特瀑布上游的一段 12.7-mile 河段确定为一级鳟鱼水域。DNR 将那段河流描述为一条高质量鳟鱼溪流，其自然繁殖足以使野生鳟鱼种群维持在承载力水平或接近承载力。该分类将靠近 Suukjak Sep Creek 汇流处的特劳特瀑布确定为该高质量鳟鱼水域的下游基准点。
因此，这条盛产鳟鱼的河流与瀑布之间的联系，不仅来自地理，也来自景观本身的特质。
今天的游客仍可看到拉克罗斯河流经松景休闲区并越过特劳特瀑布。
从训练用地到休闲区
特劳特瀑布历史的下一重要篇章，始于这片土地成为军事保留地的一部分之后。麦考伊堡现代松景休闲区是在20世纪60年代中期构想的，旨在为基地内提供一个社区休闲区。
1969年，约200 acres 的训练用地被重新划区，用于开发特劳特瀑布—斯阔湖地区。大部分建设在1971年夏季进行，最初的项目包括一个5-acre 野餐区和一个50-unit 露营区。
这次改造为当地居民世代早已熟悉的这片土地开启了新篇章。1972年6月24日，派恩维尤露营地以特劳特福尔斯-斯阔湖休闲区的名称正式开放。最初的休闲区开发规模远小于如今的派恩维尤综合体，但其名称具有重要历史意义。陆军并非只是在一个风景点附近建一个露营地。特劳特福尔斯本身就是原休闲区名称的一部分。
几十年来，该休闲区不断扩建，并发展成如今的派恩维尤休闲区。该区域最终以派恩维尤之名广为人知，但特劳特福尔斯仍是其中一处重要的自然地标。
从特劳特福尔斯-斯阔湖到派恩维尤
1972年开放的休闲区在随后的几十年里持续发展。
该露营地最终远远超出了最初50个单元的设计规模。麦科伊堡2014年的一份出版物指出，该露营地已扩建至176个营位，其中包括38个无电帐篷营位，另有小木屋、蒙古包、旅行拖车和其他设施。
同一份历史记述强调了某种至今仍然属实的情况：该露营地及休闲区不仅供军人家庭使用，也向普通公众开放。当时，每年约有65,000人使用该区域。
从最初的特劳特福尔斯-斯阔湖休闲区到如今的派恩维尤休闲区的转变，说明了一处早在麦科伊堡成为军事设施之前就吸引游客的自然景观，如何被纳入一个现代户外休闲目的地。
今天的特劳特福尔斯
如今，特劳特瀑布只是一个规模大得多的休闲景观的一部分。
派恩维尤休闲区占地数百英亩，包括拉克罗斯河、特劳特瀑布、苏克贾克塞普湖和苏克贾克塞普溪、派恩维尤露营地、徒步步道以及白尾岭滑雪场。麦科伊堡称该区域提供四季全年休闲活动，包括露营、徒步和钓鱼。
麦科伊堡目前的露营信息明确指出，麦科伊堡社区成员和公众均可使用派恩维尤休闲区，且派恩维尤全年全面开放运营。
休闲区内维护有两英里的自然与徒步步道，通往特劳特瀑布的步道起点位于派恩维尤野餐区。这使得希望徒步体验该地区的游客尤其容易抵达瀑布。
不过，公众应记住，麦科伊堡是一处现役军事设施，进出受到管制。游客在前往该地区前，应查询当前的进入要求、休闲区规定、开放时间及季节性状况。麦科伊堡现有信息将派恩维尤列为该设施向公众开放的休闲设施之一。
秋季带来别样的特劳特瀑布。对许多游客而言，秋季可能是体验特劳特瀑布最壮观的时节。随着拉克罗斯河周边的树叶由绿转为威斯康星秋季的红色、橙色和黄色，瀑布成为更大一片色彩景观的一部分。
麦科伊堡公共事务部门2023年9月25日拍摄的照片记录了秋叶环绕的特劳特瀑布。2024年10月10日拍摄的类似照片显示，拉克罗斯河流经瀑布，周围树林呈现出当季的色彩。
麦科伊堡休闲事务官员特别鼓励游客在秋季前往体验特劳特瀑布。
麦科伊堡家庭与士气、福利和娱乐局的监督娱乐专家兼设施经理亚历克斯·卡里斯（Alex Karis）称，鳟鱼瀑布是秋季一个风景格外优美的目的地。
该景点并不只限于观光。游客可以在休闲区内沿步道徒步，观赏河流，欣赏不断变化的树叶，并将游览瀑布与派恩维尤的其他活动结合起来。
水、岩石、森林和变幻的树叶相结合，使鳟鱼瀑布呈现出与20世纪初历史明信片上所见不同的面貌。
然而，基本景致仍然非常容易辨认。河流仍流经同一片景观。瀑布仍吸引游客。周围的树林仍是这一体验的重要组成部分。
冬季再次改变瀑布的面貌
当秋季结束、降雪到来时，鳟鱼瀑布呈现出另一种风貌。麦科伊堡特别推广冬季游览该瀑布，指出即便主要露营季节已经结束，这里的河流、步道和周边景观仍能提供一个风景优美的冬季目的地。
卡里斯鼓励游客在降雪后前往观赏鳟鱼瀑布，称瀑布在冬季格外美丽。当积雪条件允许时，游客可以在该地区的步道上使用雪鞋或越野滑雪板。步道沿拉克罗斯河延伸，分布在瀑布上游和下游，桥梁可供跨越河流。
2023年11月28日，麦科伊堡公共事务办公室的一张照片为瀑布留下了现代冬季记录，展示了白雪覆盖景观中的河流和瀑布。
冬季还带来了历史照片无法呈现的东西：一个亲眼目睹当冰雪成为景致一部分时瀑布发生何等剧烈变化的机会。
河流的声音与流动在冬季景观之下依旧延续，而积雪和冰层则会在岩石和周边植被旁不断堆积。
对于对摄影感兴趣的游客来说，这种季节性的对比尤为醒目。
一段带有军事历史的自然地标 鳟鱼瀑布（Trout Falls）代表着威斯康星州自然史、当地社区历史与麦科伊堡（Fort McCoy）历史不同寻常的交汇。在陆军购得周边土地之前，当地居民就已知道这处瀑布。
它出现在20世纪初的明信片上。1910年，斯巴达（Sparta）居民对其十分熟悉，以至于当地一家冰淇淋店把它用作辨识度很高的场景。一张1929年的明信片记录了在瀑布边和河畔一座建筑旁的游客。数十年后，陆军将这处瀑布纳入一项娱乐项目，该项目于1972年成为鳟鱼瀑布-斯阔湖娱乐区（Trout Falls-Squaw Lake Recreation Area）。
该娱乐区最终演变为今天的松景娱乐区（Pine View Recreation Area）。名字变了，露营地扩大了，设施增加了，周边军事基地也在不断演变。但鳟鱼瀑布依然如故。
在训练任务之外体验麦科伊堡的地方 麦科伊堡最为人所知的是其作为军事训练基地的角色，但像鳟鱼瀑布这样的地方为访客提供了看待这座基地的不同视角。
松景娱乐区让人们有机会在仍处于一座现役陆军基地边界之内的情况下，体验威斯康星州西部的自然景观。
该区域提供徒步、露营、钓鱼和其他户外休闲机会。麦科伊堡的当前信息将Pine View列为公共休闲目的地，而基地规章仍对进入和活动加以管理。
因此，对首次到访麦科伊堡的人来说，鳟鱼瀑布可以提醒他们，该基地不只是训练区和军事设施。
这里还是一个河流穿行于林木覆盖的山丘之间的地方，鳟鱼栖息在拉克罗斯河中，徒步者可沿步道穿行于这片景观，而一个多世纪前被拍摄过的一处自然景观如今仍可造访。
一个世纪的访客——且仍在延续
鳟鱼瀑布的历史记录呈现出非凡的延续性。1906年，一群女性站在瀑布旁拍照，这张照片后来成为明信片。1910年，斯巴达的居民将鳟鱼瀑布视为熟悉的当地景致。
1929年，游客被拍到坐在河畔，瀑布就在近旁流淌。1969年，陆军指定约200 acres用于开发鳟鱼瀑布-斯阔湖休闲区。
1972年，该休闲区正式开放。2022年，Pine View迎来休闲使用50周年。2023年和2024年，麦科伊堡的摄影师记录了秋季和冬季的瀑布。
如今，公众仍可沿步道前往鳟鱼瀑布，站在那条曾在几代人之前吸引访客的河流旁。
景色随季节变换，但吸引力始终如一。对于那些想找个地方欣赏威斯康星州秋色、进行冬季徒步、拍摄一处历史悠久的自然地标，或者只是想在户外消磨时光的人来说，特劳特瀑布（Trout Falls）提供了一种日益罕见的东西：一片有据可查、历史可追溯到一个多世纪以前的活态景观。
这些瀑布并不只是派恩维尤休闲区（Pine View Recreation Area）的一处景观。它们是这片土地自身历史的一部分。在被拍摄、造访和铭记一百多年之后，特劳特瀑布（Trout Falls）依然是麦科伊堡（Fort McCoy）最具特色的户外体验地之一。
人们可访问 https://mccoy.armymwr.com，进一步了解该休闲区及其向公众提供的全部内容。
（本文由麦科伊堡公共事务办公室撰写。）

这一提及意义重大，因为它表明特劳特瀑布并不仅仅是一个鲜为人知的地理特征。到1910年，它已为斯巴达民众所足够熟悉，以至于瀑布的图像可以被用作市中心一家商铺中可辨识的本地景致。

《门罗县先驱报》的历史注释还指出，特劳特瀑布周边地区在20世纪40年代之前并不属于麦科伊堡，而且在当时更容易为公众所进入。因此，早在陆军开发派恩维尤休闲区之前，特劳特瀑布就已经是斯巴达地区休闲与视觉景观的一部分。

造就特劳特瀑布特色的河流

特劳特瀑布位于拉克罗斯河上，这条水道至今仍是松景休闲区的重要自然特征。

这条河也为“特劳特瀑布”这一名称提供了解释。

威斯康星州自然资源部的记录将拉克罗斯河在特劳特瀑布上游的一段 12.7-mile 河段确定为一级鳟鱼水域。DNR 将那段河流描述为一条高质量鳟鱼溪流，其自然繁殖足以使野生鳟鱼种群维持在承载力水平或接近承载力。该分类将靠近 Suukjak Sep Creek 汇流处的特劳特瀑布确定为该高质量鳟鱼水域的下游基准点。

因此，这条盛产鳟鱼的河流与瀑布之间的联系，不仅来自地理，也来自景观本身的特质。

今天的游客仍可看到拉克罗斯河流经松景休闲区并越过特劳特瀑布。

从训练用地到休闲区

特劳特瀑布历史的下一重要篇章，始于这片土地成为军事保留地的一部分之后。麦考伊堡现代松景休闲区是在20世纪60年代中期构想的，旨在为基地内提供一个社区休闲区。

1969年，约200 acres 的训练用地被重新划区，用于开发特劳特瀑布—斯阔湖地区。大部分建设在1971年夏季进行，最初的项目包括一个5-acre 野餐区和一个50-unit 露营区。

这次改造为当地居民世代早已熟悉的这片土地开启了新篇章。1972年6月24日，派恩维尤露营地以特劳特福尔斯-斯阔湖休闲区的名称正式开放。最初的休闲区开发规模远小于如今的派恩维尤综合体，但其名称具有重要历史意义。陆军并非只是在一个风景点附近建一个露营地。特劳特福尔斯本身就是原休闲区名称的一部分。

几十年来，该休闲区不断扩建，并发展成如今的派恩维尤休闲区。该区域最终以派恩维尤之名广为人知，但特劳特福尔斯仍是其中一处重要的自然地标。

从特劳特福尔斯-斯阔湖到派恩维尤

1972年开放的休闲区在随后的几十年里持续发展。

该露营地最终远远超出了最初50个单元的设计规模。麦科伊堡2014年的一份出版物指出，该露营地已扩建至176个营位，其中包括38个无电帐篷营位，另有小木屋、蒙古包、旅行拖车和其他设施。

同一份历史记述强调了某种至今仍然属实的情况：该露营地及休闲区不仅供军人家庭使用，也向普通公众开放。当时，每年约有65,000人使用该区域。

从最初的特劳特福尔斯-斯阔湖休闲区到如今的派恩维尤休闲区的转变，说明了一处早在麦科伊堡成为军事设施之前就吸引游客的自然景观，如何被纳入一个现代户外休闲目的地。

今天的特劳特福尔斯

如今，特劳特瀑布只是一个规模大得多的休闲景观的一部分。

派恩维尤休闲区占地数百英亩，包括拉克罗斯河、特劳特瀑布、苏克贾克塞普湖和苏克贾克塞普溪、派恩维尤露营地、徒步步道以及白尾岭滑雪场。麦科伊堡称该区域提供四季全年休闲活动，包括露营、徒步和钓鱼。

麦科伊堡目前的露营信息明确指出，麦科伊堡社区成员和公众均可使用派恩维尤休闲区，且派恩维尤全年全面开放运营。

休闲区内维护有两英里的自然与徒步步道，通往特劳特瀑布的步道起点位于派恩维尤野餐区。这使得希望徒步体验该地区的游客尤其容易抵达瀑布。

不过，公众应记住，麦科伊堡是一处现役军事设施，进出受到管制。游客在前往该地区前，应查询当前的进入要求、休闲区规定、开放时间及季节性状况。麦科伊堡现有信息将派恩维尤列为该设施向公众开放的休闲设施之一。

秋季带来别样的特劳特瀑布。对许多游客而言，秋季可能是体验特劳特瀑布最壮观的时节。随着拉克罗斯河周边的树叶由绿转为威斯康星秋季的红色、橙色和黄色，瀑布成为更大一片色彩景观的一部分。

麦科伊堡公共事务部门2023年9月25日拍摄的照片记录了秋叶环绕的特劳特瀑布。2024年10月10日拍摄的类似照片显示，拉克罗斯河流经瀑布，周围树林呈现出当季的色彩。

麦科伊堡休闲事务官员特别鼓励游客在秋季前往体验特劳特瀑布。

麦科伊堡家庭与士气、福利和娱乐局的监督娱乐专家兼设施经理亚历克斯·卡里斯（Alex Karis）称，鳟鱼瀑布是秋季一个风景格外优美的目的地。

该景点并不只限于观光。游客可以在休闲区内沿步道徒步，观赏河流，欣赏不断变化的树叶，并将游览瀑布与派恩维尤的其他活动结合起来。

水、岩石、森林和变幻的树叶相结合，使鳟鱼瀑布呈现出与20世纪初历史明信片上所见不同的面貌。

然而，基本景致仍然非常容易辨认。河流仍流经同一片景观。瀑布仍吸引游客。周围的树林仍是这一体验的重要组成部分。

冬季再次改变瀑布的面貌

当秋季结束、降雪到来时，鳟鱼瀑布呈现出另一种风貌。麦科伊堡特别推广冬季游览该瀑布，指出即便主要露营季节已经结束，这里的河流、步道和周边景观仍能提供一个风景优美的冬季目的地。

卡里斯鼓励游客在降雪后前往观赏鳟鱼瀑布，称瀑布在冬季格外美丽。当积雪条件允许时，游客可以在该地区的步道上使用雪鞋或越野滑雪板。步道沿拉克罗斯河延伸，分布在瀑布上游和下游，桥梁可供跨越河流。

2023年11月28日，麦科伊堡公共事务办公室的一张照片为瀑布留下了现代冬季记录，展示了白雪覆盖景观中的河流和瀑布。

冬季还带来了历史照片无法呈现的东西：一个亲眼目睹当冰雪成为景致一部分时瀑布发生何等剧烈变化的机会。

河流的声音与流动在冬季景观之下依旧延续，而积雪和冰层则会在岩石和周边植被旁不断堆积。

对于对摄影感兴趣的游客来说，这种季节性的对比尤为醒目。

一段带有军事历史的自然地标 鳟鱼瀑布（Trout Falls）代表着威斯康星州自然史、当地社区历史与麦科伊堡（Fort McCoy）历史不同寻常的交汇。在陆军购得周边土地之前，当地居民就已知道这处瀑布。

它出现在20世纪初的明信片上。1910年，斯巴达（Sparta）居民对其十分熟悉，以至于当地一家冰淇淋店把它用作辨识度很高的场景。一张1929年的明信片记录了在瀑布边和河畔一座建筑旁的游客。数十年后，陆军将这处瀑布纳入一项娱乐项目，该项目于1972年成为鳟鱼瀑布-斯阔湖娱乐区（Trout Falls-Squaw Lake Recreation Area）。

该娱乐区最终演变为今天的松景娱乐区（Pine View Recreation Area）。名字变了，露营地扩大了，设施增加了，周边军事基地也在不断演变。但鳟鱼瀑布依然如故。

在训练任务之外体验麦科伊堡的地方 麦科伊堡最为人所知的是其作为军事训练基地的角色，但像鳟鱼瀑布这样的地方为访客提供了看待这座基地的不同视角。

松景娱乐区让人们有机会在仍处于一座现役陆军基地边界之内的情况下，体验威斯康星州西部的自然景观。

该区域提供徒步、露营、钓鱼和其他户外休闲机会。麦科伊堡的当前信息将Pine View列为公共休闲目的地，而基地规章仍对进入和活动加以管理。

因此，对首次到访麦科伊堡的人来说，鳟鱼瀑布可以提醒他们，该基地不只是训练区和军事设施。

这里还是一个河流穿行于林木覆盖的山丘之间的地方，鳟鱼栖息在拉克罗斯河中，徒步者可沿步道穿行于这片景观，而一个多世纪前被拍摄过的一处自然景观如今仍可造访。

一个世纪的访客——且仍在延续

鳟鱼瀑布的历史记录呈现出非凡的延续性。1906年，一群女性站在瀑布旁拍照，这张照片后来成为明信片。1910年，斯巴达的居民将鳟鱼瀑布视为熟悉的当地景致。

1929年，游客被拍到坐在河畔，瀑布就在近旁流淌。1969年，陆军指定约200 acres用于开发鳟鱼瀑布-斯阔湖休闲区。

1972年，该休闲区正式开放。2022年，Pine View迎来休闲使用50周年。2023年和2024年，麦科伊堡的摄影师记录了秋季和冬季的瀑布。

如今，公众仍可沿步道前往鳟鱼瀑布，站在那条曾在几代人之前吸引访客的河流旁。

景色随季节变换，但吸引力始终如一。对于那些想找个地方欣赏威斯康星州秋色、进行冬季徒步、拍摄一处历史悠久的自然地标，或者只是想在户外消磨时光的人来说，特劳特瀑布（Trout Falls）提供了一种日益罕见的东西：一片有据可查、历史可追溯到一个多世纪以前的活态景观。

这些瀑布并不只是派恩维尤休闲区（Pine View Recreation Area）的一处景观。它们是这片土地自身历史的一部分。在被拍摄、造访和铭记一百多年之后，特劳特瀑布（Trout Falls）依然是麦科伊堡（Fort McCoy）最具特色的户外体验地之一。

人们可访问 https://mccoy.armymwr.com，进一步了解该休闲区及其向公众提供的全部内容。

（本文由麦科伊堡公共事务办公室撰写。）

items.title: Air Force Bombers and Fighters Fly Over Chinese Leader’s DC Visit
items.author: Steve Losey
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington D.C. has been filled with signs of American airpower: U.S. Air Force B-1 and B-2 bombers and F-22 fighters have all performed flyovers Sept. 23-24. The post Air Force Bombers and Fighters Fly Over Chinese Leader’s DC Visit appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington D.C. has been filled with signs of American airpower: U.S. Air Force B-1 and B-2 bombers and F-22 fighters have all performed flyovers Sept. 23-24.

Xi arrived at Joint Base Andrews, Md., on Sept. 23, and was greeted planeside by President Donald Trump—an unusual occurrence—and a military honor guard. The Presidential Salute Battery of the Army’s Old Guard, formally known as the 3rd Infantry Regiment, conducted a 21-gun salute as part of the arrival ceremony, and two B-1B Lancers roared overhead as the national anthem played.

A day later, a single B-2 Spirit, flanked by four F-22 Raptors, soared over the White House to cap a morning of military pomp and ceremony for Xi and his wife, Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan.

This is Xi’s first state visit to the U.S. since 2015.

First Lady Melania Trump’s office released a statement Sept. 21 saying the welcoming event would feature 479 military personnel from all branches of the U.S. military.

As they arrived, Xi and his wife were met with a full military honor cordon along the White House’s South Drive, which led to a display of the flags of the U.S. and China. U.S. Army Herald Trumpets presented a fanfare for the Xis, and the Army Old Guard Fife and Drum Corps, the Marine Corps Silent Drill Platoon, and the United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps—known as “The Commandant’s Own”—performed military demonstrations, before the B-2 and F-22 flyover.

Military flyovers are not unusual for state visits. A few months ago, four F-35s flew over the White House in honor of King Charles III’s state visit. But the presence of bombers is less routine and somewhat reminiscent of an August 2025 flyover of Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska, that featured a B-2 Spirit and four F-35s.
zhParas: 中国国家主席习近平（Xi Jinping）对华盛顿特区的国事访问处处可见美国空中力量的展示：9月23日至24日，美国空军B-1和B-2轰炸机以及F-22战斗机均进行了飞越。
习近平于9月23日抵达马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地，在舷梯旁受到总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）——这一情形并不寻常——和一支军队仪仗队的迎接。陆军老卫队（正式名称为第3步兵团）的总统礼炮连在抵达仪式上鸣放21响礼炮，国歌奏响时，两架B-1B“枪骑兵”轰鸣着飞过头顶。
一天后，一架B-2“幽灵”在四架F-22“猛禽”的伴随下飞越白宫，为习近平及其夫人、中国第一夫人彭丽媛（Peng Liyuan）的上午军事盛典和仪式画上句号。
这是习近平自2015年以来首次对美国进行国事访问。
第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普（Melania Trump）的办公室9月21日发表声明称，欢迎活动将有来自美国军队各军种的479名军人参加。
他们抵达时，习近平和夫人在白宫南车道沿线受到军方完整荣誉警戒线迎接，南车道通向美中两国国旗展示区。美国陆军礼号队为习近平夫妇奏响号角，陆军老卫队笛鼓队、海军陆战队静默操枪排以及被称为“司令专属”的美国海军陆战队鼓号队进行了军事表演，之后是B-2和F-22的飞越。
国事访问中进行军事飞越并不罕见。几个月前，四架F-35曾为查尔斯三世国王（King Charles III）的国事访问飞越白宫。但轰炸机的出现则不那么常规，且在某种程度上让人想起2025年8月特朗普和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京（Vladimir Putin）在阿拉斯加埃尔门多夫-理查森联合基地观看的一次飞越，那次有一架B-2“幽灵”和四架F-35参加。

items.title: McChord Encourages Rider Mentorship Through Motorcycle Safety Program
items.author: SrA Benjamin Riddle
items.summary: The 62d Airlift Wing hosted a Department of the Air Force Rider Mentor Program trainer course at Heritage Hill on Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, Sept. 8-9, 2026. The program supports the mandatory motorcycle training requirements of Level II training within one year of earning a Level I initial license and Level III refresher training every five years after. The program takes care to emphasize the decisions that affect rider safety the most.
items.body: The 62d Airlift Wing hosted a Department of the Air Force Rider Mentor Program trainer course at Heritage Hill on Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, Sept. 8-9, 2026. Seven riders from multiple squadrons completed the course, including two members of the 142nd Wing, Oregon Air National Guard. The newly trained mentors will help expand local access to motorcycle safety training and assist experienced riders with mentoring others in their units. The program supports the mandatory motorcycle training requirements of Level II training within one year of earning a Level I initial license and Level III refresher training every five years after. The program takes care to emphasize the decisions that affect rider safety the most. “It comes down to what gets our guardians and our airmen injured, hurt, or killed,” said John McLaughlin, Air Force Safety Center deputy chief of traffic safety and outreach. “It’s the decision making, the behaviors that they’re using while they’re out on motorcycles.” McLaughlin highlighted how the program will be able to give units a more direct path to required training. “This training is a supplement to the current training and an alternative way of acquiring those skills across the DAF,” said McLaughlin. “This program will make it so here at JBLM, training can be done at the squadron level, and you don’t have to go all the way to the installation level to get training.” Before this new program, Air Force riders at JBLM would often need to coordinate through their motorcycle safety representatives, who would coordinate through wing safety who would then schedule training with the Army. The new mentor network will allow MSRs to provide instruction directly to the riders who need it. The course critically prepares mentors to lead discussions and practical exercises that reinforce riding fundamentals, sound judgment and risk management. The program also creates opportunities for riders to learn from one another’s experiences, said McLaughlin. “I can share stories to help others learn so they don’t have to go through some of the experiences I went through,” said McLaughlin. “That’s the main point of the program, current riders mentoring newer and older riders alike to all learn together.” Tech. Sgt. Corey Walrath, 62d Aircraft Maintenance Squadron squadron program manager, who helped bring McLaughlin to JBLM, said the local program gives the wing flexibility to meet increased demands for training. “With the rider mentor program, now Airmen can come to their MSRs or me for the 62d AMXS, and we can come up with a schedule that works for them right then and there,” said Walrath. “This will be able to quickly get them the training they need to stay safe on the roads.” Staff Sgt. Garrett Cofield, 62d Aerial Port Squadron passenger service supervisor, gave his thoughts on how the course reinforced the value of continuing to learn, regardless of experience level. “When I was doing the Level II, I thought I was a really good rider, I was a lot younger and I had a much bigger ego,” said Cofield. “I think coming to these trainings and learning the fundamentals and setting your ego aside is super important.” Ryan Meeks, 62d Airlift Wing occupational safety technician, took time to further highlight the critical nature of the program throughout the DAF. “Inexperienced riders are our primary concern as they account for 90% of the fatalities that the Airforce experiences,” said Meeks “Experienced riders can teach advanced riding techniques, but they also teach awareness, safety, temperament, and maturity factors. Having a trained and experienced rider mentor that you personally know or work with creates an environment of trust and familiarity that cannot be gained in a short class.” The continued growth of the program currently depends on experienced riders stepping forward to mentoring others and leading their unit is fundamental safety, said McLaughlin. If you are interested in becoming an MSR, rider mentor, or rider mentor instructor please contact the wing safety office today at 253-982-9999.
zhParas: 第62空运联队于2026年9月8日至9日在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地（JBLM）的Heritage Hill主办了空军部骑手导师计划教官培训课程。来自多个中队的7名骑手完成了课程，其中包括俄勒冈州空军国民警卫队第142联队的2名成员。新受训的导师将帮助扩大当地获得摩托车安全培训的渠道，并协助经验丰富的骑手指导其所在单位的其他人。该计划支持强制性摩托车培训要求，即在获得I级初始驾照后一年内完成II级培训，此后每五年进行一次III级复训。该计划注重强调对骑手安全影响最大的决策。“归根结底，问题在于是什么导致我们的守护者和空军人员受伤、受到伤害或丧生，”空军安全中心交通安全与外联副主任约翰·麦克劳克林（John McLaughlin）说。“是决策，是他们在骑摩托车时所采取的行为。”麦克劳克林强调，该计划将能够为单位提供更直接的所需培训途径。“这项培训是对现有培训的补充，也是在整个空军部获得这些技能的另一种途径，”麦克劳克林说。“该计划将使得在JBLM这里，培训可以在中队一级完成，你不必一路到基地层级去接受培训。”在这项新计划之前，JBLM的空军骑手通常需要通过他们的摩托车安全代表进行协调，而摩托车安全代表则要通过联队安全部门协调，后者再与陆军安排培训。新的导师网络将使MSR能够直接向需要培训的骑手提供指导。该课程至关重要地培养导师引导讨论和实操练习的能力，以强化骑行基本功、正确判断和风险管理。麦克劳克林说，该计划还为骑手创造了从彼此经验中学习的机会。“我可以分享故事来帮助他人学习，这样他们就不必经历我经历过的一些事情，”麦克劳克林说。“这就是该计划的主旨：现有骑手指导新老骑手，让大家共同学习。”Tech. Sgt. 科里·沃尔拉斯（Corey Walrath），第62飞机维修中队项目主管，曾帮助将麦克劳克林请到JBLM，他说，当地计划使该联队能够灵活满足日益增长的培训需求。“有了骑手导师计划，现在空军人员可以来找他们的MSR，或者来找我（第62飞机维修中队），我们可以当场制定适合他们的安排，”沃尔拉斯说。“这样就能迅速让他们获得在道路上保持安全所需的培训。”Staff Sgt. 加勒特·科菲尔德（Garrett Cofield），第62空中港口中队旅客服务主管，谈到了该课程如何强化了无论经验水平如何都应继续学习的价值。“我参加II级培训时，以为自己是一名非常优秀的骑手，那时我年轻得多，也自负得多，”科菲尔德说。“我认为参加这些培训、学习基本功并放下自负非常重要。”瑞安·米克斯（Ryan Meeks），第62空运联队职业安全技术员，特意进一步强调该计划在整个空军部的关键性质。“经验不足的骑手是我们的首要关切，因为他们占空军所经历死亡事故的90%，”米克斯说。“经验丰富的骑手可以教授高级骑行技术，但他们也传授意识、安全、性情和成熟度等方面的因素。拥有一名你个人认识或共事过的、训练有素且经验丰富的骑手导师，会营造出一种信任和熟悉的氛围，这是短期课程无法获得的。”麦克劳克林说，该计划的持续发展目前取决于经验丰富的骑手挺身而出去指导他人，并带领其单位做好基本安全。如果你有兴趣成为MSR、骑手导师或骑手导师教官，请立即致电253-982-9999联系联队安全办公室。

items.summary: MARINE CORPS LOGISTICS BASE BARSTOW, Calif. —Marines participate in Tactical Combat Casualty Care All Service Members training at the Headquarters Company building aboard Marine Corps Logistics Base Barstow, California, September 23. items.body:
MARINE CORPS LOGISTICS BASE BARSTOW, Calif.

—Marines participate in Tactical Combat Casualty Care All Service Members training at the Headquarters Company building aboard Marine Corps Logistics Base Barstow, California, September 23.

The training refreshed lifesaving skills for Marines who had not been certified in TCCC ASM within the past three years, supporting the installation’s goal of achieving eighty-five percent force certification readiness.

items.title: NETCOM Organizational Day strengthens the team behind the mission
items.author: Amanda Pearson
items.summary: FORT HUACHUCA, Ariz. — Soldiers, Department of the Army Civilians and family members from the Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM) participated in an organizational day last week at Greely Hall, reinforcing the relationships, resilience and trust that help the command accomplish its global mission.
items.body:
FORT HUACHUCA, Ariz. — Soldiers, Department of the Army Civilians and family members from the Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM) participated in an organizational day last week at Greely Hall, reinforcing the relationships, resilience and trust that help the command accomplish its global mission. The event provided the opportunity for participants to connect outside their normal work environments through various entertainment activities. Although the activities differed from the unit’s daily operational requirements, their purpose remained directly connected to readiness.

NETCOM secures, operates and defends the Army’s portion of the Department of War Information Network, a mission that requires personnel to coordinate across organizations, time zones and areas of responsibility. Building trust before it is tested operationally helps teams communicate more effectively, solve problems faster and remain resilient during periods of increased mission demand.

The organizational day also reflected NETCOM’s continued investment in the people responsible for operating and defending the Army’s global network. During the past year, NETCOM personnel supported and defended more than 1 million defense activities every day, 1.2 million Army 365 users, 35,000 BYOAD users, 5 million Army 365 meetings, and more than 283 million emails, across the enterprise.

That focus on mission readiness extended beyond technology. NETCOM’s monthly fitness challenges drew 1,524 participants throughout the enterprise who collectively biked, walked and ran more than 133,994 miles. Participants also completed 1,510,341 push-ups, 51,020 pull-ups, 57,698 burpees and 14,423 minutes of planks. Those figures represent more than physical activity. They demonstrate sustained participation across NETCOM’s globally dispersed workforce and reinforce the command’s understanding that readiness depends on healthy, resilient and connected people.

The event also highlighted the network of resources available to NETCOM Soldiers, civilians and their families across the Fort Huachuca community. Installation support organizations joined the day’s activities, giving attendees an opportunity to connect directly with the people and services that support them beyond the workplace. Representatives from the Fort Huachuca Military Police, Fort Huachuca Fire Department, USO and Army Community Services were on hand to share information, answer questions and demonstrate their continued support to the NETCOM community. Their participation reinforced an important part of readiness: ensuring Soldiers, Civilians and families know where to turn for resources, assistance and support when they need it.

"Family [Organizational] Day recognizes the families that stand beside our service members and support them through the demands of military life. It gives our Soldiers, civilians and their families an opportunity to come together, build relationships, and feel connected to the organization they're a part of," said Cpt. Ara L. Gahan, HHC NETCOM, Company Commander. "That sense of connection doesn't stop when the event ends- it carries back into the workplace, strengthening teamwork, morale, and our ability to support one another as a team."

Because NETCOM’s mission operates continuously, organizational readiness depends on more than technical expertise. It also depends on teams whose members trust one another, communicate openly and understand how their individual contributions support the larger mission.

The organizational day represented a deliberate investment in those relationships. Participants returned to their workplaces with stronger connections across the organization and a renewed understanding that taking care of people is an essential part of sustaining the mission.

As NETCOM continues to modernize and defend the Army’s global network, events that strengthen its workforce help ensure the command remains ready to secure, operate and defend—anytime and anywhere.
zhParas: 亚利桑那州华楚卡堡——来自网络企业技术司令部（NETCOM）的士兵、陆军部文职人员和家属上周在格里利大厅参加了组织日活动，增进了有助于该司令部完成全球任务的关系、韧性与信任。此次活动通过各种娱乐活动，为参与者提供了在正常工作环境之外相互联系的机会。尽管这些活动不同于该部队的日常作战要求，但其目的仍与战备直接相关。
NETCOM 负责保护、运行和防御战争部信息网络中的陆军部分，这一任务要求人员跨组织、跨时区和跨责任区进行协调。在信任经受作战检验之前建立信任，有助于团队更有效地沟通、更快地解决问题，并在任务需求增加期间保持韧性。
组织日也反映出 NETCOM 对其负责运行和防御陆军全球网络的人员的持续投入。过去一年，NETCOM 人员每天在整个企业范围内为超过 100 万次国防活动、120 万 Army 365 用户、3.5 万 BYOAD 用户、500 万次 Army 365 会议以及超过 2.83 亿封电子邮件提供支持和防御。

对任务战备的关注不仅限于技术。NETCOM 的月度体能挑战吸引了整个企业 1,524 名参与者，他们总共骑行、步行和跑步超过 133,994 miles。参与者还完成了 1,510,341 个俯卧撑、51,020 个引体向上、57,698 个波比跳和 14,423 minutes 的平板支撑。这些数字不仅代表身体活动。它们表明 NETCOM 全球分散的员工队伍持续参与，并强化了该司令部的认识：战备取决于健康、有韧性且相互联系的人员。

活动还重点介绍了华楚卡堡社区中 NETCOM 士兵、文职人员及其家属可获得的资源网络。基地支持组织参加了当天的活动，使参与者有机会直接与在工作场所之外为他们提供支持的人员和服务建立联系。华楚卡堡军事警察、华楚卡堡消防局、USO 和陆军社区服务处的代表到场分享信息、回答问题，并展示他们对 NETCOM 社区的持续支持。他们的参与强化了战备的一个重要部分：确保士兵、文职人员和家属在需要时知道去哪里寻求资源、援助和支持。
“家庭[组织]日旨在肯定那些站在我们军人身边、支持他们应对军旅生活各种要求的家属。它让我们的士兵、文职人员及其家属有机会聚在一起、建立关系，并感受到与他们所属组织的联系，”NETCOM 总部与总部连（HHC）连长 Cpt. Ara L. Gahan（阿拉·L·加汉）说。“这种联系感不会在活动结束时停止——它会带回工作场所，增强团队合作、士气，以及我们作为一个团队相互支持的能力。”
由于 NETCOM 的任务连续运行，组织战备不仅取决于技术专长。它还取决于这样的团队：其成员相互信任、坦诚沟通，并理解自己的个人贡献如何支持更大的任务。
组织日是对这些关系的有意投入。参与者返回工作岗位时，整个组织内的联系更加牢固，并重新认识到关心人员是维持任务不可或缺的一部分。
随着NETCOM继续推进现代化并保卫陆军的全球网络，旨在加强其人员队伍的各项活动有助于确保该司令部保持战备状态，能够随时随地保护、运行和防御网络。

活动还重点介绍了华楚卡堡社区中 NETCOM 士兵、文职人员及其家属可获得的资源网络。基地支持组织参加了当天的活动，使参与者有机会直接与在工作场所之外为他们提供支持的人员和服务建立联系。华楚卡堡军事警察、华楚卡堡消防局、USO 和陆军社区服务处的代表到场分享信息、回答问题，并展示他们对 NETCOM 社区的持续支持。他们的参与强化了战备的一个重要部分：确保士兵、文职人员和家属在需要时知道去哪里寻求资源、援助和支持。

“家庭[组织]日旨在肯定那些站在我们军人身边、支持他们应对军旅生活各种要求的家属。它让我们的士兵、文职人员及其家属有机会聚在一起、建立关系，并感受到与他们所属组织的联系，”NETCOM 总部与总部连（HHC）连长 Cpt. Ara L. Gahan（阿拉·L·加汉）说。“这种联系感不会在活动结束时停止——它会带回工作场所，增强团队合作、士气，以及我们作为一个团队相互支持的能力。”

由于 NETCOM 的任务连续运行，组织战备不仅取决于技术专长。它还取决于这样的团队：其成员相互信任、坦诚沟通，并理解自己的个人贡献如何支持更大的任务。

组织日是对这些关系的有意投入。参与者返回工作岗位时，整个组织内的联系更加牢固，并重新认识到关心人员是维持任务不可或缺的一部分。

随着NETCOM继续推进现代化并保卫陆军的全球网络，旨在加强其人员队伍的各项活动有助于确保该司令部保持战备状态，能够随时随地保护、运行和防御网络。

items.title: Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center 75th anniversary
items.author: Cpl Damian Oso
items.summary: The Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center celebrates their 75th anniversary Sept. 25th, 2026. MCMWTC was established in 1951 as the Cold Weather Battalion and has since been a prime force in ensuring the lethality of Marines across the full-spectrum of mountain warfare.

items.title: ARTRANS Data Day Showcases Automated Tools for Global Operations
items.author: Christopher Parr
items.summary: U.S. Army Transportation Command (ARTRANS) showcased how automated data tools are accelerating decision-making and strengthening global logistics during its second annual Data Day, held Sept. 16 at the Seay Auditorium here and streamed live to units globally.
items.body: U.S. Army Transportation Command (ARTRANS) showcased how automated data tools are accelerating decision-making and strengthening global logistics during its second annual Data Day, held Sept. 16 at the Seay Auditorium here and streamed live to units globally. With the theme “Data to Dominance: From Insight to Action,” the event brought together leaders, data scientists and staff officers to highlight the shift from manual tracking to live, automated data pipelines. In her opening comments, ARTRANS Executive Director Kristina M. O’Brien noted that “treating data as a ‘primary weapon system’ is essential for sustaining logistics in high‑intensity operations.” ARTRANS leaders emphasized that the command already operates from a strong data foundation. Moving approximately one million freight shipments and 150,000 ocean shipments annually, ARTRANS “consistently generates and replicates the signal that allows leaders to make informed decisions,” said Bryan J. King, ARTRANS CIO and Deputy G‑6. He added that the event’s success reflects “ARTRANS’ continued growth as a data‑centric organization, developing culture and processes to operationalize this department shift.” More than 350 personnel attended Data Day, including representatives from USTRANSCOM, NGA, the Air Force and peer Army commands. Other speakers demonstrated tools designed to streamline staff processes, including the Maven Smart System and the Maven Linehaul Routing Tool, which automate workflow digitization, route distance calculations and cost‑per‑mile analysis across thousands of carrier routes. A major focus was SITREP.IO, presented by Army Capt. Bradley Miller, chief of the Commander’s Action Group, and Laurie Boros, command knowledge management officer. Miller said the tool “removes no fewer than 20 steps alone within the CAG when generating Situation Reports,” noting that additional action‑officer‑level steps are also eliminated. He emphasized the “centralization and simplification of the input and collection process for all involved parties,” explaining that SITREP.IO standardizes how tactical updates flow into U.S. Transportation Command and Army Materiel Command reports while building consistent historical records and integrated tracking of information requests. Members of the G‑3 directorate unveiled several new automated platforms, including the Maven Global Common Operating Picture, the Maven Port Assessment Tool and the International Requirements Synchronization Matrix. Representatives from the 618th Air Operations Center presented NITMRE Geo, an AI‑enabled geospatial system that alerts operators to emerging mobility risks before they disrupt missions. Laurie Boros, ARTRANS Knowledge Management Officer, said the day’s discussions underscored the cultural transformation required to fully leverage tools like MAVEN. “The real power of a tool like MAVEN isn't just its technical capability; it's the cultural shift it enables,” she said. “T2COM’s HALO brief drove this home: successful transformation requires us to build a shared understanding of our own processes, which is the foundation for capturing sustainable corporate knowledge. When we combine that process discipline with powerful technology, we don't just get a better report—we create a more agile, collaborative command that can deliver insights at mission speed.” Leaders stressed that cultural change is as important as technology. “Our goal is simple: give our people their time back,” said Elbert “Aaron” Lunn, ARTRANS chief data and technical officer. He said real‑time tools allow leaders to make “fast, smart calls that win,” replacing hours of manual product building. O’Brien noted the tools have already proven their value during real‑world operations, including Operation Epic Fury, where automated insights replaced slide‑based updates and helped identify bottlenecks and infrastructure limitations. Data Day attendees said the demonstrations underscored the power of data standardization. Fiona Hershberger, knowledge manager for the Transportation Engineering Agency, said SITREP.IO and other tools “significantly reduce the staff burden and increase standardization,” but she also emphasized the broader impact. “Replacing legacy spreadsheets creates a single source of truth,” she said. “Once data is consolidated, it can be analyzed, and that analysis often reveals insights masked by legacy processes. Today showed how these platforms don’t just make reporting easier—they expand what’s possible. They demonstrate how inputs can move seamlessly through leadership levels, how shared data strengthens operational understanding, and how automation frees staff to focus on mission outcomes rather than formatting products.” Hershberger called the NITMRE Geo demonstration “a truly impressive look at what can be accomplished with the right blend of SME involvement and premier industry technology experts.” As ARTRANS continues modernizing its battle rhythms, leaders urged staff to rethink processes rather than simply digitize old ones. “The real win is when we feel empowered to rethink how we work, not just where we work,” Lunn said.
zhParas: 美国陆军运输司令部（ARTRANS）在其第二届年度“数据日”活动上展示了自动化数据工具如何加快决策并强化全球物流。此次活动于9月16日在当地西伊礼堂举行，并向全球部队直播。活动以“数据制胜：从洞察到行动”为主题，汇聚了领导人、数据科学家和参谋军官，重点展示从人工跟踪向实时自动化数据管道的转变。ARTRANS 执行主任克里斯蒂娜·M·奥布莱恩（Kristina M. O’Brien）在开幕致辞中指出，“将数据视为‘主要武器系统’对于在高强度行动中维持后勤至关重要。”ARTRANS 领导人强调，该司令部已依托坚实的数据基础运行。ARTRANS 每年运送约100万批货运和15万批海运货物，“持续生成并复制信号，使领导人能够作出知情决策，”ARTRANS 首席信息官兼 G-6 副职布赖恩·J·金（Bryan J. King）说。他补充说，此次活动的成功反映了“ARTRANS 作为一个以数据为中心的组织持续成长，正在发展文化和流程，以将这一部门转变付诸实施。”超过350名人员参加了“数据日”，包括来自美国运输司令部（USTRANSCOM）、国家地理空间情报局（NGA）、空军和陆军同级司令部的代表。其他发言者演示了旨在简化参谋流程的工具，包括 Maven Smart System 和 Maven Linehaul Routing Tool，这些工具可在数千条承运线路上自动完成工作流程数字化、路线距离计算和每英里成本分析。一个主要焦点是由美国陆军 Capt. 布拉德利·米勒（Bradley Miller）——指挥官行动组组长——和司令部知识管理官劳里·博罗斯（Laurie Boros）展示的 SITREP.IO。米勒说，该工具“单是在 CAG 内生成态势报告时就省去了不少于20个步骤”，并指出行动军官层级的额外步骤也被消除。他强调“所有相关方的输入和收集流程的集中化与简化”，并解释说，SITREP.IO 规范了战术更新流入美国运输司令部和陆军物资司令部报告的方式，同时建立一致的历史记录和信息请求的综合跟踪。G-3 处成员发布了若干新的自动化平台，包括 Maven 全球通用作战图、Maven 港口评估工具和国际需求同步矩阵。第618空中作战中心的代表展示了 NITMRE Geo，这是一个具备人工智能能力的地理空间系统，可在新出现的机动风险扰乱任务之前提醒操作人员。ARTRANS 知识管理官劳里·博罗斯表示，当天的讨论凸显了要充分运用像 MAVEN 这样的工具所需的文化转型。她说：“像 MAVEN 这样的工具的真正力量不仅在于其技术能力，还在于它所促成的文化转变。”“T2COM 的 HALO 简报让人深刻认识到这一点：成功的转型要求我们对我们自身流程建立共同理解，这是捕获可持续组织知识的基础。当我们将这种流程纪律与强大技术结合起来时，我们得到的不仅是一份更好的报告——我们创建的是一个更敏捷、更协作的司令部，能够以任务速度提供洞察。”领导人强调，文化变革与技术同样重要。ARTRANS 首席数据与技术官埃尔伯特·“亚伦”·伦（Elbert “Aaron” Lunn）说：“我们的目标很简单：把时间还给我们的员工。”他说，实时工具使领导人能够作出“快速、明智且能取胜的决策”，取代数小时的人工产品制作。奥布莱恩指出，这些工具已在“史诗之怒”行动等现实行动中证明了自身价值；在该行动中，自动化洞察取代了基于幻灯片的更新，并帮助识别瓶颈和基础设施限制。“数据日”与会者表示，这些演示凸显了数据标准化的力量。运输工程局知识经理菲奥娜·赫什伯格（Fiona Hershberger）表示，SITREP.IO 和其他工具“显著减轻了参谋负担并提高了标准化程度”，但她还强调了更广泛的影响。她说：“取代传统电子表格可创建单一事实来源。”“一旦数据得到整合，就可以进行分析，而这种分析往往会揭示被传统流程掩盖的洞察。今天表明，这些平台不仅让报告更容易——它们还拓展了可能性。它们展示了输入如何无缝地流经各级领导层，共享数据如何增强作战理解，以及自动化如何让参谋人员腾出精力专注于任务成果，而不是格式化产品。”赫什伯格称 NITMRE Geo 演示“真正令人印象深刻地展示了在领域专家参与和顶尖行业技术专家的恰当结合下能够取得的成果。”随着 ARTRANS 继续推进其作战节奏现代化，领导人敦促参谋人员重新思考流程，而不是仅仅将旧流程数字化。伦说：“真正的胜利在于，我们感到有权重新思考我们如何工作，而不仅仅是在哪里工作。”

items.title: Ambient Listening Streamlines Care at DDEAMC
items.author: Kalee Sexton
items.summary: Ambient listening technology is giving providers at Dwight D. Eisenhower Army Medical Center (DDEAMC) another tool to support patient care.
items.body:
Ambient listening technology is giving providers at Dwight D. Eisenhower Army Medical Center (DDEAMC) another tool to support patient care.

The technology works like a digital scribe on the computer during an appointment. With the patient’s permission, it listens to the conversation, turns the discussion into text and organizes key medical details into a draft clinical note. The provider reviews the draft, makes any needed changes and completes the record.

Military hospitals and clinics are adopting ambient listening to help improve the patient experience and reduce the time providers spend documenting visits. The goal is to give providers more time to listen, ask questions and connect with patients.

For patients, that can mean more eye contact and a more natural conversation during an appointment. For providers, it can mean less time spent typing during the visit or completing notes after clinic hours.

Michele Meddings, PA-C, uses ambient listening in the Pain Management Clinic at DDEAMC. She said she explains the technology to patients before using it.

“Once I explain that it is like a digital scribe, patients understand that it listens in the background and creates a note from our conversation,” Meddings said. “It helps me get home to my family on time, and it helps capture the things patients wanted to say that day.”

The technology only records medical information discussed during the visit. Providers still guide the appointment, use their clinical judgment and review each note before it becomes part of the patient’s record.

Meddings said the tool has helped her keep the focus on the patient instead of on a computer screen.

“Before, I was writing notes throughout the visit because I needed to remember what to document later,” she said. “Now, I can place the computer to the side, listen to the patient and be present in that moment. I know I can go back and review what was captured.”

That extra attention can be important during complex visits, when patients may bring up more than one concern. For example, a patient may come to the clinic for low back pain and mention elbow pain during the same conversation. Ambient listening can identify the elbow pain as a separate concern in the draft note.

The provider can then document that concern and include any follow-up guidance, such as seeing a primary care provider for further evaluation.

Meddings said patients appreciate knowing their concerns are being captured.

“Some patients say they told several providers about an issue, but it was never in the note,” she said. “That can create problems later, especially when they need care from another provider or transition to the Department of Veterans Affairs.”

Accurate documentation supports continuity of care. It gives future providers a clearer picture of the patient’s concerns, symptoms and care plan.

Patient choice remains an important part of ambient listening. Military Health System guidance states that providers must receive verbal consent before turning on the tool. Patients may decline its use at any time during their visit.

Ambient listening is one example of how military treatment facilities are using newer technology to support providers and patients.

For Meddings, the value comes back to the patient encounter.

“It allows me to really listen,” she said. “I can focus on the patient, make sure their concerns are captured and still have time to complete the work that comes with each visit.”
zhParas: 环境监听技术为德怀特·D·艾森豪威尔陆军医疗中心（DDEAMC）的医护人员提供了又一件支持患者诊疗的工具。
该技术在就诊过程中就像电脑上的数字抄写员。在患者许可的前提下，它聆听对话，将谈话内容转为文字，并把关键医疗细节整理成一份临床记录草稿。医护人员审阅草稿，作出必要修改后完成记录。
军队医院和诊所正在采用环境监听技术，以帮助改善患者就医体验，并减少医护人员用于记录就诊情况的时间。目标是让医护人员有更多时间倾听、提问并与患者交流。
对患者而言，这意味着就诊时能有更多眼神接触和更自然的对话；对医护人员而言，这意味着在就诊过程中花在打字上的时间更少，也不必在下班后补写记录。
米歇尔·梅丁斯（Michele Meddings），PA-C，在 DDEAMC 的疼痛管理门诊使用环境监听技术。她说，她在使用前会向患者解释这项技术。
“当我解释说它就像一位数字抄写员后，患者就明白它在后台聆听，并根据我们的对话生成记录，”梅丁斯说。“它帮助我准时回家与家人团聚，也帮助记录下患者当天想说的内容。”
该技术只记录就诊期间讨论的医疗信息。医护人员仍主导就诊过程，运用其临床判断，并在每条记录纳入患者病历之前进行审阅。
梅丁斯说，这项工具帮助她把注意力放在患者身上，而不是电脑屏幕上。
“以前，我在整个就诊过程中都在记笔记，因为我需要记住之后要记录什么，”她说。“现在，我可以把电脑放到一边，倾听患者，并全身心投入当下。我知道我可以回看所记录的内容。”
这种额外的关注在复杂的就诊中可能很重要，因为患者可能会提出多个问题。例如，患者可能因下背痛来到诊所，却在同一段对话中提到肘部疼痛。环境聆听可以在记录草稿中把肘部疼痛识别为一项独立的问题。
医疗服务提供者随后可以记录该问题，并纳入任何随访指导，例如去看初级保健提供者以接受进一步评估。
梅丁斯（Meddings）说，患者很感激知道自己的问题正被记录下来。
“有些患者说，他们曾向多位医疗服务提供者讲过某个问题，但记录中从未体现，”她说。“这会在之后造成问题，尤其是在他们需要接受另一位医疗服务提供者的诊疗或转至美国退伍军人事务部时。”
准确的记录有助于医疗服务的连续性。它让未来的医疗服务提供者更清楚地了解患者的问题、症状和诊疗计划。
患者选择仍然是环境聆听的重要组成部分。军事卫生系统指南指出，医疗服务提供者在开启该工具前必须获得口头同意。患者可在就诊期间随时拒绝使用该工具。
环境聆听是军队医疗机构如何利用较新技术支持医疗服务提供者和患者的一个例子。
对梅丁斯（Meddings）而言，其价值最终要回到与患者的问诊交流上。
“它让我能够真正地去倾听，”她说。“我可以专注于患者，确保他们的关切得到记录，同时仍有时间完成每次就诊伴随的工作。”
