items.title: Florida Marine Corps facility opens indoor range, brings weapons training on-site
items.author: Dustin Senger
items.summary: Marine Corps Support Facility Blount Island opened a six-lane modular indoor firing range Sept. 24, bringing firearms qualifications and other training to the installation for Marine Corps Police Department officers.
items.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — Marine Corps Support Facility Blount Island opened a six-lane modular indoor firing range Sept. 24, bringing firearms qualifications and other training to the installation for Marine Corps Police Department officers.

The department now controls the schedule for pistol, rifle and shotgun qualifications, low-light drills and other courses of fire, allowing officers to train during the day or at night, regardless of weather.

“Every mission on this installation depends on people who can protect it,” said U.S. Marine Corps Col. David Merles, the facility’s commanding officer. Merles declared the range open, and Marine Corps Police Capt. Jacob Dickerson, the range’s certifying official, then fired a ceremonial first round.

Minutes later, downrange lights cut through a faint haze from pistol fire. Black curtains framed the firing lanes, and the polished gray floor reflected the light. At the firing line, officers aimed at paper targets marked with rows of circles.

“Let’s speed it up a little bit,” said Lt. Joseph Maxfield, the police department’s assistant operations officer, as he led the first fundamentals drill. “Move to the second target over. Stand by.”

“Threat,” he called, cueing officers to fire downrange.

Maxfield coached the officers in grip, stance, trigger control and shooting while moving. Such drills reinforce safe weapons handling and marksmanship for personnel responsible for installation defense and law enforcement.

Before the range opened, the department trained at outdoor ranges operated by the Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office and the Nassau County Sheriff’s Office and, occasionally, the St. Marys Police Department in Georgia. Access depended on those agencies’ schedules, and officers adjusted shifts to conduct low-light drills after dark.

“It’s been a long time coming — a lot of work went into opening this,” Maxfield said. “This is more convenient, and we can do low-light shooting with patrol lights flashing.”

The range also gives Marines assigned to the Security Augmentation Force more flexibility to complete required weapons training while meeting their primary-duty responsibilities. They augment police in protecting the people, infrastructure and operations that support Blount Island Command’s global sustainment mission.

Planning for the range began in November 2022. Marine Corps Installations Command funded construction of the foundation and utility connections. Marine Corps Installations East funded the range’s relocation from Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina.

The Marine Corps facility later invested nearly $100,000 in repairs and modifications. The range passed required industrial hygiene testing in August. The coordinated effort paired an existing modular range valued at nearly $2 million with the infrastructure and improvements needed to place it into service.

“We are putting the training and tools behind the responsibility we ask our police officers to carry,” Merles said. “A federal police career here means protecting the people and capabilities that allow the Marine Corps to project and sustain combat power around the world.”

Application instructions for anticipated federal police vacancies at the Marine Corps facility are available through a public notice on USAJobs.gov .

The range opened during National Preparedness Month, following a full-scale force protection exercise and a coordinated response to a simulated worst-case fuel spill at the Marine Corps facility earlier in September. The Marine Corps’ 2026 theme was “Prepare Today. Protect Tomorrow.”
zhParas: 佛罗里达州杰克逊维尔——9月24日，海军陆战队支援设施布朗特岛启用了一座设有6条射道的模块化室内靶场，使海军陆战队警察局的警员可在该基地内进行枪械资质考核及其他训练。
该警察局现在自行掌控手枪、步枪和霰弹枪资质考核、低光演练及其他射击课目的日程安排，使警员无论天气如何都能在白天或夜间训练。
“这座基地上的每一项任务都离不开能够保卫它的人，”该设施司令、美国海军陆战队上校 David Merles（戴维·默尔斯）说。Merles 宣布靶场启用，随后靶场认证官、海军陆战队警察上尉 Jacob Dickerson（雅各布·迪克森）鸣响了仪式性的第一枪。
几分钟后，靶场远端的灯光穿透了手枪射击留下的淡淡烟雾。黑色幕布框住各条射道，抛光的灰色地面映着灯光。在射击线前，警员们瞄准印有一排排圆圈的纸质靶。
“我们稍微加快一点速度，”警察局助理作战官、中尉 Joseph Maxfield（约瑟夫·马克斯韦尔）在带领首项基础动作训练时说，“移到左边第二个靶。准备。”
“有威胁，”他喊道，示意警员向靶场远端开火。
Maxfield 就握枪、站姿、扳机控制和移动中射击对警员进行指导。此类训练可强化负责基地防御和执法的人员的安全武器操作与射击技能。
靶场启用前，该警察局在杰克逊维尔治安官办公室和拿骚县治安官办公室运营的户外靶场训练，偶尔也前往佐治亚州圣玛丽斯警察局训练。能否使用取决于这些机构的日程安排，警员们还需调整班次，以便在天黑后进行低光演练。
“这来得不容易——为启用它投入了大量工作，”马克斯菲尔德（Maxfield）说。“这更方便，而且我们可以在巡逻灯闪烁的情况下进行低光射击。”
该靶场还使被分配至安全增强部队的海军陆战队队员在履行主要职责的同时，拥有更大灵活性来完成所要求的武器训练。他们增援警察，保护那些支持布朗特岛司令部全球保障任务的人员、基础设施和行动。
该靶场的规划始于2022年11月。海军陆战队设施司令部资助了地基和公用设施连接的建设。海军陆战队东部设施司令部资助了该靶场从北卡罗来纳州勒琼营海军陆战队基地的搬迁。
该海军陆战队设施随后投入近10万美元进行维修和改造。该靶场于8月通过了所要求的工业卫生检测。这项协调努力将一座价值近200万美元的现有模块化靶场与使其投入使用所需的基础设施和改造结合起来。
“我们正在以训练和工具来支撑我们要求警员承担的责任，”默尔斯（Merles）说。“在这里从事联邦警察职业，意味着保护那些使海军陆战队能够在全球投射和维持作战能力的人员和能力。”
该海军陆战队设施预计出现的联邦警察职位空缺的申请说明，可通过 USAJobs.gov 上的公告获取。
该靶场在国家应急准备月期间启用；此前9月早些时候，该海军陆战队设施举行了一次全面部队防护演习，并对模拟的最坏情况燃料泄漏作出协调应对。海军陆战队2026年的主题是“今日准备，保护明天。”

该靶场还使被分配至安全增强部队的海军陆战队队员在履行主要职责的同时，拥有更大灵活性来完成所要求的武器训练。他们增援警察，保护那些支持布朗特岛司令部全球保障任务的人员、基础设施和行动。

该靶场的规划始于2022年11月。海军陆战队设施司令部资助了地基和公用设施连接的建设。海军陆战队东部设施司令部资助了该靶场从北卡罗来纳州勒琼营海军陆战队基地的搬迁。

该海军陆战队设施随后投入近10万美元进行维修和改造。该靶场于8月通过了所要求的工业卫生检测。这项协调努力将一座价值近200万美元的现有模块化靶场与使其投入使用所需的基础设施和改造结合起来。

“我们正在以训练和工具来支撑我们要求警员承担的责任，”默尔斯（Merles）说。“在这里从事联邦警察职业，意味着保护那些使海军陆战队能够在全球投射和维持作战能力的人员和能力。”

该海军陆战队设施预计出现的联邦警察职位空缺的申请说明，可通过 USAJobs.gov 上的公告获取。

该靶场在国家应急准备月期间启用；此前9月早些时候，该海军陆战队设施举行了一次全面部队防护演习，并对模拟的最坏情况燃料泄漏作出协调应对。海军陆战队2026年的主题是“今日准备，保护明天。”

items.title: Ready to Respond
items.author: TSgt Jana Somero
items.summary: Vermont Air National Guard firefighters joined airport personnel, community partner agencies, and hundreds of volunteers for the triennial Federal Aviation Administration aircraft rescue firefighting exercise at the Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport, Sept. 12, 2026.
items.body:
SOUTH BURLINGTON, Vt. – Vermont Air National Guard firefighters joined airport personnel, community partner agencies, and hundreds of volunteers for the triennial Federal Aviation Administration aircraft rescue firefighting exercise at the Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport, Sept. 12, 2026.

This was a full-scale aircraft emergency exercise designed to test emergency responder’s ability to respond to a mass casualty aviation event. The exercise evaluates interagency coordination, emergency procedures, and the ability of the responders themselves to save lives.

“The whole point of this exercise is to assess everyone’s ability to respond to an aircraft incident,” said Tim Francis, a civilian fire captain for the VTANG. “In this year’s scenario we had an Embraer 170 experiencing a right-side engine fire that occurred on takeoff, which ultimately resulted in a runway excursion causing a post-crash fire with multiple victims.”

VTANG firefighters responded to the simulated emergency, providing initial aircraft fire suppression and rescue capabilities while integrating with other county fire departments. They then responded from standby positions to protect the available evacuation routes, enter the aircraft, and then begin assessing and removing the casualties for further care.

The response is organized through a shared incident command structure. This allows VTANG firefighters and other local fire and emergency response agencies to quickly integrate their personnel and resources to get the mission complete as timely as they can.

“It solidifies the relationships we have with other agencies,” Francis said. “Being able to include them and work face to face with them is absolutely integral. Together, we validated a mutual aid plan which had emergency responders coming from several counties working together. That plan was tested. It worked.”

Responding to an aircraft emergency of this scale can quickly exceed the personnel and resources available within a single department. Nearly a dozen community partners participated in this exercise, which allowed the VTANG to test and integrate with other agencies that could very well be called upon during a real world emergency.

Successfully completing the scenario was only one measure of the exercise. Putting the plans into reality also exposes responders to the resource challenges that can be difficult to replicate in a classroom.

“It’s easy to sit back and tabletop things in a classroom setting,” said Dustin Lasher, an assistant fire chief of operations participating in the exercise. “But at the end of the day you don’t know what you need or are lacking until you are actually faced with those challenges yourself.”

For the VTANG firefighters, physically executing the response allows them to identify communication limitations, equipment considerations, and areas where the current established procedures could better be adjusted to aid in real world operations. These observations provide the participating agencies with information they need to refine their training, policies, and equipment requirements.

“If our policies aren’t aligning to how we’re executing the mission, it’s a good mark for me to go back and say, ‘Hey, this isn’t matching real world operations, we need to adjust this policy,’” Francis stated.

Being able to train under realistic conditions gave the VTANG firefighters and their community partners the opportunity to validate not only what worked, but also where they may need to adapt. Whether responding with a full team or adapting to limited resources and members, the exercise reinforced the importance of trained Airmen, established partnerships, and the ability to adjust when conditions differ from the plan.

“Timelines change, but at the end of the day, the mission is still getting done,” Francis said. “We’re ready to respond.”
zhParas: 佛蒙特州南伯灵顿——佛蒙特州空军国民警卫队消防员与机场人员、社区合作机构以及数百名志愿者一起，参加了2026年9月12日在帕特里克·莱希伯灵顿国际机场举行的美国联邦航空管理局三年一度飞机救援消防演习。
这是一次全规模飞机紧急情况演习，旨在检验应急响应人员应对大规模伤亡航空事件的能力。演习评估跨机构协调、应急程序以及响应人员自身的救人能力。
“这次演习的全部意义在于评估每个人应对飞机事件的能力，”佛蒙特州空军国民警卫队（VTANG）文职消防队长蒂姆·弗朗西斯（Tim Francis）说。“在今年的想定中，我们设定一架 Embraer 170 在起飞时发生右侧发动机起火，最终导致飞机冲出跑道，并造成坠机后起火，有多名受害者。”
VTANG消防员响应了模拟紧急情况，在与其他县消防部门协同的同时，提供初始飞机灭火和救援能力。随后，他们从待命位置出动，保护可用撤离路线，进入飞机，然后开始评估并转移伤员，以便进一步救治。
应急响应通过共享的事件指挥架构组织。这使VTANG消防员以及其他当地消防和应急响应机构能够迅速整合人员和资源，以尽可能及时完成任务。
“这巩固了我们与其他机构的关系，”弗朗西斯说。“能够让他们参与进来并面对面合作，绝对不可或缺。我们共同验证了一项互助计划，来自几个县的应急响应人员在该计划下协同工作。该计划经受了检验。它奏效了。”
应对这种规模的飞机紧急情况，可能很快超出一个部门可用的人员和资源。近十二个社区合作伙伴参加了此次演习，这使VTANG得以测试并与其他机构整合；在现实世界的紧急情况中，这些机构很可能会被调集参与。
成功完成该想定只是此次演习的一项衡量标准。将计划付诸现实，也让响应人员直面资源挑战，而这些挑战往往难以在课堂上复现。
“坐在教室环境里做桌面推演很容易，”参加演习的负责行动的助理消防队长达斯汀·拉舍（Dustin Lasher）说，“但归根结底，除非你自己真正面对那些挑战，否则你不知道自己需要什么或缺少什么。”
对VTANG消防员来说，实际执行响应使他们能够发现通信局限、装备考量，以及当前既定程序可如何更好地调整以协助现实行动。这些观察结果为参与机构提供了改进其训练、政策和装备需求所需的信息。
“如果我们的政策与我们执行任务的方式不一致，那对我来说就是一个很好的信号，让我可以回去说，‘嘿，这不符合现实行动，我们需要调整这项政策，’”弗朗西斯（Francis）表示。
能够在逼真条件下训练，使VTANG消防员及其社区伙伴有机会不仅验证哪些做法有效，还验证他们可能需要在哪些方面进行调整。无论是全员响应，还是适应有限的资源和人员，这次演习都强化了训练有素的空军人员、既有的伙伴关系，以及在条件与计划不同时作出调整的能力的重要性。
“时间表会变化，但归根结底，任务仍然要完成，”弗朗西斯说，“我们随时准备响应。”

items.title: Michigan’s NADWC Positions Camp Grayling for Directed Energy Weapons Testing and Experimentation
items.author: MAJ Trevor Kay
items.summary: Camp Grayling and the National All-Domain Warfighting Center offer defense companies a path to test directed energy weapons, counter-UAS systems and supporting technologies in realistic operational conditions.
items.body:
Directed energy weapons are moving rapidly from concept to capability. At the Air, Space & Cyber Conference in National Harbor, Maryland, defense companies showcased high-energy lasers, high-power microwave systems, counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), advanced sensors, power solutions, thermal-management equipment and battle-management networks.

For any defense industry planner or research and development leader, the associated question is nearly universal: where can these systems be tested against the conditions they may face in actual operations?

A system can perform well during a controlled demonstration and still struggle when exposed to the elements and the operational environment. Inevitably within the fog of war—weather changes, communications are disrupted, positioning data is degraded, the electromagnetic spectrum is crowded, or operators must make decisions with incomplete information. System performance can depend on a wide variety of variables. Treating capability holistically, the emitter, sensing hardware, target tracking, power generation, cooling mechanisms, command and control, safety, spectrum access and trained operators all contribute to weapon effectiveness, and cannot be discounted as novel. Given these requirements for function, dedicated range space to test directed energy weapons through a wide variety of variables is paramount to their development.

Michigan’s National All-Domain Warfighting Center, anchored by Camp Grayling Joint Maneuver Training Center, is positioned to help industry answer those questions.

The Michigan Department of Military and Veterans Affairs is inviting companies developing directed energy weapons and enabling technologies to bring forward their test requirements. Through the National All-Domain Warfighting Center and its Joint Experimentation Warfighting Laboratory, or JEWL, Michigan can help companies define their operational problems, identify feasible range conditions, coordinate military and technical partners, and develop a responsible test plan.

Testing Directed Energy Weapons Against Operational Problems

Directed energy weapons do not arrive with identical test requirements.

A laser-based counter-UAS system may need space to assess detection, tracking, engagement geometry and safety controls. A high-power microwave system may require a realistic electromagnetic environment. Other companies may need to examine the issues that determine whether a directed energy weapon can operate as part of a larger defensive architecture, including resilient power, thermal management, autonomy, sensor-fusion software, data integration, target identification, degraded communications, positioning and command-and-control system interoperability.

Camp Grayling and Alpena provide options across those requirements.

The National All-Domain Warfighting Center includes nearly 148,000 acres of maneuver space at Camp Grayling and more than 17,000 square miles of special-use military airspace at the Alpena Combat Readiness Training Center (CRTC). The combined environment supports training, experimentation and testing across land, air, maritime, space and cyber domains.

That scale gives companies room to test directed energy weapons under conditions that better reflect battlefield friction. It also allows the National All-Domain Warfighting Center to connect a technology demonstration to a military problem set rather than treating the range as a showroom.

The Michigan National Guard has developed Exercise Northern Strike into a joint, multinational readiness exercise that includes contested logistics, integrated counter-UAS protection measures, maritime targeting, cyber and electromagnetic activities, and an operational environment consistent with large-scale combat operations (LSCO). Those conditions can provide useful context for defense industry companies seeking to move a promising directed energy weapon prototype forward from concept to operational capability.

Demonstrated DDIL Testing at Camp Grayling

Camp Grayling recently demonstrated its ability to support system testing in a Denied, Disrupted, Intermittent and Limited, or DDIL, environment.

From Sept. 13–18, the Michigan Department of Military and Veterans Affairs coordinated with Army Test and Evaluation Command (ATEC) and the Threat System Management Office to host a DDIL testing environment for the defense industry at Camp Grayling. The event was aligned with the Army’s Permissive Range Initiative, which expands opportunities for industry and service members to mutually test and evaluate emerging technologies in realistic operational environments.

Participating organizations on the DDIL testing environment included Eagle NXT, Noah Labs, Archangel Response Corps and Superfocus AI. Unmanned aerial systems used autonomous reasoning software to identify targets in an urban environment across three increasingly difficult scenarios. Systems were also evaluated in positioning, navigation and timing, or PNT, and radio-frequency DDIL conditions.

PNT DDIL conditions create a high-threat environment in which traditional positioning, navigation and timing sources are compromised. Radio-frequency DDIL conditions challenge systems to continue operating when communications are degraded, disrupted or intermittent.

These conditions are directly relevant to directed energy weapons and counter-UAS developers. A directed energy weapon must detect, identify, track and respond to a threat while operating within a larger defensive network. Its sensors, battle-management tools and operators may need to continue supporting decisions when data links, radio-frequency conditions or positioning sources are compromised.

“The combination of expansive training areas, diverse terrain, electromagnetic spectrum access and multi-domain capabilities allows innovators and military organizations to test systems under realistic conditions, identify gaps and rapidly improve them,” said Col. Lucas Lanczy, commander of Camp Grayling Joint Maneuver Training Center.

The DDIL event exhibited how Camp Grayling can support tailored testing for companies working through complicated technical and operational requirements. For directed energy weapons developers, that may include evaluating counter-UAS systems in degraded communications conditions, assessing sensor performance in a contested electromagnetic environment, or examining how a directed energy weapon contributes to an integrated air and missile defense architecture.

A Direct Path for Industry

In August, the U.S. Army identified Camp Grayling, through the National All-Domain Warfighting Center, as one of four premier stateside military test ranges available to private industry for internal research, development and rapid experimentation. The Army’s Permissive Range Initiative created a digital entry point for companies seeking access to military test infrastructure, including industry start-ups and companies that may not already hold a federal contract.

That designation gives industry a starting point. JEWL provides the coordination needed to turn an inquiry into a feasible test event.

“Our mission is simple: We want to bridge the gap between a great concept and a fielded capability, and we use the unique agility of the National Guard to get disruptive tech to the Joint Warfighter, faster,” said Capt. Nicholas S. Schweikart, deputy director of JEWL at the National All-Domain Warfighting Center. “We put Army and Air Force scientists, engineers and operators in the same room to innovate at the edge of what is possible. That gives industry direct feedback from the people who will use their systems.”

At the NADWC, industry does not need to arrive with a finished military test plan. A company should bring a clear requirement, an understanding of the capability it wants to evaluate and a willingness to test against real operational variables.

Per Schweikart, JEWL can help determine:

The operational problem the technology is intended to address

The range, airspace, spectrum and environmental conditions required

The military and technical partners required to support the test

Appropriate safety, classification and operational security controls

Whether the effort should occur at Camp Grayling, Alpena CRTC or multiple locations through a phased approach

How the test can produce useful feedback for the next design iteration

“Industry should not have to solve government coordination problems alone,” Schweikart said. “You bring us the requirement, and we will help them determine what a responsible, highly useful test event looks like. We take the burden of coordinating range conditions, expertise and partners off the company so that they can focus on building the technology that our warfighters need.”

Directed Energy Weapons Require Integrated Testing

Directed energy weapons have potential applications in counter-UAS operations, installation defense, air and missile defense, and force protection. They may provide commanders with additional options against low-cost aerial threats that can impose significant costs on conventional interceptor inventories. That potential still must be demonstrated under demanding conditions. Those conditions are available in Michigan.

A directed energy weapon must be powered, cooled, aimed, networked, operated safely and sustained. It may also function alongside sensors, command-and-control tools, other defensive systems and human operators. Testing at the National All-Domain Warfighting Center can address those connected requirements. Companies may evaluate a high-energy laser’s ability to detect and track unmanned aircraft, assess a high-power microwave system in a realistic electromagnetic environment, or examine how power, thermal management, autonomy and data fusion affect mission performance.

The test environment can also be adapted to the maturity of the technology. Some efforts may begin with a focused technical evaluation. Others may require a campaign that progresses from individual component testing to integrated counter-UAS or multi-domain experimentation.

Every request requires deliberate review. Range capacity, safety planning, airspace coordination, environmental requirements, classification, electromagnetic spectrum considerations and operational security all affect test design. Some efforts may fit at Camp Grayling. Others may require Alpena CRTC, support from Army Test and Evaluation Command, a different configuration of National All-Domain Warfighting Center locations or a phased approach before a larger event.

Michigan’s National All-Domain Warfighting Center Is Open for Directed Energy Weapons Testing

The National All-Domain Warfighting Center gives directed energy weapons and counter-UAS companies a place to test, learn, adjust and return to the range on an expedient timeline.

Camp Grayling and Alpena CRTC offer large-scale maneuver space, special-use airspace, electromagnetic spectrum availability, multi-domain training conditions and connections to military organizations working through current operational problems. JEWL provides a coordination point for companies that need help translating a technology requirement into a responsible and useful test event.

The JEWL’s commitment in this effort is to provide industry with the best available venue and conditions to test their directed energy weapons, and advance system development to benefit the warfighter at the leading edge of the battlefield.

Companies interested in testing directed energy weapons, counter-UAS systems and enabling technologies at Camp Grayling and the National All-Domain Warfighting Center can begin their inquiry through the Army Test Range Reservation portal.

Defense industry companies can advance their research with a range reservation inquiry without defining their perfect test plan. Rather, bring the requirements and vision for your project and the National All-Domain Warfighting Center will work to support the shared effort with world-class resources.

Army Test Range Reservation Portal: https://testrange.army.mil/ArmyRangeReservation/s/?tabset-5dba2=3
zhParas: 定向能武器正迅速从概念走向实战能力。在马里兰州国家港举行的航空、航天与网络会议上，国防企业展示了高能激光、高功率微波系统、反无人机系统（UAS）、先进传感器、电源解决方案、热管理设备以及战场管理网络。
对任何一位国防工业规划人员或研发负责人而言，随之而来的问题几乎具有普遍性：这些系统能在哪里针对其在实际作战中可能面临的条件接受测试？

一套系统在受控演示中可能表现良好，但一旦暴露于自然环境和作战环境中仍可能举步维艰。在战争迷雾中，天气变化、通信中断、定位数据降级、电磁频谱拥挤，或操作人员不得不在信息不完整的情况下作出决策，都在所难免。系统性能可能取决于多种变量。若从整体视角看待作战能力，则发射装置、传感硬件、目标跟踪、发电、冷却机制、指挥控制、安全、频谱使用权限以及训练有素的操作人员都会影响武器效能，不能因其新颖而加以忽视。鉴于这些功能要求，专门划设靶场空间，使定向能武器在多种变量条件下接受测试，对其研发至关重要。
以格雷灵营联合机动训练中心为核心的密歇根州国家全领域作战中心，具备帮助工业界回答这些问题的条件。
密歇根州军事与退伍军人事务部正邀请研发定向能武器及使能技术的企业提出其测试需求。通过国家全领域作战中心及其联合试验作战实验室（JEWL），密歇根州可以帮助企业界定其作战问题、确定可行的靶场条件、协调军方与技术合作伙伴，并制定负责任的测试计划。
针对作战问题测试定向能武器
定向能武器的测试需求并不相同。
以激光为基础的反无人机系统可能需要空间，以评估探测、跟踪、交战几何关系和安全控制。高功率微波系统可能需要真实的电磁环境。其他企业则可能需要考察那些决定定向能武器能否作为更大防御体系一部分运行的问题，包括韧性电源、热管理、自主性、传感器融合软件、数据集成、目标识别、降级通信、定位以及指挥控制系统的互操作性。
格雷林营和阿尔皮纳为满足这些需求提供了多种选择。
国家全领域作战中心包括格雷林营近148,000 acres的机动空间，以及阿尔皮纳战备训练中心（CRTC）超过17,000 square miles的专用军事空域。这一联合环境支持陆、空、海、天和网络领域的训练、实验与测试。
这种规模使企业有空间在更能反映战场摩擦的条件下测试定向能武器。它也使国家全领域作战中心能够将技术演示与军事问题集相衔接，而不是把靶场当作展示厅。
密歇根国民警卫队已将“北方打击”演习发展为联合、多国战备演习，内容包括对抗性后勤、综合反无人机系统防护措施、海上目标瞄准、网络与电磁活动，以及与大规模作战行动（LSCO）相一致的作战环境。这些条件可为那些寻求将一款有前景的定向能武器原型从概念推进到作战能力的国防工业公司提供有益背景。
格雷林营的DDIL测试演示
格雷林营最近展示了其在拒止、受扰、间歇和受限（DDIL）环境中支持系统测试的能力。
9月13日至18日，密歇根州军事与退伍军人事务部与陆军测试与评估司令部（ATEC）及威胁系统管理办公室协调，在格雷林营为国防工业主办了一个DDIL测试环境。该活动与陆军的Permissive Range Initiative保持一致，该倡议扩大了工业界和军人共同在现实作战环境中测试与评估新兴技术的机会。
参与DDIL测试环境的组织包括Eagle NXT、Noah Labs、Archangel Response Corps和Superfocus AI。无人机系统使用自主推理软件，在三种难度递增的场景中识别城市环境中的目标。系统还在定位、导航与授时（PNT）以及射频DDIL条件下接受了评估。
PNT DDIL 条件会形成一种高威胁环境，在其中传统定位、导航和授时源受到削弱。射频 DDIL 条件则对系统在通信降级、中断或间歇时继续运行构成挑战。
这些条件与定向能武器和反无人机系统研发人员直接相关。定向能武器必须在更大的防御网络中运行，同时探测、识别、跟踪并应对威胁。当数据链、射频条件或定位源受到削弱时，其传感器、战斗管理工具和操作人员可能需要继续支持决策。
“广阔的训练区域、多样的地形、电磁频谱接入和多域能力相结合，使创新者和军事组织能够在逼真条件下测试系统、发现差距并迅速改进系统，”格雷灵营联合机动训练中心指挥官 Col. 卢卡斯·兰齐（Lucas Lanczy）说。
此次 DDIL 活动展示了格雷灵营如何为正在解决复杂技术和作战需求的公司支持定制化测试。对定向能武器研发人员而言，这可能包括在通信降级条件下评估反无人机系统、在有争议电磁环境中评估传感器性能，或考察定向能武器如何为一套一体化防空反导体系作出贡献。
为工业界提供直接路径
8月，美国陆军通过国家全域作战中心（National All-Domain Warfighting Center）将格雷灵营确定为美国本土四个首要军事试验靶场之一，可供私营工业用于内部研究、开发和快速实验。陆军的“许可靶场倡议”（Permissive Range Initiative）为寻求使用军事试验基础设施的公司创建了一个数字化入口，其中包括行业初创企业和可能尚未持有联邦合同的公司。
这一认定给工业界提供了一个起点。JEWL 提供必要的协调，将询问转化为可行的试验活动。
“我们的使命很简单：我们想弥合一个伟大构想与实际部署能力之间的差距，并利用国民警卫队独特的敏捷性，更快地将颠覆性技术送到联合作战人员手中，”国家全域作战中心 JEWL 副主任 Capt. 尼古拉斯·S·施韦卡特（Nicholas S. Schweikart）说。“我们让陆军和空军的科学家、工程师和操作人员同处一室，在可能性的边缘进行创新。这使工业界能够直接从将使用其系统的人员那里获得反馈。”
在NADWC，企业无需带着一份已完成的军事测试计划到场。公司应带着明确的需求、对其想要评估的能力的理解，以及针对真实作战变量进行测试的意愿。
据施韦卡特（Schweikart）称，JEWL可帮助确定：
该技术旨在解决的作战问题
所需的靶场、空域、频谱和环境条件
支持测试所需的军事和技术合作伙伴
适当的安全、密级和作战安全控制
这项工作应在Camp Grayling、Alpena CRTC进行，还是通过分阶段方式在多个地点进行
测试如何为下一轮设计迭代提供有用反馈
“工业界不应独自解决政府协调问题，”施韦卡特（Schweikart）说。“你们把需求带给我们，我们将帮助他们确定一场负责任且极具价值的试验活动应该是什么样。我们把协调靶场条件、专业知识和合作伙伴的负担从企业身上卸下，这样他们就能专注于构建我们作战人员所需的技术。”
定向能武器需要综合测试
定向能武器在反无人机系统作战、设施防御、防空反导和部队防护方面具有潜在应用。它们可为指挥官提供更多选项，以应对低成本空中威胁——这类威胁可能给常规拦截弹库存带来沉重成本。这种潜力仍必须在严苛条件下得到验证。密歇根州具备这些条件。
定向能武器必须获得供电、冷却、瞄准、联网、安全操作并持续运行。它还可能要与传感器、指挥控制工具、其他防御系统和人工操作员协同工作。在国家全域作战中心进行测试可以解决这些相互关联的需求。企业可以评估高能激光探测和跟踪无人机的能力，在真实电磁环境中评估高功率微波系统，或考察电力、热管理、自主性和数据融合如何影响任务性能。
测试环境还可以根据技术的成熟度进行调整。有些工作可能从有针对性的技术评估开始。另一些工作则可能需要开展一系列活动，从单个组件测试逐步推进到一体化反无人机系统或多域试验。
每项请求都需要经过审慎审查。靶场容量、安全规划、空域协调、环境要求、密级、电磁频谱考虑因素和行动安全都会影响测试设计。有些工作可能适合在格雷林营进行。另一些则可能需要阿尔皮纳CRTC、美国陆军测试与评估司令部的支持、国家全域作战中心不同地点的配置，或在更大规模活动前采取分阶段方法。
密歇根州国家全域作战中心开放定向能武器测试
国家全域作战中心为定向能武器和反无人机系统企业提供了一个可以测试、学习、调整并及时重返靶场的场所。
格雷灵营和阿尔皮纳 CRTC 提供大规模机动空间、特殊用途空域、电磁频谱可用性、多域训练条件，以及与正在解决当前作战问题的军事组织之间的联系。JEWL 为需要帮助将技术需求转化为负责任且有用的测试活动的公司提供协调点。
JEWL 在这项工作中的承诺是，为工业界提供现有最佳场地和条件，以测试其定向能武器，并推进系统开发，使战场最前沿的作战人员受益。
有意在格雷灵营和国家全域作战中心测试定向能武器、反无人机系统及使能技术的公司，可通过陆军试验靶场预约门户开始垂询。
国防工业企业可以通过靶场预约咨询推进其研究，而无需先制定完美的测试计划。相反，只需提出项目的需求和愿景，国家全域作战中心将致力于以世界级资源支持这一共同努力。
陆军试验靶场预约门户：https://testrange.army.mil/ArmyRangeReservation/s/?tabset-5dba2=3

“工业界不应独自解决政府协调问题，”施韦卡特（Schweikart）说。“你们把需求带给我们，我们将帮助他们确定一场负责任且极具价值的试验活动应该是什么样。我们把协调靶场条件、专业知识和合作伙伴的负担从企业身上卸下，这样他们就能专注于构建我们作战人员所需的技术。”

定向能武器需要综合测试

定向能武器在反无人机系统作战、设施防御、防空反导和部队防护方面具有潜在应用。它们可为指挥官提供更多选项，以应对低成本空中威胁——这类威胁可能给常规拦截弹库存带来沉重成本。这种潜力仍必须在严苛条件下得到验证。密歇根州具备这些条件。

定向能武器必须获得供电、冷却、瞄准、联网、安全操作并持续运行。它还可能要与传感器、指挥控制工具、其他防御系统和人工操作员协同工作。在国家全域作战中心进行测试可以解决这些相互关联的需求。企业可以评估高能激光探测和跟踪无人机的能力，在真实电磁环境中评估高功率微波系统，或考察电力、热管理、自主性和数据融合如何影响任务性能。

测试环境还可以根据技术的成熟度进行调整。有些工作可能从有针对性的技术评估开始。另一些工作则可能需要开展一系列活动，从单个组件测试逐步推进到一体化反无人机系统或多域试验。

每项请求都需要经过审慎审查。靶场容量、安全规划、空域协调、环境要求、密级、电磁频谱考虑因素和行动安全都会影响测试设计。有些工作可能适合在格雷林营进行。另一些则可能需要阿尔皮纳CRTC、美国陆军测试与评估司令部的支持、国家全域作战中心不同地点的配置，或在更大规模活动前采取分阶段方法。

密歇根州国家全域作战中心开放定向能武器测试

国家全域作战中心为定向能武器和反无人机系统企业提供了一个可以测试、学习、调整并及时重返靶场的场所。

格雷灵营和阿尔皮纳 CRTC 提供大规模机动空间、特殊用途空域、电磁频谱可用性、多域训练条件，以及与正在解决当前作战问题的军事组织之间的联系。JEWL 为需要帮助将技术需求转化为负责任且有用的测试活动的公司提供协调点。

JEWL 在这项工作中的承诺是，为工业界提供现有最佳场地和条件，以测试其定向能武器，并推进系统开发，使战场最前沿的作战人员受益。

有意在格雷灵营和国家全域作战中心测试定向能武器、反无人机系统及使能技术的公司，可通过陆军试验靶场预约门户开始垂询。

国防工业企业可以通过靶场预约咨询推进其研究，而无需先制定完美的测试计划。相反，只需提出项目的需求和愿景，国家全域作战中心将致力于以世界级资源支持这一共同努力。

items.title: Bells Across America ceremony honors fallen heroes of North Carolina
items.author: 2LT Brooke Waugh
items.summary: CAMP LEJEUNE, N.C. – Honorary guests and local North Carolina leaders attended the Bells Across America ceremony at the Carolina Museum of the Marine in Jacksonville, Sept. 24.
items.body:
CAMP LEJEUNE, N.C. – Honorary guests and local North Carolina leaders attended the Bells Across America ceremony at the Carolina Museum of the Marine in Jacksonville, Sept. 24. The ceremony was held as part of the U.S. Navy Gold Star Program to honor and remember the sacrifice of fallen service members and provide long-term support to their surviving families.

Bells Across America ceremonies are held nationwide each September. This year’s ceremony honored more than a dozen Gold Star families in attendance. “This is the second year we’ve been able to hold this formal event here in North Carolina” Alicia McCoy, Navy Gold Star Coordinator, said. “It’s because of the wonderful folks here at Marine Corps Installation East that this was able to take place and i am extremely grateful”

Col. Gregory Pace, deputy commander, Marine Corps Installations East-Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, also delivered remarks emphasizing that the ceremony honored those lost and reaffirmed that their service and sacrifice will never be forgotten, nor will their families cease to be part of the installation community.

“Each name represents a life, each name represents a story; that’s why the ringing of the bell carries such meaning,” Pace said. “To our gold star families, as long as we continue to speak their names, tell their stories, and honor their service, their legacy remains a lasting part of our community.”

McCoy closed the ceremony by reading the names of service members who have fallenin the past year. She concluded, “The mission of the Gold Star Program is to ensure that our nation’s heroes are not forgotten and that their loved ones and surviving family members remain connected to the military community.”
zhParas: 北卡罗来纳州勒琼营——9月24日，荣誉嘉宾和北卡罗来纳州当地领导人出席了在杰克逊维尔卡罗来纳海军陆战队博物馆举行的“全美钟声”仪式。该仪式是美国海军金星计划的一部分，旨在缅怀并纪念阵亡军人的牺牲，并为其遗属提供长期支持。
“全美钟声”仪式每年9月在全国各地举行。今年的仪式向出席的十多个金星家庭表达了敬意。海军金星计划协调员艾丽西亚·麦考伊（Alicia McCoy）说：“这是我们第二年能够在北卡罗来纳州举行这一正式活动。正是因为海军陆战队东部设施司令部这里的优秀人员，这次活动才得以举行，我对此极为感激。”
海军陆战队东部设施司令部—勒琼营海军陆战队基地副司令 Col. 格雷戈里·佩斯（Gregory Pace）也发表了讲话，强调这一仪式缅怀了阵亡者，并重申他们的服役和牺牲永远不会被遗忘，他们的家人也不会脱离基地社区。
“每一个名字都代表一条生命，每一个名字都代表一个故事；正因如此，敲响钟声才具有如此意义，”佩斯说。“致我们的金星家庭：只要我们继续说出他们的名字、讲述他们的故事、缅怀他们的服役，他们的精神遗产就将永远是我们社区持久的一部分。”
麦考伊通过宣读过去一年阵亡军人的姓名，为仪式画上句号。她最后说：“金星计划的使命是确保我们国家的英雄不被遗忘，并确保他们的亲人和遗属仍然与军队社区保持联系。”

items.title: Naval Air Station Pensacola holds annual Bells Across America for Fallen Service Members ceremony at Naval Aviation Memorial Chapel
items.author: ENS Anthony Aspenson
items.summary: The Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola Fleet and Family Support Center (FFSC) held the annual Bells Across America for Fallen Service Members ceremony at the Naval Aviation Memorial Chapel onboard the installation.
items.body: NAS PENSACOLA, Fla. — The Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola Fleet and Family Support Center (FFSC) held the annual Bells Across America for Fallen Service Members ceremony at the Naval Aviation Memorial Chapel onboard the installation. Retired U.S. Army Cavalry Scout and combat veteran, Robert “Matt” McDaniel, was the guest speaker for the ceremony. As an initiative of the Navy Gold Star program, ceremonies were conducted concurrently throughout the United States to remember and celebrate the lives of fallen service members from all branches of the military, regardless of their cause of death. The Navy Gold Star program serves as the advocate for the families and provides support, information and services such as reserved Gold Star family parking. Base Commanders have designated parking in various locations such as the Commissary, Exchanges, FFSC and Military Treatment Facilities (MTF) to promote awareness, educate the military community on the sacrifices of families of deceased active duty and to honor their loss. Capt. Chandra Newman, commanding officer of NAS Pensacola, delivered the opening remarks for the ceremony. “Your loved one has given the ultimate sacrifice and we know that there is nothing we can say or do that will completely comfort you in your loss, but we are dedicated to delivering on the promise of taking care of our own by providing support to surviving families,” said Newman. “For us here at NAS Pensacola, there is no greater honor than to support the families of those who have died in service to our nation.” Bells Across America is held at U.S. military installations worldwide on the same day and is coordinated in partnership with the Gold Star Program. NGS Program supports family members of fallen military members by providing them with resources as well as assisting with counseling, financial planning and job hunting. NGS personnel also assist with paperwork and requests for documents while ensuring survivors remain connected with the Navy family. Founded in 1826, Naval Air Station Pensacola, known as the “Cradle of Naval Aviation,” supports operational and training missions for several tenant commands, Naval Air Technical Training Center, Naval Aviation Schools Command and Center for Technical Training. The installation also hosts Marine Aviation Training Support Group 21 and Marine Aviation Training Support Group 23 and serves as the headquarters for Naval Education and Training Command. In addition to an active airfield, NAS Pensacola maintains a deepwater port supporting operations for the U.S. Coast Guard.
zhParas: 佛罗里达州彭萨科拉海军航空站——彭萨科拉海军航空站（NAS）舰队与家庭支持中心（FFSC）在该基地内的海军航空纪念教堂举行了年度“全美钟声纪念阵亡军人”仪式。退役美国陆军骑兵侦察兵、战斗老兵罗伯特·“马特”·麦克丹尼尔（Robert “Matt” McDaniel）担任仪式特邀演讲人。作为海军金星计划的一项倡议，全美各地同时举行仪式，以缅怀和纪念各军种阵亡军人，不论其死因。海军金星计划为这些家庭提供权益倡导，并为他们提供支持、信息和服务，例如预留的金星家庭停车位。基地指挥官已在军人服务社（Commissary）、军人商店（Exchange）、FFSC 和军事治疗设施（MTF）等多个地点指定停车位，以提高认识、教育军人社区了解已故现役人员家庭所作的牺牲，并向他们失去的亲人致敬。NAS Pensacola 指挥官 Capt. 钱德拉·纽曼（Chandra Newman）为仪式致开幕词。“你们的亲人作出了终极牺牲，我们知道，无论我们说什么或做什么，都无法完全抚慰你们失去亲人的痛苦，但我们致力于兑现照顾好自己人的承诺，为遗属家庭提供支持，”纽曼说。“对于 NAS Pensacola 的我们来说，最大的荣耀莫过于支持那些为国捐躯者的家庭。”“全美钟声”活动于同一天在全球各地的美国军事基地举行，并与金星计划合作协调。NGS 计划通过向阵亡军人家庭成员提供资源，以及协助心理咨询、财务规划和求职，来支持他们。NGS 人员还协助处理文书工作和文件申请，同时确保遗属与海军大家庭保持联系。彭萨科拉海军航空站成立于 1826 年，被誉为“海军航空兵的摇篮”，为多个驻站单位，包括海军航空技术训练中心、海军航空学校司令部和海军技术训练中心，提供作战与训练支持。该基地还驻有海军陆战队航空训练支援第 21 大队和海军陆战队航空训练支援第 23 大队，并作为海军教育与训练司令部总部。除现役机场外，NAS Pensacola 还维护一个深水港，支持美国海岸警卫队的行动。

items.body:
Catterick Training Area firing and activity forecast

Annual firing schedule for Battle Hill, Bellerby, Feldom and Wathgill Ranges.

Ministry of Defence and Defence Infrastructure Organisation

7 September 2022

24 September 2026 — See all updates

Catterick Training Area firing forecast for October 2026

Catterick Training Area firing forecast for September 2026

Public access to the ranges is permitted on specified tarmac roads, public footpaths and bridleways only when no red flags or red lights are displayed, and outside the scheduled firing times. Public access is governed by the Catterick Training Area byelaws .

Do not enter the danger area when the range is in use, this is a danger to life. If ‘red flags’ or lights are hoisted, regardless of the timings, do not enter the training area. Learn more about accessing MOD training areas safely .

items.title: Guidance: Otterburn firing times
items.summary: Dates and times when Otterburn and Redesdale ranges and Bellshiel demolition range are being used for live firing.
items.body:
As seen in the Security Defence Review, the Army are at heightened readiness due to a new era of threat. This has placed greater demands on the Defence Training Estate across the UK, which is being used for training more regularly and at shorter notice.

As such, the firing time notifications published on Gov.UK have been standardised to show the daily timings for when live-firing is permitted on the UK DTE. This is a change from the previous method of showing when training bookings had been made in advance.

This to ensure safety of all users, as it is not possible to change Gov.UK notifications at short notice. Broadly, the only guaranteed safe times for access are before or after the firing times provided on this page, however there may be exceptional circumstances where extensions have been requested.

If you wish to use the DTE for recreation, please always refer to onsite safety warning signals to understand if the site is safe to access before doing so.

Danger - When warning signals are displayed, regardless of the timings, do not cross the range boundary.

Warning signals are red flags by day and red lamps by night; range boundaries are marked by red and white poles.

Red flags and red lamps indicate that live firing is taking place within the range boundaries.

Do not enter the danger area when in use, this could result in loss of life.

Do not touch any military debris, it may be dangerous. Please note the location and inform a Training Safety Officer (TSO) via 0191 239 4261 or the police.

Learn more about accessing MOD training areas

Public access to military areas - GOV.UK
zhParas: 正如《安全防务评估》所述，由于进入新的威胁时代，陆军处于高度战备状态。这对英国各地的国防训练场地提出了更高要求，这些场地正被更频繁且更短通知期内用于训练。
因此，发布在 Gov.UK 上的射击时间通知已标准化，以显示英国国防训练场地每日允许实弹射击的时间。这不同于以往显示提前预订训练时间的方法。
这样做是为了确保所有使用者的安全，因为无法在短时间内更改 Gov.UK 上的通知。总体而言，唯一有保障的安全进入时间是本页所列射击时间之前或之后，但在特殊情况下，可能会申请延长时间。
如果您希望将国防训练场地用于休闲活动，请务必先查看现场安全警告信号，以了解该场地是否可以安全进入。
危险——当显示警告信号时，无论时间如何，都不要越过靶场边界。
警告信号白天为红旗，夜间为红灯；靶场边界用红白相间的柱子标示。
红旗和红灯表示靶场边界内正在进行实弹射击。
危险区域在使用时切勿进入，否则可能导致人员死亡。
请勿触摸任何军事残骸，它们可能很危险。请记录位置，并拨打 0191 239 4261 通知训练安全官（TSO）或警方。
进一步了解如何进入国防部训练区域
公众进入军事区域 - GOV.UK

Ministry of Defence and Defence Infrastructure Organisation

items.title: Italy taps state-owned firms to build two naval destroyers in $4.2 billion deal
items.author: Tom Kington
items.summary: Italy has signed to buy two new naval destroyers that will mark a quantum leap in capabilities for the Italian navy, the ships’ builders have promised.
items.body:
ROME — Italy has signed to buy two new naval destroyers that will mark a quantum leap in capabilities for the Italian navy, the ships’ builders have promised.

In a deal brokered by European procurement office OCCAR, Italy signed a €3.7 billion ($4.2 billion) for two so-called DDX destroyers for delivery in 2033 and 2035.

The deal was signed with Orizzonte Sistemi Navali (OSN), an Italian joint venture in which state shipyard Fincantieri holds 51% and state defense giant Leonardo has the remaining 49%. With a displacement of 13,500 tonnes, the 180-meter DDX destroyers will carry a crew of 251 and have a range of 4,000 nautical miles, Fincantieri said in a statement.

The combat system supplied by Leonardo will feature “advanced digitalization”, while the vessel will also include a “DC power sub-network with its associated energy storage system, an innovative stabilization system integrated with the steering system, new algorithms and methodologies for calculating thermal and electrical balances, and further digital developments of the Ship Management System,” the firms said.

The vessels will feature Leonardo’s SADOC 5 command-and-control system, digital S-band AESA radar and MBDA weapon systems, the firms added.

After ordering FREMM-class frigates, PPA multimission ships, a new landing helicopter dock, new submarines and logistics vessels, the DDX order marks the continuation of a fleet renewal splurge for the Italian navy.

The destroyers will sail alongside but ultimately replace the Italian navy’s two Horizon vessels, a navy spokesman told Defense News.

Tom Kington is the Italy correspondent for Defense News.
zhParas: 罗马——意大利已签署协议购买两艘新型海军驱逐舰，承建方承诺，这将是意大利海军作战能力的一次质的飞跃。
在欧洲采购机构 OCCAR 的斡旋下，意大利签署了一份价值 37 亿欧元（42 亿美元）的合同，购买两艘所谓的 DDX 驱逐舰，交付时间分别为 2033 年和 2035 年。
该合同与意大利合资企业 Orizzonte Sistemi Navali（OSN）签署，其中国有船厂 Fincantieri 持股 51%，国有防务巨头 Leonardo 持有其余 49% 的股份。Fincantieri 在一份声明中表示，DDX 驱逐舰长 180 米，排水量 13,500 吨，舰员编制 251 人，续航里程 4,000 海里。
两家公司表示，Leonardo 提供的作战系统将具备“先进的数字化”特征，该舰还将配备“直流电力子网及其配套储能系统、与操舵系统一体化的创新稳定系统、用于计算热平衡与电力平衡的新算法和新方法，以及舰船管理系统（Ship Management System）的进一步数字化开发”。
两家公司补充说，这些舰艇将配备 Leonardo 的 SADOC 5 指挥与控制系统、数字式 S 波段 AESA 雷达以及 MBDA 武器系统。
在订购 FREMM 级护卫舰、PPA 多任务舰艇、一艘新型直升机船坞登陆舰、新型潜艇和后勤舰船之后，这份 DDX 订单标志着意大利海军舰队更新的大规模采购仍在持续。
一名海军发言人向《防务新闻》（Defense News）表示，这些驱逐舰将与意大利海军现有的两艘“地平线”级舰艇一同服役，但最终将取而代之。
汤姆·金顿（Tom Kington）是《防务新闻》驻意大利记者。

items.title: US to provide critical but more limited capabilities to NATO, top commander says
items.author: Sabine Siebold, Reuters
items.summary: NATO’s top commander said on Thursday the United States would continue to provide “critical but more limited capabilities” to the alliance.
items.body:
NATO’s top commander said on Thursday the United States would continue to provide “critical but more limited capabilities” to the alliance as Europeans take up a greater role in defending the continent.

U.S. Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, was speaking in a phone interview with Reuters en route to a change of command ceremony at a NATO headquarters in Norfolk, Virginia, where a British army general will take over from a U.S. Navy vice admiral.

However, NATO recently announced that is stepping up intelligence-sharing in response to a wave of sabotage and other incidents apparently linked to Russia but should be “calm and confident” that it can handle any threat posed by Moscow, the alliance’s top commander told Reuters on Thursday.

The comments by US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich came after Denmark’s defense intelligence service warned that Russia was likely to intensify a hybrid war — a term that covers a range of attacks below the level of a conventional military assault — against the West in the coming months.

The Danish service added there was “a low but growing risk” that Moscow might launch a limited military attack against one or several NATO countries that border Russia.

“It’s concerning,” Grynkewich, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, said of a string of incidents in recent weeks including an attempted drone attack at Germany’s Leipzig/Halle Airport and a Russian ship firing flares towards a Danish military helicopter.

“But we should be calm and confident that we as an alliance, the most powerful alliance in history, have the tools that we need and have the mechanisms that we need in order to manage the risk here,” he added.

Moscow has repeatedly denied any involvement in hybrid warfare or sabotage operations in NATO countries, or plotting any confrontation.

PUTIN BETTER NOT TRY ATTACK ‘ON MY WATCH’, GENERAL SAYS

Grynkewich was speaking in a phone interview with Reuters en route to a change-of-command ceremony at a NATO headquarters in Norfolk, Virginia, where a British army general is taking over from a US Navy vice admiral.

Asked about the risk of a limited Russian attack on NATO territory, Grynkewich stressed the alliance’s readiness for any such contingency, saying such a development was “unlikely but something that we can’t rule out”.

Grynkewich dismissed suggestions that Russian President Vladimir Putin might see an opportunity to strike at NATO, given that the US has used up much of its global stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles in the war with Iran, according to people familiar with the data.

“Absolutely not. He better not try it on my watch,” he said, adding NATO was well positioned to defend every inch of its territory.

“If we proceed from the phase we’re in and we start to see emerging threats, I’m confident that I have the authorities now that I need in order to take actions to deter any aggression against the alliance.”

NATO IN MIDST OF CHANGE AS EUROPEANS TAKE GREATER ROLE

The handover of Norfolk to a European commander is part of a broader reshuffle in keeping with US President Donald Trump’s demands that European nations take more responsibility for their own security. It will also see a European taking charge of NATO’s Joint Force Command in Naples.

NATO’s Joint Force Command Norfolk is responsible for operations in the Arctic and northern Europe as well as protecting transatlantic resupply routes.

Attempting to reassure European allies concerned about an ongoing review of US forces on the continent, Grynkewich said Washington would continue “to provide critical but more limited capabilities” to NATO as Europeans took on a greater role.

He said there was “no predetermined outcome” in terms of how many US troops would remain in Europe and “what the capabilities are that might relocate”. About 80,000 US troops are currently based on the continent.

Trump has repeatedly threatened to leave NATO, which has been dominated by the US since its establishment in 1949, accusing Europeans of being free-riders on security.
zhParas: 北约最高指挥官周四表示，随着欧洲人在保卫欧洲大陆方面承担更大角色，美国将继续向该联盟提供“关键但更有限的能力”。
美国空军上将阿莱克瑟斯·格林凯维奇（Alexus Grynkewich）是北约欧洲盟军最高司令，他在前往弗吉尼亚州诺福克一处北约总部参加指挥权交接仪式途中接受路透社电话采访时作出上述表示。在那里，一名英国陆军将领将接替一名美国海军中将。
不过，北约最近宣布正在加强情报共享，以应对一波显然与俄罗斯有关的破坏和其他事件，但应当“冷静而自信”地认为能够应对莫斯科构成的任何威胁，北约最高指挥官周四对路透社表示。
美国空军上将阿莱克瑟斯·格林凯维奇的上述评论，是在丹麦国防情报局警告俄罗斯可能在未来数月加大对西方发动混合战争之后作出的——该术语涵盖一系列低于常规军事攻击门槛的攻击。
丹麦该机构还表示，莫斯科可能对一个或多个与俄罗斯接壤的北约国家发动有限军事攻击，这一风险“虽低但正在上升”。
“这令人担忧，”北约欧洲盟军最高司令格林凯维奇在谈到最近数周发生的一系列事件时说，其中包括德国莱比锡/哈勒机场发生的一起未遂无人机袭击，以及一艘俄罗斯舰船向一架丹麦军用直升机发射信号弹。
“但我们应该冷静而自信，作为史上最强大的联盟，我们拥有所需的工具，也拥有所需的机制，以便管控这里的风险，”他补充说。
莫斯科多次否认参与北约国家的混合战争或破坏行动，也否认策划任何对抗。
将军称，普京（Putin）最好别想“在我任内”发动攻击
格林凯维奇（Grynkewich）是在前往弗吉尼亚州诺福克一个北约总部参加指挥权交接仪式途中接受路透社电话采访时说这番话的。仪式上，一名英国陆军上将将接替一名美国海军中将。
当被问及俄罗斯对北约领土发动有限攻击的风险时，格林凯维奇强调，北约已做好应对任何此类突发情况的战备，称这一事态发展“不太可能，但也不能排除”。
格林凯维奇驳斥了有关俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京（Vladimir Putin）可能看到打击北约机会的说法，因为据熟悉相关数据的人士称，美国在与伊朗的战争中已消耗掉其全球高精度远程导弹库存的大部分。
“绝对不会。他最好别想在我任内尝试，”他说，并补充称北约完全有能力保卫其每一寸领土。
“如果我们从当前所处阶段出发，并开始看到新出现的威胁，我有信心，我现在已拥有所需的授权，可以采取行动威慑针对北约的任何侵略。”
随着欧洲人发挥更大作用，北约正处于变革之中
将诺福克移交给一名欧洲指挥官，是更广泛人事调整的一部分，此举符合美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）要求欧洲国家为自己的安全承担更多责任的主张。这也将意味着由一名欧洲人执掌北约那不勒斯联合部队司令部。
北约诺福克联合部队司令部负责北极和北欧地区的行动，以及保护跨大西洋补给路线。
格林凯维奇（Grynkewich）试图安抚对正在进行的驻欧美军审查感到担忧的欧洲盟友。他表示，随着欧洲人承担更大角色，华盛顿将继续向北约“提供关键但更为有限的能力”。
他说，就多少美军将留在欧洲以及“哪些能力可能转移”而言，没有“预先确定的结果”。目前约有8万美军驻扎在欧洲大陆。
特朗普多次威胁要退出北约，并指责欧洲人在安全上搭便车。北约自1949年成立以来一直由美国主导。

Langport Range and dry training area firing notice October 2026

Langport range involves live firing with rifles.

Dry military training at Breech Wood involves blank ammunition, pyrotechnics, vehicles and helicopters.

Do not enter the danger area when the range is in use, this is a danger to life. Learn more about accessing MOD training areas safely .

Military court centres court listings

Court listings for the military court centres.

Ministry of Defence

6 January 2012

24 September 2026 — See all updates

Military Court Centre Listings 25 September to 9 October 2026

PDF , 118 KB , 4 pages

In line with the government’s transparency and open data initiative, the Military Court Service is to publish the court listings for the military court centres.

Each court listing covers the next one or two week assize period. This will be published on the internet by the last working day in advance of the assize period.

In addition to this, the court listings are published using digital signage technology within the reception areas of both military court centres.

Please be aware that the court listings are subject to change after publication, if you wish to find out more please contact the relevant military court centre. Details can be found at the bottom of each court listing.

Military Court Service

items.title: Why the last tactical mile is crucial to acquisition reform
items.author: Dr. Katherine A. McGrady
items.summary: If acquisition reform is to succeed, it must migrate to the warfighter's last tactical mile, the president and chief executive officer of CNA writes.
items.body:
The Pentagon is right to treat acquisition reform as a warfighting imperative. In an era when technology is evolving fast, and our adversaries have built arsenals designed to compete asymmetrically, those who can adapt at speed will win.

The effort to implement the Warfighting Acquisition System — transforming the acquisition system around speed, accountability and mission relevance — is both necessary and overdue.

However, if this reform is to deliver its full promise, it must extend beyond headquarters processes, portfolio structures and contracting authorities. Acquisition reform needs to migrate to the last tactical mile — where warfighters confront real-world friction, adapt in real time and generate operational lessons that should shape requirements, accelerate integration and compress acquisition timelines.

The true test of these reforms will not be how quickly decisions move through the system, but how effectively the system learns from the edge, where combat effectiveness is ultimately determined. The avenue to more certain victory leads to and from the warfighter, embracing analysis at the last tactical mile.

America’s warfighters operate at the edge, just as good operations analysts — like those in my own organization — must do in a fast-moving acquisition ecosystem. Successful acquisition reform will need insights from the edge, empowered by empirically trained analysts (uniformed and civilian) who understand systems, tactics, strategy and operations as seen from the perspective of the sailor, soldier, airman, guardian or Marine.

Speed in acquisition will not be achieved by process reform alone. Analysis at the tactical edge is often overlooked but in need of energy and capital to capture insights that drive decisions. Rapid acquisition to field systems that provide military utility demands a continuous learning loop between those who build capability and those who employ it under actual operating conditions — and the ability to measure results quickly.

In this loop, field-level insights should not be treated as downstream feedback after system deployment; they must become upstream drivers of requirements refinement, system integration and prioritization.

By institutionalizing this feedback loop, the department can reduce costly redesign cycles, shorten decision timelines and field capabilities that are not only delivered faster but have greater military value. This is consistent with the department’s own shift toward “speed of relevance,” operational outcomes, and fulfilling the promise to the warfighter.

The department does not need to build this learning architecture from scratch. Proven models already exist in pockets within the force. The Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory, for example, works closely with warfighters to test and analyze new systems. The operator perspective gets fused early into the technical development process, which then allows fielding at speed. This approach to development can outpace program-of-record development, even when going after the same warfighting gaps.

But this warfighter-centric approach should not be confined to formal military innovation organizations alone. Operator-informed analysis must extend across the defense ecosystem, accelerating integration, reducing acquisition timelines and scaling trusted results.

This is not mere assertion. When acquisition works, whether rapid or otherwise, it does so in part because analysts got in the foxhole, in the aircraft, or inside the combat information center to assess, validate and inform acquisition efforts from the point of view of the warfighter.

I know, because my analysts have led that kind of impactful work. We have designed and executed tests of prototypes in the real world, providing independent technical analysis of performance. Analysis at the tactical edge has uncovered critical problems that have to be addressed before warfighters can safely use systems. It has also revealed new tactical use cases for systems — ones that weren’t anticipated by the manufacturer.

The complexity of the counter-IED fight in Operations Iraqi Freedom and Enduring Freedom offers a clear case where warfighter feedback alone was not enough to assess a technology’s utility. So many counter-IED systems were being pushed to the warfighters that it became important to understand which systems worked under which conditions.

Yet one of the most challenging problems in analysis is proving a negative. In other words, if an IED did not go off, was that because of the counter-IED system or not? Our analysts deployed alongside Marine Corps units to collect data and employed complex statistical methods to make that determination. Lives were at stake, and our analyses made a difference.

The department’s shift to the Warfighting Acquisition System is both necessary and timely. Victory on future battlefields belongs to the nation that can create military advantage through rapid acquisition and wartime adaptation. That much is clear. But enduring speed does not come from process redesign alone. It comes from building an acquisition enterprise that learns from the warfighter — where data is analog and results require deep insight to interpret.

If the department fully integrates such a learning loop, it will do more than shorten timelines. It will create a force that adapts faster, integrates better and delivers combat-relevant capability at the pace warfare demands. This is how acquisition reform becomes warfighting advantage.

Dr. Katherine A. McGrady is the president and chief executive officer of CNA, which operates the Center for Naval Analyses, a federally funded research and development center that pioneered the field of operations analysis in support of the U.S. Navy during World War II.

items.title: So Long, Pave Hawk: Air Force’s HH-60G Combat Rescue Helicopter Completes Final Flight
items.author: Greg Hadley
items.summary: The Air Force’s HH-60G Pave Hawk helicopter made its final flight earlier this month. The 129th Rescue Wing retired its last HH-60G with a final flight and ceremony on Sept. 10 at Moffett Air National Guard Base, Calif. The Pave Hawk is being replaced by an updated model, HH-60W Jolly Green II. The post So Long, Pave Hawk: Air Force’s HH-60G Combat Rescue Helicopter Completes Final Flight appeared first on Air
items.body:
The Air Force’s HH-60G Pave Hawk helicopter made its final flight earlier this month.

The 129th Rescue Wing retired its last HH-60G with a final flight and ceremony on Sept. 10 at Moffett Air National Guard Base, Calif. The Pave Hawk is being replaced by an updated model, HH-60W Jolly Green II.

Tail number 27045 is the last operational HH-60G in the entire Air Force, a service spokesperson said, noting that a few remaining G-models are still in the inventory for now and will be processed out by Sept. 30, the end of the fiscal year.

Often called the “Golf,” the HH-60G entered service in 1982, was the Air Force’s combat search and rescue helicopter for more than 40 years until the updated “Whiskey” models began to supplant it in 2022. Both are UH-60 Black Hawk variants.

In addition to CSAR, the Air Force used the Pave Hawk for disaster relief, humanitarian missions, and casualty and medical evacuations. Capable of carrying eight-plus passengers, it could fly at speeds of 180 miles per hour with a range of 580 miles and be aerially refueled. It was equipped with two guns, a cargo hook that could lift up to 8,000 pounds, and folding rotor blades allowing it to be transported in cargo aircraft like the C-5M Galaxy.

The Pave Hawk played a key role in events like the military’s humanitarian response to Hurricane Katrina in 2005, operations during the Global War on Terror in Iraq and Afghanistan, and the noncombatant evacuation out of Afghanistan in 2021. Airmen were decorated with Distinguished Flying Crosses and Presidential Unit Citations for their actions in the Afghanistan evacuation, where they faced small arms fire from the ground as they evacuated scores of people ahead of the Taliban’s advance.

“When you’re flying the [Pave Hawk], you kind of become one with that machine,” Lt. Col. Benjamin Buchta, HH-60 pilot and commander of the 129th Rescue Squadron, said in a statement. “The Golf feels like home when I sit in it.”

At its peak, there were more than 100 HH-60Gs in the Air Force inventory, split among Active, Guard, and Reserve units. By 2024, units across the globe were saying their final farewells to the Golf—Kadena Air Base in Japan retired its last Golf in August 2024, Gabreski Air National Guard Base, N.Y., followed in October 2024, and Kirtland Air Force Base, N.M., and Aviano Air Base, Italy, both completed the switch in December 2024. The Air Force Reserve’s last HH-60Gs left Patrick Space Force Base, Fla., in September 2025.

The Air Force’s fiscal 2026 budget funded the final 11 Pave Hawk divestments. The Alaska Air National Guard retired its last HH-60G in July 2026, setting the stage for the California Air Guard to follow in September, just ahead of the new fiscal year on Oct. 1.

In tributes to the HH-60G, rescue units across the Air Force credited the Golf with helping them save thousands of lives over the years.

The new HH-60Ws have fully digital glass cockpits, improved hot weather/high-altitude performance, on-board self-defenses capable of defeating higher-end threats, larger cabins, and double the internal fuel capacity of the Gs. The Air Force asked for more than $200 million in the 2027 budget request for Whiskey upgrades, including for self-protection against shoulder-fired rockets and conversions to transport VIPs around Washington D.C., which will be a new mission for the HH-60.

All told, the service plans to field 102 Whiskeys, including 11 test and developmental aircraft, with the final delivery due in January 2030, according to budget documents.

items.title: Guidance: Scotland firing times
items.summary: Firing times for ranges in Scotland including Barry Buddon, Kirkcudbright, Garelochhead, Tain, Cape Wrath, Fort George, Blackdog, Castlelaw Ranges and Dreghorn
items.body:
As seen in the Security Defence Review, the Army are at heightened readiness due to a new era of threat. This has placed greater demands on the Defence Training Estate across the UK, which is being used for training more regularly and at shorter notice.

As such, the firing time notifications published on Gov.UK have been standardised to show the daily timings for when live-firing is permitted on the UK DTE. This is a change from the previous method of showing when training bookings had been made in advance.

This to ensure safety of all users, as it is not possible to change Gov.UK notifications at short notice. Broadly, the only guaranteed safe times for access are before or after the firing times provided on this page, however there may be exceptional circumstances where extensions have been requested.

If you wish to use the DTE for recreation, please always refer to onsite safety warning signals to understand if the site is safe to access before doing so.

Danger - When warning signals are displayed, regardless of the timings, do not cross the range boundary.

Warning signals are red flags by day and red lamps by night; range boundaries are marked by red and white poles.

Red flags and red lamps indicate that live firing is taking place within the range boundaries.

Do not enter the danger area when in use, this could result in loss of life.

Do not touch any military debris, it may be dangerous. Please note the location and inform a Training Safety Officer (TSO) via 07717542336 or the police.

items.title: Grave of Guilford soldier missing since 1918 identified
items.summary: A rededication service for Second Lieutenant (2nd Lt) Frank Fleming, from Guildford, was organised by the UK MOD’s ‘War Detectives’ in Belgium
items.body:
The previously un-named grave of an officer from Guildford, Surrey, who served with the Seaforth Highlanders been identified and rededicated in his name 108 years after his death on 22 September 2026.

A rededication service for 2nd Lt Frank Fleming was organised by the UK MOD ’s ‘War Detectives’ at CWGC Voormezeele Enclosure No. 3, Belgium. The service was supported by soldiers from 4th Battalion The Royal Regiment of Scotland.

JCCC Caseworker, Nicola Nash, said:

More than 100 years after his death, it was an honour to be there today to pay tribute to Frank’s bravery and sacrifice.

Frank Fleming was one of three sons of Alexander and Mary Fleming, and all three would ultimately lose their lives during World War 1.

Born in Guildford, Surrey, on 15 October 1894, Frank grew up on his family’s farm before moving to London to work as a market clerk. He later joined the Army and was commissioned into the Seaforth Highlanders.

During the German Spring Offensive in April 1918, 2nd Lt Fleming was attached to the 7th Battalion and took part in fierce fighting near Hollebeke, Belgium. While leading his men in an attack against German positions on 11 April, he was seriously wounded. Displaying remarkable courage and selflessness, he ordered his men to withdraw to safety and refused to let stretcher-bearers risk their lives attempting to rescue him. Unable to be recovered, he was later listed as missing and was commemorated on the Tyne Cot Memorial.

Subsequent research submitted by a member of the public has now shown that 2Lt Fleming was actually buried in the Hollebeke area of Belgium and moved to Voormezeele Enclosure No. 3 after the war.

His headstone, replaced by Commonwealth War Graves Commission, now carries his name and the service today has commemorated his loss.

Catherine Nell, Identifications Manager at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, said:

It has been a privilege for the Commonwealth War Graves Commission to be involved in Second Lieutenant Frank Fleming’s identification. We shall continue to care for his grave, alongside his comrades, in perpetuity.

items.title: Grave of Angus soldier missing since 1918 identified in Belgium
items.summary: A rededication service for Private George Pert from Ferryden was organised by the UK MOD’s ‘War Detectives’ at CWGC Harlebeke New British Cemetery, Belgium
items.body:
The previously un-named grave of a soldier from Ferryden, Angus, who served with the Seaforth Highlanders been identified and rededicated in his name 108 years after his death on 22 September 2026.

A rededication service for Private George Pert was organised by the UK MOD ’s ‘War Detectives’ at CWGC Harlebeke New British Cemetery, Belgium.

JCCC Caseworker, Nicola Nash, said:

From a fishing village on the banks of the River Esk to the battlefields of Belgium, George Pert’s journey reflects the sacrifices made by ordinary people during the World War One. It was an honour to be there to pay tribute to his life and service.

Private Pert grew up in Ferryden, a traditional fishing village on the bank of the River Esk, before joining the Seaforth Highlanders.

Just a month before the end of the war the Western Front saw a massive and rapid Allied advance that forced the German army into continuous retreat. It was on the 20 October 1918, during intense fighting around Harlebeke, that Private Pert lost his life.

His body was never recovered, and he was officially recorded as missing. However, subsequent research submitted by a member of the public has shown that Private Pert was buried east of Harlebeke and moved to Harlebeke New British Cemetery after the war.

The service was supported by serving soldiers from The Royal Regiment of Scotland. Pert’s headstone, replaced by Commonwealth War Graves Commission ( CWGC ), now carries his name and today’s service commemorated his loss.

Polly Brewster, Commemorations Case Officer at CWGC , said:

More than one hundred years after he made the ultimate sacrifice, CWGC are honoured to have supported the identification of Private George Pert’s final resting place. The personal inscription chosen by his family, “Gone too soon, but not forgotten,” serves as a moving tribute to the profound loss experienced by his loved ones. His rededication service today reaffirms the Commission’s enduring commitment to preserving the memory of all those who fell during the two World Wars.

items.title: With Denmark, Saildrone logs first flag registration for naval surveillance drone
items.author: Jaroslaw Adamowski
items.summary: U.S. naval drone maker Saildrone seeks to expand its footprint in Europe, with Denmark a key customer in the contested Baltic and North seas.
items.body:
WARSAW, Poland — U.S. company Saildrone has announced that the first four Voyager unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) have been registered under the Danish flag, marking the first time the producer’s vehicle operate under a national flag.

The development comes as Saildrone is working with partners in the Netherlands, Norway and Poland to ramp up its USV production for European customers, including militaries.

Kim Løye Sørensen, the European head of business development at Saildrone Denmark, the company’s subsidiary that manages its operations in Europe, told Defense News the firm is observing a rising demand for surface drones across the continent, and is in talks with a number of navies.

“We’ve had a collaboration with the Danish Navy where we had four of our Voyager platforms … in operation for the Danish Navy for a six-month period,” Sørensen said. “Now the Danish Navy and the Danish government are in the process of creating a new contract to have more Saildrones within the Danish Armed Forces. But in the near future we also see our drones operating in different European countries in the northern part of Europe.”

Due to Denmark’s location between the Baltic Sea and the North Sea, the Royal Danish Navy plays a strategic role in monitoring and safeguarding maritime traffic through the Danish Straits, a gateway between the two seas.

The 33-foot Voyager is designed for coastal surveillance and nearshore mapping missions, performing continuous maritime intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), seafloor characterization, as well as real-time domain awareness, according to data from Saildrone. Powered by an electric motor and enabled with a mapping speed of 5 knots, the USV can operate for 100 days between service stops.

Voyager USVs can perform “maritime domain awareness and the ISR for a long period of time. More than three months out in station and being out there without doing anything, just being a forwarding sensor providing the data,” Sørensen said.

In addition to the Voyager, Explorer and Surveyor platforms, Saildrone is also developing a new product, Spectre, a 170-foot USV that will join the portfolio as its largest and fastest platform that will carry weapons.

“With our Spectre platform, there will be kinetic effectors,” Sørensen said. “It’s a container-based solution. You could either have two 40-foot containers or five 20-foot containers of various payloads, including kinetics on that platform. That will be built in 2027.”

Jaroslaw Adamowski is the Poland correspondent for Defense News.

items.title: Defence spending with Scottish industry rises above £2.5 billion
items.summary: Record breaking investment is fuelling reindustrialisation across Scotland
items.body:
Government investment in Scottish defence sector rose by 13% in real terms to £2.53 billion in 2025/26, marking the highest level of industry investment since records began.

Substantial investment translates to £460 for every person living in Scotland up from £390 the previous year.

Part of Government’s work to rebuild the nation’s defence industrial base, boosting defence readiness and the reindustrialisation of Britain.

Communities across Scotland are feeling the benefit of the government’s drive to strengthen Britain’s defence industrial base, new figures reveal .

In a significant boost to the Scottish economy, the figures, which cover the 2025/26 financial year, show a 13% increase in real terms spending, taking the total to £2.53 billion.

As the government accelerates efforts to reindustrialise Britain and strengthen deterrence, there has been a significant boost in investment in the electronics sector by 33%, ensuring UK industry can deliver at scale the modern capability and resilience the armed forces depend on.

The figures demonstrate how the government is placing the defence industrial base at the centre of national renewal, with rising investment generating jobs and opportunities in towns and cities across the UK, lifting living standards and increasing household incomes.

Defence Secretary, Wes Streeting MP, said:

We cannot strengthen our deterrence without a strong, sovereign defence industry here at home, and Scotland is at the heart of that. That’s why we are unashamedly backing British, using the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the Cold War to back jobs and skills in Scotland to build the capability and technology we need to keep us safe in a more dangerous world.

We cannot strengthen our deterrence without a strong, sovereign defence industry here at home, and Scotland is at the heart of that.

That’s why we are unashamedly backing British, using the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the Cold War to back jobs and skills in Scotland to build the capability and technology we need to keep us safe in a more dangerous world.

Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander said:

The UK Government is delivering a defence dividend for Scotland. Scotland’s defence sector is a powerhouse of innovation and expertise and a key driver for economic growth. With Ministry of Defence annual investment in Scottish industry increasing to £2.53 billion we are backing businesses to grow, supporting the creation of good jobs, driving reindustrialisation and building a stronger economy that creates opportunity. From naval shipbuilding on the Clyde and at Rosyth, to our nuclear deterrent and submarine support at Faslane, to our world-leading strengths in cyber, space, advanced radar and electronic warfare, Ministry of Defence investment is directly supporting 12,200 jobs in Scotland and opening exciting career pathways for young Scots.

The figures mark a significant increase on the previous year, representing the highest level of Scottish industry investment since records began. This significant spending equates to £460 for every person in Scotland, up from £390 the year before.

The Ministry of Defence maintains a substantial footprint in Scotland, supporting 12,200 jobs . Scotland is home to a significant defence industrial base, with major employers including BAE Systems, Babcock International and Rolls-Royce, alongside key military hubs HMNB Clyde and RAF Lossiemouth.

items.title: Report: CIA warned Europe of Russian drone attack from vessels in the Mediterranean
items.author: Linus Höller
items.summary: The CIA reportedly warned European nations of a suspected Russian plot to launch explosive drones from aboard commercial vessels in the Mediterranean.
items.body:
VIENNA — The CIA has warned European countries of a suspected Russian plot to launch Gerbera-type drones from aboard commercial vessels in the Mediterranean, a new report says.

Major Spanish daily El Mundo published the article, which was based on testimony from an anonymous Lithuanian intelligence source, late Wednesday local time.

According to the paper, the CIA had assessed that Spain, France or Italy may be the targets of these attacks, with drones launching from international waters in the Mediterranean and traveling to the coastal countries over the course of an hour or two.

The Gerbera drone was selected because of its small size – it has a wingspan of just 2.5 meters – which allows it to be concealed easily, El Mundo wrote. The drones have a maximum range of 600 kilometers, depending on load and environmental conditions, and carry a relatively small warhead that would be effective at starting a fire, destroying exposed infrastructure components or causing political and economic turmoil.

The drones were to be transported hidden in containers, which was described as being “not difficult at all,” before being catapult-launched for their attack missions on the Western Mediterranean NATO members, according to El Mundo’s sourcing.

Lithuania and other European countries were reportedly made aware of this threat shortly after the CIA director made an unannounced and secretive visit to Moscow aboard a U.S. military plane on Aug. 25.

According to El Mundo, an key CIA report was rumored to be circulating in European leadership circles in mid-September, coinciding with French President Emmanuel Macron’s decision to convene the Defense Council on Sept. 16 and then summon all party leaders and the 2027 presidential candidates to the Élysée Palace two days later.

The El Mundo report has not been independently corroborated.

The perceived threat of Russian kinetic action has increased significantly across European capitals this year, owing to heightened sabotage and hybrid warfare activity generally attributed to Moscow. Airspace violations by Russian drones along NATO’s eastern flank have become increasingly commonplace, leading to several instances of the alliance’s fighter jets shooting down intruding unmanned aerial vehicles.

A year ago, 19 unarmed Russian drones entered Polish airspace, the largest airspace violation to date, and one that was widely assessed to have been a deliberate provocation and test of NATO’s response.

The prospect of launching from Russian merchant ships has long been suspected in European policy circles, with coastal sightings of unidentified UAVs sometimes coinciding with the presence of Russian “shadow fleet” ships. In February of this year, a Swedish Navy vessel detected and jammed a drone taking off from a Russian intelligence ship in the Öresund Strait, coinciding with a visit of the French aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle to the Scandinavian country.

A new step on the escalation ladder was reached in early August, when an explosive-laden drone was found near a Ukrainian cargo aircraft and a separate plane collided with a drone mid-air at Germany’s Leipzig airport, a key freight hub in the NATO country. After a month-long investigation, German authorities officially attributed the attack to Russia.

On Sept. 19, the major pro-Russian Telegram channel Rybar published a map titled “Russian medicine against French arrogance,” suggesting supplying Algeria with Geran-5 drones to strike French aeronautical factories, military bases, nuclear plants and petrochemical sites, El Mundo reported.

Even non-NATO, landlocked European countries are taking note and stepping up their preparedness. The Austrian military has launched a “large exercise” to practice counter-drone measures and air defense, Austrian public media reported on Thursday. The drill will involve 300 soldiers spread across several townships in eastern Austria, as well as Mistral ground-to-air missiles, 35-millimeter cannons and electronic warfare measures.

Linus Höller is Defense News' Europe correspondent and OSINT investigator. He reports on the arms deals, sanctions, and geopolitics shaping Europe and the world. He holds master’s degrees in WMD nonproliferation, terrorism studies, and international relations, and works in four languages: English, German, Russian, and Spanish.

items.title: Risk Factors Measured Around Age 60 as Predictors of Dementia Around Age 80 in the U.S.
items.author: Susann Rohwedder
items.summary: We estimated the probability of dementia at age 80 as a function of risk factors measured at age 60, using a recently developed and validated probabilistic dementia measure and longitudinal regression models.
items.body:
ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 24, 2026Published in: AJE Advances: Research in Epidemiology, uuag036 (2026). DOI: 10.1093/ajeadv/uuag036

The number of older adults living with dementia in the United States and worldwide continues to rise. Identifying elevated dementia risk decades before potential onset can help individuals prepare and enable healthcare providers and policymakers to target resources that may delay onset or mitigate consequences. Using nationally representative data from the U.S. Health and Retirement Study (1992-2016), we estimated the probability of dementia at around age 80 as a function of 110 risk factors measured at around age 60, using a recently developed and validated probabilistic dementia measure and longitudinal regression models. Poor physical health, low cognitive ability, fewer than 12 years of education, and greater functional limitations at around age 60 were the strongest predictors of dementia at age 80. Additional predictors included being born in the Southeastern U.S., lacking private health insurance, non-veteran status, having poor vision or hearing, limited work history, disability, diabetes, body mass index ≥ 35, prior stroke, and both alcohol abstention and heavy drinking. Several predictors, such as geographic origin, veteran status, and work history, have received limited attention in prior prediction research. Future research should examine whether these candidate predictors represent causal risk factors rather than simply associations.

items.title: Estimating the Cost of Early Colleges
items.author: Brian Phillips
items.summary: In this paper, we assess the costs of the early college model in North Carolina relative to costs for typical high school education.
items.body:
Three Complementary Approaches

ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 24, 2026Published in: American Journal of Evaluation (2026). DOI: 10.1177/10982140261479706

Early college high schools offer students many dual enrollment courses and the opportunity to earn an associate degree while in high school. In this paper, we assess the costs of the early college model in North Carolina relative to costs for typical high school education. We use three complementary approaches: one using administrative expenditure data from high schools and colleges across the state, one using the ingredients method based on in-depth subject matter expert interviews in five case study districts, and a third “hybrid” approach combining the two methods. Our findings suggest that educating an early college student incurs higher relative costs in high school that are offset by lower costs to a college degree for students who eventually complete a postsecondary credential. However, excess credit attainment attenuates the postsecondary savings. We discuss the implications of these findings for implementation of the early college model and for cost study methodologies.
