items.title: Disconnection Among American Youth
items.author: Stephanie Bonds
items.summary: Periods of disconnection (not engaged in education, training, or work) are costly for young people and for society. This paper presents findings from a survey of 349 young adults aged 18 to 22 to inform programs designed for this at-risk population.
items.body:
Evidence on Its Duration and Impact on Well-Being

Expert InsightsPublished Sep 24, 2026

Periods of disconnection (not engaged in education, training, or work) are costly for young people and for society. Designing programs to serve the one in every three young adults aged 18 to 22 who experiences disconnection requires a better understanding of when and how disconnection occurs. This paper presents survey results of 349 young adults to inform such programs and show how disconnection relates to social interaction and mental health.

One in three young Americans experiences disconnection after high school—and for many, it lasts at least six months.

After high school, many young people hit stretches of time when they’re not engaged in school, training, or work. These periods—called disconnection—are costly for young people and for society. But relatively little is known about how long disconnection typically lasts or how it shapes young people’s broader well-being.

RAND researchers used survey data from the American Youth Panel to trace patterns of disconnection among 18- to 22-year-olds, identify who is most likely to experience the longest spells, and examine how disconnection relates to social interaction and mental health.

Nearly one in four young adults reported disconnection lasting at least six months; about 11 percent reported spells of a year or more.

Nearly one in four disconnected young men reported that their mental health was “not good” every day of the prior month.

About two-thirds of young men experiencing disconnection reported no in-person time with friends in the prior week—a stark contrast to their peers who had never been disconnected.

For disconnected young men especially, the findings suggest that education and employment programs alone may miss critical needs around social isolation and well-being.

items.title: Air Force to Cut Civilian Jobs from China-Focused Research Center
items.author: Chris Gordon
items.summary: The Air Force is slashing all civilian positions at its premier research institute for Chinese military aviation, prompting concern among experts who say it will dilute the service’s focus on the Pentagon’s most significant long-term adversary. The post Air Force to Cut Civilian Jobs from China-Focused Research Center appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
The Air Force is slashing all civilian positions at its premier research institute for Chinese military aviation, prompting concern among experts who say it will dilute the service’s focus on the Pentagon’s most significant long-term adversary.

“We are disappointed to have to announce that Air University has decided to close the China Aerospace Studies Institute,” Brendan Mulvaney, the institute’s director, wrote in a message released Sept. 22.

The China Aerospace Studies Institute has been staffed primarily by civilian scholars and analysts who work for Air University, which is part of Air Education and Training Command. For years, they have been preparing reports on the Chinese military, translating Chinese military doctrine, and contributing to what is widely considered to be the largest open-source repository of information on the People’s Liberation Army’s military aviation, space, cyber, and missile forces.

An Air Force spokesperson told Air & Space Forces Magazine that the institute “is not closing” and said its mission of analyzing developments in Chinese airpower will continue—but acknowledged that its eight civilian positions have been targeted for downsizing and did not explain in detail how the institute would continue once the staff in those positions find new jobs. Four military personnel currently work for CASI, including two military fellows, and one uninformed position remains unfilled.

“Air University continues to evaluate the alignment of the CASI mission to best support DAF priorities,” the spokesperson said. “The mission will continue using assigned military personnel and civilian personnel to execute priorities outlined in their charter.”

Mulvaney, in his update, said that as of Oct. 1, the start of the new fiscal year, all civilian positions at the research center will be considered “unfunded,” though the positions still exist—for now. “CASI has commitments that it has made and will honor, to the best of our ability, through at least March of 2027,” he wrote.

“Unless we find a new home within the Department for the whole CASI team, I expect people to find other jobs and move on,” Mulvaney added. “Once all of the civilians eventually depart, CASI will close.”

The Air Force spokesperson did not detail how CASI could be restructured or how its expertise and workflow would be preserved.

The announcement came a day before Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington D.C., to meet with President Donald Trump, though Air & Space Forces Magazine understands CASI’s status has been on shaky ground for months.

No changes have been announced to similar institutions run by the Navy and Army. The U.S. Naval War College’s China Maritime Studies Institute and the U.S. Army War College’s China Landpower Studies Center will continue their work.

Experts say the open-source nature of CASI’s work enabled Congress and much of the public to get a better understanding of the Air Force’s primary long-term challenger.

China’s military advances have driven much of the Air Force’s thinking on its future force design and justification for new platforms such as the B-21 Raider stealth bomber, the F-47 Next-Generation Air Dominance fighter, and Collaborative Combat Aircraft. Service leaders said the decision to field those programs was influenced by the need to counter China in the Pacific.

But despite the service’s stated focus on China, the future of the center was impacted by the Department of the Air Force’s push to cut civilian jobs. Air University is prioritizing funding for more traditional civilian teaching positions for professional military education, people familiar with the matter told Air & Space Forces Magazine.

One China expert said this move could hurt the Air Force’s ability to explain its funding needs on Capitol Hill.

“I think the Air Force probably undervalues open-source intelligence and underappreciates this type of scholarly research on the People’s Liberation Army,” said J. Michael Dahm, a senior fellow for aerospace and China studies at AFA’s Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies. “Leaders seem to think classified information is somehow more valid than something gleaned from open-source. But the focus on the classified record undermines the Air Force’s ability to tell its story, especially on Capitol Hill and to the American people.”

“Having unclassified, open-source intelligence about the Air Force’s pacing challenge helps tell that story,” Dahm added. “Getting rid of CASI would be a self-inflicted wound that exacerbates a long-standing Air Force problem.”

Dahm, a former intelligence community professional who served as the Senior Naval Intelligence Officer for China at the Office of Naval Intelligence and the assistant U.S. Naval Attaché in Beijing, said institutions such as CASI have filled a gap in U.S. research into the opposing militaries.

“You can make the argument that collecting and analyzing Chinese-language open-source information should be a mission for the U.S. intelligence community. But the IC is consumed with analyzing and processing a torrent of classified information,” Dahm said. “The researchers at CASI are a force multiplier that provide the intelligence community with valuable context, often pointing them toward issues they might otherwise miss.”

China has put a “much greater emphasis on open-source intelligence than we do in the U.S.,” he noted.

“China’s military has closed many of its gaps with the West by digesting and analyzing the volumes of open-source information we put out there,” Dahm said. “They institutionalized open-source scientific and technical research in the 1950s, and they have continued to harvest the volumes of scientific journal articles, trade brochures, operator manuals, and anything else they can lay their hands on to develop countermeasures against our technology and fuel their own military development. They are also downloading and translating U.S. military doctrine, safety manuals, incident reports, and lessons learned to inform their tactics and procedures.

“Eliminating CASI would be divesting the Air Force of its only institutional counterweights to China’s open-source intelligence machine.”

items.title: Army awards Palantir $48.1M to modernize ammo management
items.author: Daniel Terrill
items.summary: The tech company has built AI software designed to process data for targeting and decision-making, and now, managing ammo.
items.body:
The U.S. Army awarded a subsidiary of Palantir Technologies a $48.1 million contract to develop software designed to improve how the service tracks and manages ammunition.

According to last week’s announcement, the new software will streamline ammunition management by consolidating nine separate legacy platforms.

“Ultimately, this system is one element to modernize overall ammunition systems, retire legacy systems and improve audit readiness,” the service said.

The software will use “commercial low-code, no-code technology” and give soldiers the ability to track munitions throughout their lifecycle, the Army said.

That includes everything from “planning, production, and procurement, to storage, surveillance, distribution, expenditure, and final disposition,” according to the service.

The contract comes as the Army works to address longstanding problems with its ammunition management systems.

In March, the Army’s Line of Departure journal published an article describing shortcomings in the service’s existing ammunition processes, including inaccurate forecasting and disconnected digital systems.

According to the article, ammunition forecasts at lower levels often rely on assumptions and historical trends rather than actual demand tied to training cycles.

The legacy systems also operate independently, meaning changes to training schedules may not be reflected across the ammunition management process in real time.

“The result is an accountability model failing to meet the operational tempo or digital expectations of the modern force,” the article says.

Over the past few years alone, Palantir has led or contributed to several programs for integrating artificial intelligence into workflows and decision-making, including Army Vantage, Next Generation Command and Control and the Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node.

However, Palantir might be best known for the Maven Smart System, or MSS, an AI-enabled system used by all branches of service that’s designed to present intelligence data to enhance operational decisions like targeting options.

For the ammo management software, the Army said Palantir beat out the competition through a three-phase selection process over a six-week period.

“Vendors were evaluated on key capabilities including integrating data from disparate legacy systems, the ability to provide robust planning and forecast models, and support tactical users in disconnected or low-bandwidth environments,” the Army said.

Under the agreement, Palantir will develop the new software over the next 12 months and provide support for an additional five years.

Daniel Terrill is a contributor to Military Times. He’s been reporting on military issues, the gun industry, and the outdoors for nearly two decades. Although writing is his passion, he’s been a Marine, police officer, and, perhaps the most dangerous job of his career, a substitute teacher.

items.title: Air Force Experiment Looks at How Humans and AI Can Team Up for Command and Control
items.author: Todd South
items.summary: A recent two-week experiment tested how Airmen and Guardians can team with machines and artificial intelligence to enhance command and control in complex scenarios—with researchers measuring everything from the heart rate of participants to the quality of their decision-making. The post Air Force Experiment Looks at How Humans and AI Can Team Up for Command and Control appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
A recent two-week experiment tested how Airmen and Guardians can team with machines and artificial intelligence to enhance command and control in complex scenarios—with researchers measuring everything from participants’ heart rates to the quality of their decision-making.

A Space Force crew led an integrated operational crew with Air Force battle managers and industry software developers at USAF’s Shadow Operations Center-Nellis for the July test. It is the fourth iteration of the Decision Advantage Sprint for Human-Machine Teaming series and the first time a Guardian led the C2 team.

That team worked through different scenarios for the July 13-24 experiment, validating software and technical capabilities to support operators across the Air Force and Space Force, according to a service release.

The Air Force Research Laboratory and its 711th Human Performance Wing were on hand to assess the effects of the new AI tools. The wing analyzed the speed, quality, and decision accuracy of a human-machine team versus a human-only team. They also measured heart rate, real-time cognitive workload, and tracked gaze fixation patterns to better understand human reaction and response.

“This biometric and behavioral analysis mapped visual attention distribution, evaluated cognitive workload thresholds, and analyzed workflow dynamics during high-tempo operational scenarios,” Amanda Szczublewski, AFRL’s technology transition office acquisition program management specialist, told Air & Space Forces Magazine.

The 805th Combat Training Squadron at Nellis Air Force Base, Nev., hosted the experiment, and participants got a taste of scenarios operators would face in the heat of battle.

“This isn’t a scenario from a video game. It is one crafted to challenge operators and engineers alike,” said Air Force Lt. Col. Wesley Schultz, squadron commander. “We reflect the real-world challenges of geography and logistics, and even real-time changes in the rules of engagement, because that reflects the reality of modern warfare.”

The Space Force portion of the DASH specifically used existing operational data such as simulated space domain awareness and electromagnetic warfare parameters, Space Force Col. Teina Stallings-Lilly, deputy director of operations integration for the Advanced Battle Management System Cross Functional Team, told Air & Space Forces Magazine in an email.

“This enabled the artificial intelligence decision aids to evaluate how space asset positioning and readiness directly impact theater-wide courses of action in real time,” Stallings-Lilly said.

Air Force Col. John Ohlund, ABMS-CFT Director, said the experiment focused on “game theory” to test battle managers.

“We are moving beyond simple, reactive scenarios and presenting our warfighters with complex, ambiguous problems where they must be proactive, weigh tradeoffs, and make decisions when there is no perfect answer,” Ohlund said. “This approach is essential for developing the cognitive superiority our joint force needs to out-think and outmaneuver a peer adversary in a high-end conflict.”

The 805th, also known as the Shadow Operations Center-Nellis, made sure the experiment “generates authentic, high-tempo combat data,” Schultz said.

“By immersing operators in complex, game-theory-driven scenarios, our battle lab allows the AFRL and 711th teams to capture both real-time system performance metrics and objective warfighter feedback, producing rigorous, scientifically validated insights into human-machine teaming,” Schultz said.

The combined human and machine data gave observers a clearer picture of the demands of air and space battle management at a high operational tempo.

“Our data and direct observations confirm that the fundamental cognitive challenges for a battle manager are domain-agnostic,” Dr. Elizabeth Frost, AFRL’s DASH lead, said in the release. “Both Airmen and Guardians are tasked with synthesizing vast amounts of complex data and prioritizing actions under intense time pressure. This event demonstrated that a well-designed human-machine team can effectively free up an operator’s cognitive resources.”

The analysis will help quantify cognitive workload mitigation, validate trust in autonomy, and inform future interface and architecture training requirements for battle management systems, Szczublewski said.

Government assessors evaluated team effectiveness using key metrics:

- Number, Speed, and Quality of Decisions: Assessing how effectively the system supported risk-versus-opportunity evaluations, time-critical execution, and prioritizing mission tasks aligned with the commander’s intent.

- Contribution to Human-Machine Team Performance: The primary objective was to help the human operator make higher-quality, faster decisions by synthesizing complex data and delivering actionable posturing directions and options for the operator to select and execute.

The DASH experiment isn’t just about generating research insights. The ShOC-N also serves as an operational proving ground for new software, hardware, and tactics, techniques, and procedures to evaluate before deploying across the force, Schultz said.

For operators, having quick access to these software tools proved their worth quickly.

“These sprints represent the biggest shift in battle management in my career,” Schultz said. “We’re taking what technology allows for and shaping it in a way that magnifies the skills and training of warfighters to ensure we maintain decisive advantage in conflict.”

The Air Force has conducted four DASH events since March 2025 and a single Multi-Decision Advantage Sprint for Human-Machine Teaming, or MASH, in May, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported.

“Every event in the DASH and MASH series is uniquely designed around specific operational objectives. Rather than simply making a scenario ‘harder,’ the 805th scenario design team crafts tailored, high-fidelity threat environments based on targeted operational requirements,” said Schultz, the 805th’s commander.

The squadron’s domain experts inject operational complexities, such as contested logistics, dynamic geography, and shifting rules of engagement, Schultz said.

Then, the modeling and simulation team translates the variables into digital representations and ensures the software tools are evaluated against authentic combat conditions rather than idealized laboratory settings, he said.

The MASH experiment launched a government-owned software orchestrator, and the July DASH event validated the “plug-and-play” software design by linking the system with various software solutions. The government’s orchestrator interface let users test multiple, competing industry applications on the system.

The orchestrator is a “tool-agnostic decision engine” that determines which vendor decision function to call on based on the state of the current operational environment, Szczublewski said.

The interface is designed to work with any vendor’s decision tool and allows a mix-and-match of vendor solutions, giving users diverse options to deal with posture and sustainment asset problems, she said.

“Our goal is to get the most advanced capabilities into the hands of the joint force at speed,” Air Force Lt. Col. Corey Ellsworth, ABMS-CFT integration lead, told Air & Space Forces Magazine. “This entire framework was built from the ground up to ensure that once a capability is validated here, we can securely and efficiently transition it to the classified networks where our Airmen and Guardians will actually use it in a high-end fight.”

Officials declined to disclose the industry participants, citing operational security risks.

“By executing these sprints in an unclassified environment, the experiment demonstrated how the department can leverage rapid industry innovation within a modular, microservices-based architecture,” an Air Force spokesperson told Air & Space Forces Magazine in an email.
items.zhFull:
最近一项为期两周的实验测试了空军人员和太空军人员如何与机器和人工智能协同，以增强复杂场景中的指挥与控制——研究人员测量了从参与者心率到决策质量等各项指标。

在7月的测试中，一个太空军团队在美国空军的Shadow Operations Center-Nellis领导了一支由空军战斗管理人员和行业软件开发人员组成的综合作战团队。这是“人机编组决策优势冲刺”（Decision Advantage Sprint for Human-Machine Teaming）系列的第四次迭代，也是首次由太空军人员领导C2团队。

据军方发布的消息，该团队在7月13日至24日的实验中演练了不同场景，验证了支持空军和太空军操作人员的软件与技术能力。

美国空军研究实验室及其第711人体效能联队到场评估了新AI工具的效果。该联队分析了人机团队与纯人工团队的速度、质量和决策准确性。他们还测量了心率、实时认知负荷，并追踪注视固视模式，以更好地理解人的反应与响应。

“这种生物特征与行为分析绘制了视觉注意力分布，评估了认知负荷阈值，并分析了高节奏作战场景中的工作流程动态，”AFRL技术转化办公室采办项目管理专家阿曼达·什丘布莱夫斯基（Amanda Szczublewski）对《Air & Space Forces Magazine》表示。

位于内华达州内利斯空军基地的第805战斗训练中队主办了此次实验，参与者体验了操作人员在激烈战斗中可能面对的场景。

“这不是电子游戏中的场景。它是为同时挑战操作人员和工程师而精心设计的场景，”空军 Lt. Col. 韦斯利·舒尔茨（Wesley Schultz），中队指挥官，说。“我们反映了地理和后勤方面的现实挑战，甚至还有交战规则的实时变化，因为这反映了现代战争的现实。”

DASH的太空军部分特别使用了现有作战数据，例如模拟的太空域感知和电磁战参数，太空军 Col. 蒂娜·斯托林斯-莉莉（Teina Stallings-Lilly），先进作战管理系统跨职能团队作战集成副主任，在电子邮件中对《Air & Space Forces Magazine》表示。

“这使人工智能决策辅助工具能够实时评估太空资产定位与战备如何直接影响战区范围内的行动方案，”斯托林斯-莉莉（Stallings-Lilly）说。

空军 Col. 约翰·奥伦德（John Ohlund），ABMS-CFT 主任，表示该实验侧重于“博弈论”，以测试战斗管理人员。

“我们正在超越简单、反应式的场景，向作战人员提出复杂、模糊的问题，他们必须主动作为、权衡取舍，并在没有完美答案时做出决策，”奥伦德说。“这种方法对于培养联合部队所需的认知优势至关重要，以便在高端冲突中智胜并机动超越同等对手。”

第805部队，亦称内利斯影子作战中心，确保该实验“生成真实、高节奏的战斗数据，”舒尔茨（Schultz）说。

“通过让操作人员沉浸在复杂的、博弈论驱动的场景中，我们的战斗实验室使 AFRL 和 711th 团队能够同时采集实时系统性能指标和客观的作战人员反馈，从而产生关于人机协同的严谨、经科学验证的洞见，”舒尔茨说。

将人的数据与机器数据结合起来，使观察者更清楚地了解高作战节奏下空天战斗管理的需求。

“我们的数据和直接观察证实，战斗管理人员面临的根本认知挑战与领域无关，”AFRL 的 DASH 负责人伊丽莎白·弗罗斯特（Elizabeth Frost）博士在新闻稿中表示。“空军人员和太空军人员都肩负着综合大量复杂数据并在巨大时间压力下确定行动优先级的任务。这次活动表明，设计良好的人机团队能够有效释放操作人员的认知资源。”

什丘布莱夫斯基（Szczublewski）说，该分析将有助于量化认知工作负荷的缓解、验证对自主系统的信任，并为战斗管理系统的未来界面与架构训练需求提供依据。

政府评估人员使用关键指标评估团队效能：

- 决策数量、速度与质量：评估该系统在多大程度上有效支持风险与机遇权衡评估、时间紧迫的执行，以及按照指挥官意图确定任务优先级。

- 对人机团队绩效的贡献：主要目标是帮助人类操作员做出更高质量、更快速的决策，方式是综合复杂数据，并提供可操作的态势调整方向与选项，供操作员选择和执行。

DASH实验不仅仅是产生研究见解。舒尔茨（Schultz）说，ShOC-N还充当新的软件、硬件以及战术、技术和程序的作战试验场，以便在全军部署前进行评估。

对于操作员来说，能够快速使用这些软件工具很快就证明了其价值。

“这些冲刺活动代表了我职业生涯中作战管理的最大转变，”舒尔茨说。“我们正在利用技术所能实现的能力，并以其放大作战人员技能与训练的方式加以塑造，以确保我们在冲突中保持决定性优势。”

据《空军与太空军杂志》报道，自2025年3月以来，空军已举行四次DASH活动，并于5月举行了一次人机团队多决策优势冲刺（MASH）。

“DASH和MASH系列中的每一次活动都围绕特定作战目标进行独特设计。第805中队想定设计团队不是简单地让想定变得‘更难’，而是根据有针对性的作战需求，精心构建量身定制的高保真威胁环境，”第805中队指挥官舒尔茨说。

舒尔茨（Schultz）表示，该中队领域专家引入了作战复杂性，如受争夺的后勤、动态地理环境以及不断变化的交战规则。

他说，随后，建模与仿真团队将这些变量转化为数字表示，并确保软件工具在真实作战条件下、而非理想化实验室环境中接受评估。

MASH 实验启动了一个政府所有的软件编排器，而 7 月的 DASH 活动通过将该系统与多种软件解决方案连接，验证了“即插即用”软件设计。政府的编排器接口让用户能够在该系统上测试多个相互竞争的行业应用。

什丘布莱夫斯基（Szczublewski）表示，该编排器是一种“工具无关的决策引擎”，它根据当前作战环境的状态来决定调用哪家供应商的决策功能。

她说，该接口设计用于兼容任何供应商的决策工具，并允许对供应商解决方案进行混合搭配，为用户处理态势与保障资产问题提供多种选择。

“我们的目标是将最先进的能力快速交到联合部队手中，”空军 Lt. Col. 科里·埃尔斯沃思（Corey Ellsworth），ABMS-CFT 整合负责人，对《空天军杂志》表示。“整个框架从一开始就旨在确保，一旦某项能力在这里得到验证，我们就能安全、高效地将其转移到机密网络，让我们的空军人员和太空军人员在高强度战斗中实际使用它。”

官员们以作战安全风险为由，拒绝披露业界参与方。

“通过在不保密环境中执行这些冲刺，该实验展示了该部门如何在模块化、基于微服务的架构中利用快速的行业创新，”一位空军发言人在电子邮件中对《空天军杂志》表示。
zhParas: 最近一项为期两周的实验测试了空军人员和太空军人员如何与机器和人工智能协同，以增强复杂场景中的指挥与控制——研究人员测量了从参与者心率到决策质量等各项指标。

位于内华达州内利斯空军基地的第805战斗训练中队主办了此次实验，参与者体验了操作人员在激烈战斗中可能面对的场景。

空军 Col. 约翰·奥伦德（John Ohlund），ABMS-CFT 主任，表示该实验侧重于“博弈论”，以测试战斗管理人员。

将人的数据与机器数据结合起来，使观察者更清楚地了解高作战节奏下空天战斗管理的需求。
“我们的数据和直接观察证实，战斗管理人员面临的根本认知挑战与领域无关，”AFRL 的 DASH 负责人伊丽莎白·弗罗斯特（Elizabeth Frost）博士在新闻稿中表示。“空军人员和太空军人员都肩负着综合大量复杂数据并在巨大时间压力下确定行动优先级的任务。这次活动表明，设计良好的人机团队能够有效释放操作人员的认知资源。”

items.title: CCA Builders Start Revving Production Rates, as They Await 2027 Funding
items.author: Steve Losey
items.summary: General Atomics Aeronautical Systems Inc. and Anduril Industries both say they’re ready to produce Collaborative Combat Aircraft at a rapid clip and even expand that production, as they wait for a fiscal 2027 budget to fund that work. The post CCA Builders Start Revving Production Rates, as They Await 2027 Funding appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
General Atomics Aeronautical Systems Inc. and Anduril Industries both say they’re ready to produce Collaborative Combat Aircraft in volume as they wait for a fiscal 2027 budget to fund that work.

General Atomics announced earlier this week it has the capacity to produce its FQ-42A Vengeance drones at a rate of “six aircraft per month to meet USAF goals” and could make more if needed. Competitor Anduril, which started production of its FQ-44A Fury at its new Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio in March, aims to build 150 aircraft annually, its officials said last week at AFA’s Air, Space & Cyber Conference.

The Air Force’s 2027 budget request includes $996.5 million to acquire production CCAs in fiscal 2027, plus another $150 million in advance procurement funds for 2028. But USAF has not specified how many aircraft that might cover.

General Atomics spokesman C. Mark Brinkley declined to tell Air & Space Forces Magazine exactly how many FQ-42s are rolling off the company’s production line right now, but did confirm production is underway. “Some of those aircraft will become company aircraft,” he said, meaning that not all are for its Air Force customer.

Brinkley said the company’s potential production expansion could be used to answer international demand for its Gambit series of autonomous drones, which are closely related to the FQ-42.

General Atomics also said in its statement that it is self-funding FQ-42 production today as it awaits Congressional fiscal 2027 appropriations. The new fiscal year launches Oct. 1, but lawmakers failed to pass a budget for fiscal ’27, and instead passed a continuing resolution that would hold current year funding steady, but provides no new funding. The measure ensures funding through Dec. 11, 2026.

GA’s self-funding will help support the government’s procurement plans and prevent delivery delays, the company said, and building aircraft for its own fleet will help it invest in new technologies that reduce risk and increase capabilities.

The Air Force plans to use CCAs as a complement to crewed fighters in a bid to add combat capacity at a lower cost than convention fighter jets. CCAs are designed to be flown semi-autonomously, at times alongside piloted fighters like the F-22 and F-35 Lightning II, and could eventually carry out a variety of missions including air-to-air or air-to-ground strikes; intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance; or electronic warfare operations. The concept is still comparatively early in its development.

Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said Sept. 14 that USAF is aiming to field at least 500 CCAs by 2032. The Anduril and General Atomics CCAs were selected following a competition in April 2024, andboth companies won initial production contracts in June 2026.

General Atomics said a new FQ-42 was delivered to Creech Air Force Base, Nev., on Sept. 18, for test and evaluation. Creech is home to the Air Force’s Experimental Operations Unit, which has been experimenting with CCAs to develop approaches to how they might be employed in real-life operations.

Jason Levin, Anduril’s senior vice president for air dominance and strike, said Sept. 14 that his firm delivered an FQ-44 to the EOU in August. Prior to that, the YFQ-44A prototype took part in two exercises with the EOU, the first in April and the second in July.

The July exercise at Creech, Levin said, demonstrated that CCA had advanced enough for a single Air Force operator to launch and recover an aircraft on his own after just a few hours of training.

“The Air Force was operating mission autonomy by themselves, which was a first,” Levin said. “They were flying multiple times a day, operating mission autonomy without Anduril personnel—they were on-site kind of helping, but it was really the Air Force operating that.”

Levin said that during the July exercise, Fury flew in the same airspace as crewed fighters and other drones using mission autonomy, helping build Airmen’s trust that CCAs can operate in congested airspace.

The production model of the FQ-44 that will start to roll off the line next year at Arsenal-1 will be able to carry four air-to-air weapons, such as the AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile, or AMRAAM, under its wings.

The FQ-42, General Atomics said, has flown in formation with piloted F-35 Lightning II and F-15E Strike Eagle jets to prepare for future test flights, when fighter pilots will actually command the drones. The FQ-42 represents fifth-generation stealth and operates with an internal weapons bay.

General Atomics previously conducted flights of its MQ-20 Avenger drone, operating as a CCA surrogate, to demonstrate how collaborative control flights might work. The company said its aircraft, including the Vengeance, Avenger, and XQ-67A Off-Board Sensing Station, have flown both semi-autonomously and autonomously using AI pilots and under the collaborative control of human pilots flying in the F-22 Raptor and F-35.

“The CCA program’s rate of progress has been incredible,” said Mike Atwood, vice president of advanced programs at General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, in a company statement. “Every week, the Air Force is pushing forward with new and more impressive accomplishments using Vengeance. It’s amazing to think of how far this program has come in such a short amount of time.”
items.zhFull:
通用原子航空系统公司和Anduril Industries（安杜里尔工业公司）均表示，他们已做好批量生产协同作战飞机（CCA）的准备，目前正等待2027财年预算为这项工作提供资金。

通用原子公司本周早些时候宣布，其有能力以“每月6架”的速度生产FQ-42A Vengeance无人机，以满足美国空军的目标，如有需要还可生产更多。竞争对手Anduril公司于3月在俄亥俄州新建的Arsenal-1工厂启动了FQ-44A Fury的生产，其目标是每年制造150架，该公司官员上周在AFA航空、航天与网络会议上表示。

美国空军2027财年预算申请中包括9.965亿美元，用于在2027财年采购量产型CCA，另有1.5亿美元的预先采购资金用于2028年。但美国空军未具体说明这可能涵盖多少架飞机。

通用原子公司发言人C. Mark Brinkley（C·马克·布林克利）拒绝向《空军与太空军杂志》透露目前究竟有多少架FQ-42正从该公司生产线上下线，但证实生产正在进行。“其中一些飞机将成为公司自有飞机，”他说，这意味着并非所有飞机都交付给其空军客户。

Brinkley表示，该公司潜在的产能扩张可用于满足国际市场对其Gambit系列自主无人机的需求，该系列与FQ-42关系密切。

通用原子公司还在声明中表示，在等待国会2027财年拨款之际，目前正自筹资金进行FQ-42的生产。新财年于10月1日开始，但议员们未能通过2027财年预算，而是通过了一项持续决议，使本财年拨款保持稳定，但不提供任何新资金。该措施确保资金维持到2026年12月11日。

通用原子公司表示，其自筹资金将有助于支持政府的采购计划并防止交付延迟，而为自身机队制造飞机将有助于其投资于降低风险、提升能力的新技术。

美国空军计划将CCA作为有人驾驶战斗机的补充，以期以低于常规战斗机的成本增加作战能力。CCA被设计为可半自主飞行，有时与F-22和F-35 Lightning II等有人驾驶战斗机并肩飞行，最终可能执行多种任务，包括空对空或空对地打击、情报、监视与侦察，或电子战行动。该概念的发展仍相对处于早期阶段。

空军部长特洛伊·迈因克（Troy Meink）9月14日表示，美国空军的目标是到2032年至少列装500架CCA。Anduril公司和通用原子公司的CCA是在2024年4月的一场竞标后选定的，两家公司于2026年6月赢得了初始生产合同。

通用原子公司表示，一架新的FQ-42已于9月18日交付至内华达州克里奇空军基地，用于测试与评估。克里奇空军基地是美国空军实验作战单位的驻地，该单位一直在对CCA进行试验，以研究其在实际行动中的可能运用方式。

Anduril公司负责空中优势与打击业务的高级副总裁杰森·莱文（Jason Levin）9月14日表示，该公司已于8月向实验作战单位交付一架FQ-44。此前，YFQ-44A原型机与该实验作战单位一起参加了两次演习，第一次在4月，第二次在7月。

莱文说，7月在克里奇空军基地举行的演习表明，CCA已足够先进，只需数小时训练，一名空军操作员就能独自发射和回收一架飞机。

“空军自行操作任务自主系统，这是首次，”莱文说。“他们每天飞行多次，在没有Anduril公司人员的情况下操作任务自主系统——Anduril公司人员确实在现场提供了一些帮助，但实际操作的确实是空军。”

莱文说，在7月的演习中，Fury与有人驾驶战斗机和其他无人机在同一空域飞行，并使用了任务自主系统，这有助于让空军人员相信CCA能够在拥挤空域中运行。

将于明年在Arsenal-1开始下线的FQ-44量产型，将能够在机翼下携带四枚空对空武器，例如AIM-120先进中程空对空导弹（AMRAAM）。

通用原子公司表示，FQ-42已与有人驾驶的F-35 Lightning II和F-15E Strike Eagle战机编队飞行，为未来的试飞做准备；届时战斗机飞行员将实际指挥这些无人机。FQ-42具备第五代隐身能力，并采用内部武器舱。

通用原子公司此前曾让其作为CCA替代平台的MQ-20 Avenger无人机进行飞行，以展示协同控制飞行可能如何运作。该公司表示，其包括Vengeance、Avenger和XQ-67A Off-Board Sensing Station在内的飞机，已在使用AI飞行员的情况下进行半自主和自主飞行，并已在驾驶F-22 Raptor和F-35的人类飞行员的协同控制下飞行。

通用原子公司本周早些时候宣布，其有能力以“每月6架”的速度生产FQ-42A Vengeance无人机，以满足美国空军的目标，如有需要还可生产更多。竞争对手Anduril公司于3月在俄亥俄州新建的Arsenal-1工厂启动了FQ-44A Fury的生产，其目标是每年制造150架，该公司官员上周在AFA航空、航天与网络会议上表示。
美国空军2027财年预算申请中包括9.965亿美元，用于在2027财年采购量产型CCA，另有1.5亿美元的预先采购资金用于2028年。但美国空军未具体说明这可能涵盖多少架飞机。

通用原子公司还在声明中表示，在等待国会2027财年拨款之际，目前正自筹资金进行FQ-42的生产。新财年于10月1日开始，但议员们未能通过2027财年预算，而是通过了一项持续决议，使本财年拨款保持稳定，但不提供任何新资金。该措施确保资金维持到2026年12月11日。

items.title: Steam catapults? US Navy appears to be sticking with electromagnetics on carriers
items.author: Michael Peck
items.summary: Despite an August order for the U.S. Navy to return to steam catapults on its newest carriers, the service appears to be sticking with electromagnetics.
items.body:
Despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s nostalgia for old-fashioned steam catapults, the U.S. Navy appears to be sticking with electromagnetics for its newest class of aircraft carriers.

The Navy recently awarded contracts for the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System, or EMALS, which uses electrically generated magnetic fields to launch aircraft from Ford-class carriers.

Kato Engineering announced a $49.3 million contract this week to support the energy storage subsystem of EMALS. The Navy also published a sources sought notice on Wednesday, seeking vendors to supply components such as EMALS recirculation pumps.

The Navy maintains that electromagnetic catapults provide smoother acceleration, can be adjusted to launch various types of aircraft such as drones, can be reset for faster launches and require less maintenance and personnel. China, meanwhile, is equipping its new Fujian-class carriers with electromagnetic catapults.

Trump resurrected the steam catapult versus EMALS conversation in August, when he ordered the Navy to replace EMALS with the older system on the USS Doris Miller, the next Ford-class carrier under construction.

In an August memo, Trump pointed at a Navy that has suffered from “a series of shipbuilding setbacks stemming from overly complex designs and iterative design change procedures, which have resulted in cost growth, delays, and cancellations.”

The president suggested mandating that the Navy submit “a plan on the required measures to replace the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System and Advanced Weapons Elevators with steam and hydraulic systems for the construction of CVN-81 [USS Doris Miller], including timelines and resourcing requirements.”

The White House’s order baffled naval experts. The Navy has not ordered a steam catapult in 20 years, with the last order placed for the USS George H. W. Bush, commissioned in 2009 as the final Nimitz-class carrier.

Finding a manufacturer for steam catapults, and then redesigning Ford-class carriers to accept them, would likely require sweeping manufacturing overhauls at considerable expense, critics of the order said.

Despite their planned phasing out, steam catapults are a proven technology. They were developed by Britain in the 1950s to replace the hydraulic catapults of World War II-era carriers and were later copied by the U.S.

“The decision was made in April 1952 that the steam catapult would probably be the most satisfactory type for a service catapult,” noted a 1954 article in the U.S. Naval Institute magazine Proceedings. “Arrangements were made for the manufacturing rights to the British catapult. British drawings were obtained and redrawn to U. S. standards and modified to fit U.S. naval requirements.”

Manufactured for 21st century carriers, EMALS “is designed to expand the operational capability of Ford-class carriers, providing the Navy with capability for launching all current and future carrier air wing platforms – lightweight unmanned to heavy strike fighters.

The rapid evolution of unmanned aircraft, which may soon become the backbone of carrier air wings, will likely require a more sophisticated launch system. Recent contracts suggest the U.S. Navy is planning accordingly.

Michael Peck is a correspondent for Defense News and a columnist for the Center for European Policy Analysis. He holds an M.A. in political science from Rutgers University. Find him at theuncommondefense.com. His email is mikedefense1@gmail.com.

尽管美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）对老式蒸汽弹射器念念不忘，但美国海军似乎仍将在其最新一级航空母舰上坚持采用电磁弹射系统。

美国海军最近授予了电磁飞机弹射系统（EMALS）相关合同，该系统利用电力产生的磁场从福特级航母上弹射飞机。

Kato Engineering本周宣布获得一份价值4930万美元的合同，以支持EMALS的储能子系统。海军还在周三发布了一份来源征询通知，寻求供应商提供EMALS再循环泵等部件。

海军坚持认为，电磁弹射器可提供更平稳的加速，可调整以弹射无人机等各类飞机，可重置以实现更快弹射，并且所需维护和人员更少。与此同时，中国正在为其新型福建级航母配备电磁弹射器。

特朗普在8月重新引发了蒸汽弹射器与EMALS之争，当时他命令海军在正在建造的下一艘福特级航母USS Doris Miller上，用较老的系统替换EMALS。

在8月的一份备忘录中，特朗普指出，海军已遭受“一系列造船挫折，这些挫折源于过于复杂的设计和反复迭代的设计变更程序，导致成本增长、延误和取消。”

总统建议强制要求海军提交“一份关于所需措施的计划，以蒸汽和液压系统替换电磁飞机弹射系统和先进武器升降机，用于CVN-81 [USS Doris Miller]的建造，包括时间表和资源需求。”

白宫的命令令海军专家困惑不已。美国海军已有20年未订购蒸汽弹射器，最后一次订购是为USS George H. W. Bush，该舰于2009年服役，是最后一艘尼米兹级航母。

批评该命令的人士说，为蒸汽弹射器寻找制造商，然后再重新设计福特级航母以适配蒸汽弹射器，很可能需要在制造业进行全面改造，且代价高昂。

尽管按计划将被逐步淘汰，蒸汽弹射器仍是一项经过验证的技术。它由英国在20世纪50年代研发，用于取代二战时期航母上的液压弹射器，后来被美国仿制。

美国海军学会杂志《Proceedings》1954年的一篇文章指出：“1952年4月作出了决定，认为蒸汽弹射器很可能成为军用弹射器中最令人满意的一种。”“当时已就英国弹射器的制造权作出安排。美方获得了英国的图纸，按美国标准重新绘制，并加以修改以符合美国海军的要求。”

EMALS是为21世纪航母而制造的，“其设计目的是拓展福特级航母的作战能力，使海军具备弹射当前和未来所有航母航空联队平台的能力——从轻型无人机到重型打击战斗机。”

无人机正快速演进，可能很快就会成为航母航空联队的骨干力量，这很可能需要一套更为先进的弹射系统。最近的合同显示，美国海军正据此进行规划。

迈克尔·佩克（Michael Peck）是《防务新闻》的记者，也是欧洲政策分析中心的专栏作家。他拥有罗格斯大学政治学硕士学位。可在theuncommondefense.com上找到他。他的电子邮箱是mikedefense1@gmail.com。

items.title: Air Force, civilian staff dispute status of China Aerospace Studies Institute
items.author: Michael Scanlon
items.summary: CASI's director said the move will effectively end the institute, even as the service says CASI’s mission will continue.
items.body:
On Oct. 1, the Air Force will eliminate all 10 civilian positions at the China Aerospace Studies Institute, the Air University center that publishes unclassified research on the People’s Liberation Army’s air, space and missile forces. Its director said the move will effectively end the institute, even as the service says CASI’s mission will continue.

“As a part of the ongoing civilian restructure within Air Education and Training Command, civilian positions will no longer be assigned to China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI),” an Air Force spokesperson said in a statement to Defense News on Tuesday. “The CASI mission continues, with the organization leveraging assigned military service members to accomplish its objectives.”

Civilians affected by the restructuring will stay in their current positions until further notice and will be evaluated for reassignment, the spokesperson said.

CASI Director Brendan Mulvaney described the fallout differently. All of the institute’s civilian billets are being eliminated, “effectively ending CASI,” he said Tuesday. No military positions are affected, he said, noting the institute has two master sergeant billets and a deputy position that has remained unfilled for over a year.

Asked how the cut would impact the institute’s research, Mulvaney said, “All of the research has always been done by the civilian personnel.”

According to Mulvaney, the decision was made by the previous Air University commander and forwarded by AETC under a requirement to cut civilian jobs across the Department of the Air Force. The quota originated with the Air Force’s manpower and reserve affairs office, he said.

The cut “had nothing to do with CASI’s mission,” Mulvaney said, but due to the fact that the institute does not produce professional military education students, which is Air University’s primary mission.

Asked whether another organization would take on CASI’s China aerospace research, Mulvaney said, “Nothing has been identified.” It is also unknown whether CASI’s reports, translations and course materials will remain publicly available, or whether its website will remain online, he said.

The cuts became public Monday, when a note from a CASI civilian circulated on social media. The employee wrote that every CASI civilian position would be unfunded as of Oct. 1 and that the staff would become “surplus federal employees,” a federal personnel term for workers whose positions are being eliminated.

The note described CASI’s future as “uncertain,” adding that “CASI punched above its weight given our small team and budget.”

Will Yale, a Navy surface warfare officer who posted the note on X, wrote that it was “extremely unfortunate and regrettable” that the Department of the Air Force “has decided to shutter” CASI. He described the institute as one of the most prominent in its field and wrote that it had “measurably increased knowledge about the PLA” inside the U.S. government and outside it.

Andrew Erickson, a Naval War College professor and CASI associate, noted that the news is “specific to CASI only.” Mulvaney said the action does not affect the Navy’s China Maritime Studies Institute, the Army War College’s China Landpower Studies Center or the Marine Corps War College’s China Warfighting Initiative.

CASI was established in 2017 and formally chartered on June 15, 2021, by then-Chief of Staff Gen. Charles Q. Brown Jr. The charter tasked the institute with studying “everything that flies” in China, calling CASI the Air Force’s leading center for the study of China and its aerospace capabilities. It has offices at Maxwell Air Force Base, Alabama, and Fort McNair in Washington.

The institute’s research was unclassified by design, according to its charter, which directed CASI to use publicly available native-language sources and publish its findings. CASI translated PLA textbooks and doctrine, published reference primers and ran a free three-day PLA Fundamentals course that required no security clearance.

Its biennial CASI Conference, held in May at National Defense University, drew more than 250 attendees and featured the release of the fifth edition of its “PLA Aerospace Power” primer, CASI said.

In 2025, nearly 80,000 people visited CASI’s website and downloaded more than 50,000 reports, according to the institute. The site remains live and posted a new paper on Sept. 21, “From Vision to Vigilance: How Beijing’s Space-Science Roadmap Builds a Real-Time Kill Web.”

CASI had already lost staff a year ago. In an October 2025 quarterly update, the institute said a Defense Department efficiency drive had eliminated its director of education and education program manager positions as the Department of the Air Force was “reorganizing, inactivating, and realigning organizations.” CASI said things were “in flux” and it would provide a status update once it knew more.

Ryan Fedasiuk, a fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, called the move “a devastating loss for the analytic community” and an “incomprehensible decision.”

The Air Force said CASI’s mission will continue, with military members carrying on the work Mulvaney said civilians have always done.

Michael Scanlon is a defense journalist covering air and space warfare. A former U.S. Air Force A-10 crew chief, he has supported land and sea programs for the U.S. Army, Navy, Marine Corps and Coast Guard.

10月1日，美国空军将裁撤中国航空航天研究所（China Aerospace Studies Institute）的全部10个文职岗位。该研究所是空军大学下设中心，负责发布有关中国人民解放军空中、太空和导弹力量的机密研究。该研究所所长表示，此举将实际上终止该研究所，尽管空军方面称CASI的任务仍将继续。

“作为空军教育与训练司令部正在进行的文职人员重组的一部分，将不再向中国航空航天研究所（CASI）分配文职岗位，”一名空军发言人周二在给《防务新闻》的声明中说。“CASI的任务仍在继续，该机构将利用所分配的军人来完成其目标。”

该发言人说，受重组影响的文职人员将留在当前岗位，直至另行通知，并将接受重新分配评估。

CASI主任布伦丹·马尔瓦尼（Brendan Mulvaney）对影响的描述有所不同。他周二说，该研究所所有文职编制都将被裁撤，“实际上终结了CASI”。他说，没有军职岗位受到影响，并指出该研究所拥有两个军士长编制和一个已空缺一年多的副主任职位。

当被问及此次裁撤将如何影响该研究所的研究时，马尔瓦尼说：“所有研究一直都是由文职人员完成的。”

据马尔瓦尼称，这一决定由前任空军大学司令作出，并由空军教育与训练司令部根据在整个空军部裁减文职岗位的要求转呈。他说，该配额源自空军人力与预备役事务办公室。

马尔瓦尼说，此次裁撤“与CASI的任务无关”，而是因为该研究所不培养职业军事教育学员，而这是空军大学的主要任务。

当被问及是否有其他机构将接手CASI的中国航空航天研究时，马尔瓦尼说：“尚未确定任何机构。”他说，目前也不清楚CASI的报告、翻译和课程材料是否会继续公开提供，其网站是否会继续在线。

这些削减于周一公开，当时一份来自CASI文职人员的说明在社交媒体上流传。该员工写道，自10月1日起，CASI所有文职岗位都将失去经费，工作人员将成为“富余联邦雇员”，这是联邦人事术语，指岗位被撤销的工作人员。

该说明将CASI的未来描述为“不确定”，并补充说，“鉴于我们团队和预算规模很小，CASI发挥出了超出自身分量的作用。”

美国海军水面战军官威尔·耶尔（Will Yale）在X上发布了这份说明，他写道，美国空军部“决定关闭”CASI是“极其不幸和令人遗憾的”。他称该研究所是其领域内最知名的机构之一，并写道，它“显著增进了美国政府内外对解放军的了解”。

美国海军战争学院教授、CASI兼职研究员安德鲁·埃里克森（Andrew Erickson）指出，这一消息“仅针对CASI”。马尔瓦尼（Mulvaney）表示，此举不影响海军中国海事研究所、陆军战争学院中国陆权研究中心或海军陆战队战争学院中国作战倡议。

CASI成立于2017年，并于2021年6月15日由时任空军参谋长小查尔斯·Q·布朗（Charles Q. Brown Jr.）上将正式批准设立。该章程责成该研究所研究中国“一切会飞的东西”，称CASI是空军研究中国及其航空航天能力的首要中心。该研究所在阿拉巴马州麦克斯韦空军基地和华盛顿的麦克奈尔堡设有办公室。

根据其章程，该研究所的研究在性质上属于非机密，章程要求CASI使用公开可得的母语来源并公布研究结果。CASI翻译了解放军教材和条令，出版了参考入门读物，并开办了为期三天、无需安全许可的免费“解放军基础”课程。

CASI表示，其每两年举办一次的CASI会议于5月在国防大学举行，吸引了250多名与会者，并发布了其《解放军航空航天力量》入门读本的第五版。

据该研究所称，2025年，近8万人访问了CASI网站，下载了5万多份报告。该网站仍在运行，并于9月21日发布了一篇新论文《从愿景到警戒：北京的空间科学路线图如何构建实时杀伤网》。

一年前，CASI就已经流失了人员。在2025年10月的季度更新中，该研究所表示，国防部的一项效率推进计划裁撤了其教育主任和教育项目经理职位，原因是空军部正在“重组、撤编和调整机构”。CASI称情况“仍在变化”，一旦了解更多信息，将提供最新状态。

美国企业研究所研究员瑞安·费达修克（Ryan Fedasiuk）称此举是“分析界的毁灭性损失”，也是一个“令人无法理解的决策”。

空军表示，CASI的任务将继续，由军人接续承担马尔瓦尼（Mulvaney）所说的文职人员一直以来所做的工作。

迈克尔·斯坎伦（Michael Scanlon）是一名报道空战与太空战的国防记者。作为前美国空军 A-10 机务长，他曾为美国陆军、海军、海军陆战队和海岸警卫队的地面和海上项目提供支持。

items.title: Greenland welcomes US military pact but trust still shaky
items.author: Tim Barsoe and Soren Jeppesen, Reuters
items.summary: Greenland’s government and residents expressed relief about a new military pact with the United States and Denmark.
items.body:
Greenland’s government and residents expressed relief that a military pact with the United States and Denmark may end anxiety over President Donald Trump’s threats to seize their Arctic island, but many remain distrustful of Washington.

“I am incredibly relieved and think the outcome is very sensible. We can be satisfied,” Naaja Nathanielsen, a Greenlandic MP in the Danish parliament, told Reuters.

Parliament speaker Kim Kielsen urged households to raise the Greenlandic flag on Wednesday. Activist and influencer Orla Joelsen encouraged residents in the capital, Nuuk, to show up at the airport to welcome the prime minister and foreign minister back from New York, where they struck the deal.

New US bases

The agreement allows the U.S. to expand its military presence on Greenland, reopening Cold War-era bases in the settlements of Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, with a prospect of renewed spending and employment potential.

But it stopped short of Trump’s unsettling previous demand that the U.S. annex Greenland to head off the growing Arctic presence of Russia and China.

“There has previously been a significant American presence in Greenland, so this is nothing new,” added Nathanielsen. “However, in light of the unrest over the past few years, there is likely greater scepticism in Greenland, and consequently, work needs to be done to reassure the local population.”

The U.S. first built military bases in Greenland during World War II. During the Cold War, it maintained 17 military installations and more than 10,000 personnel to monitor Soviet forces. Today, only Pituffik Space Base remains, with some 150 U.S. military personnel.

Pitanguaq Mikissen, 69, a retired ship assistant, said the potential reopening of some old U.S. bases gave greater security to the territory’s 57,000 people.

But not all residents were happy.

“I think that Trump is really good at creating a lot of worry and a lot of fear,” said Jensia Dam-Davidsen, 40, a voice and choir teacher.

“It (the deal) seems wrong in every way — especially now that Denmark has expanded their military presence here.”

Denmark has significantly increased its own military footprint in Greenland since Trump’s threats peaked in January, deploying additional troops, boosting Arctic defence spending and hosting allies under military exercises.

Malene Vahl Rasmussen, mayor of Kujalleq municipality in southern Greenland, where the U.S. is looking to reopen the Narsasuaq military base, said that under the agreement, U.S. military expansion must respect the Greenlandic way of life to protect hunting and fishing.

“You can’t simply say, ‘OK, we’ve signed this, so now we trust you again’. Trust really needs to be rebuilt within that partnership,” she told Reuters.

Some Greenlanders worry that expanded military activity — including increased aircraft and vessel movement — could disrupt hunting and fishing grounds that communities rely on for a living, though the agreement states such activity must respect Greenlandic society and traditional ways of life.

格陵兰政府和居民表示宽慰，认为与美国和丹麦达成的军事协议或许能消除因唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）总统威胁夺取其北极岛屿而引发的焦虑，但许多人仍不信任华盛顿。

“我感到无比宽慰，认为这一结果非常明智。我们可以感到满意，”丹麦议会中的格陵兰议员娜娅·纳撒尼尔森（Naaja Nathanielsen）对路透社表示。

议会议长金·基尔森（Kim Kielsen）敦促各家各户在周三升起格陵兰旗帜。活动人士兼网红奥拉·约尔森（Orla Joelsen）鼓励首都努克（Nuuk）的居民前往机场，欢迎从纽约归来的总理和外交部长，他们正是在那里达成了该协议。

美国新基地

该协议允许美国扩大在格陵兰的军事存在，重新启用位于纳萨尔苏瓦克（Narsarsuaq）和梅斯特斯维格（Mestersvig）居民点的冷战时期基地，并有望重新带来开支和就业潜力。

但该协议没有满足特朗普此前令人不安的要求，即美国吞并格陵兰，以阻止俄罗斯和中国在北极日益增长的存在。

“此前美国在格陵兰已有显著存在，因此这并非新鲜事，”纳撒尼尔森补充道。“然而，鉴于过去几年的动荡，格陵兰很可能存在更大疑虑，因此需要开展工作以安抚当地民众。”

美国在二战期间首次在格陵兰修建军事基地。冷战期间，美国维持了17处军事设施和超过1万名人员，以监视苏联军队。如今，仅剩皮图菲克太空基地（Pituffik Space Base），驻有约150名美国军事人员。

69岁的退休船舶助理皮坦瓜克·米基森（Pitanguaq Mikissen）表示，一些旧美军基地可能重新启用，这给该地区5.7万居民带来了更大的安全保障。

但并非所有居民都感到高兴。

“我认为特朗普（Trump）非常擅长制造大量担忧和恐惧，”40岁的声乐与合唱教师延西亚·达姆-戴维森（Jensia Dam-Davidsen）说。

“这（这项协议）似乎从各方面看都是错的——尤其是现在丹麦已经扩大了在这里的军事存在。”

自特朗普（Trump）的威胁在1月达到顶峰以来，丹麦已大幅扩大其在格陵兰的军事存在，增派部队、增加北极防务开支，并接待参加军事演习的盟友。

美国正寻求在格陵兰南部库雅雷克市镇重新启用纳尔萨苏阿克军事基地。该市镇市长马莱娜·瓦尔·拉斯穆森（Malene Vahl Rasmussen）表示，根据协议，美国的军事扩张必须尊重格陵兰人的生活方式，以保护狩猎和捕鱼。

“你不能简单地说，‘好吧，我们签了这个，所以现在我们又信任你了’。信任确实需要在这一伙伴关系中重建，”她告诉路透社。

一些格陵兰人担心，扩大的军事活动——包括飞机和船只往来增加——可能扰乱一些社区赖以谋生的狩猎和捕鱼区，尽管协议规定此类活动必须尊重格陵兰社会和传统生活方式。

美国正寻求在格陵兰南部库雅雷克市镇重新启用纳尔萨苏阿克军事基地。该市镇市长马莱娜·瓦尔·拉斯穆森（Malene Vahl Rasmussen）表示，根据协议，美国的军事扩张必须尊重格陵兰人的生活方式，以保护狩猎和捕鱼。
“你不能简单地说，‘好吧，我们签了这个，所以现在我们又信任你了’。信任确实需要在这一伙伴关系中重建，”她告诉路透社。
一些格陵兰人担心，扩大的军事活动——包括飞机和船只往来增加——可能扰乱一些社区赖以谋生的狩猎和捕鱼区，尽管协议规定此类活动必须尊重格陵兰社会和传统生活方式。

items.title: Department of the Air Force pilot program expands to help more military spouses
items.author: Jennifer Gonzalez
items.summary: Administered by the AFPC and AFCS, the initiative connects active-duty spouses undergoing a permanent change of station with direct hiring opportunities.
items.body:
Published Sept. 23, 2026

By Jennifer Gonzalez

Air Force Personnel Center

A professional in her own right, Kayla Amie holds a master’s degree in organizational leadership and a Bachelor of Science in education, and has worked steadily since she was legally old enough to hold a job. But when she married a U.S. Air Force Airman, that professional background no longer guaranteed a career and steady income. “Every four years you are starting from scratch. I am ok with pivoting but it’s going from the fact that you worked so hard—being a professional—and having it taken away with each move and it not being your choice,” said Amie.

items.title: German defense minister sees smooth sailing in parliament for his record defense budget
items.author: Linus Höller
items.summary: Pistorius is asking lawmakers to approve nearly €140 billion ($160 billion) for defense next year, a record sum.
items.body:
VIENNA — German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius told reporters after a Bundestag defense committee hearing on Wednesday that lawmakers had shown “much agreement” on his ministry’s record 2027 budget request, even as he pushed back against criticism that Germany is buying too much legacy hardware rather than new technology.

Pistorius is asking parliament to approve nearly €140 billion ($160 billion) for defense next year, combining €109.7 billion from the core ministry budget — a 32.7% increase over 2026 — with roughly €30 billion drawn from the expiring Sondervermögen Bundeswehr, a special off-budget fund created in 2022 following Russia’s attack on Ukraine.

The committee session Wednesday was part of ongoing scrutiny before the Bundestag’s final vote, expected in the chamber’s third reading on Nov. 27, following a reconciliation session in the budget committee on November 12.

Speaking after the closed-door meeting, Pistorius rejected accusations — raised by some lawmakers and commentators — that the procurement plan favors old technology over modernization. He pointed to the Leopard 2A8 tank as a “high-tech” system rather than legacy equipment, and announced that the ministry will launch its first-ever dedicated funding program for civilian universities and research institutes working on defense-relevant technologies, including artificial intelligence and unmanned systems.

On the Franco-German Main Ground Combat System, Pistorius acknowledged that the program’s original design may not survive in its current form. A day earlier, Germany and France had published a joint announcement that the project would be transitioned to pursuing “platform-independent technology” rather than a main battle tank. Pistorius said Berlin and Paris would need to agree “in the coming weeks” on shifting toward “a different, restructured project” given a threat environment he described as markedly changed from four or five years ago. The joint next-generation tank concept traces back all the way to 2012.

Despite unified opposition from the right-wing AfD, the Greens and far-left Die Linke — who call the spending plan fiscally reckless or insufficiently transparent — the governing coalition holds the votes needed to pass the budget.

Linus Höller is Defense News' Europe correspondent and OSINT investigator. He reports on the arms deals, sanctions, and geopolitics shaping Europe and the world. He holds master’s degrees in WMD nonproliferation, terrorism studies, and international relations, and works in four languages: English, German, Russian, and Spanish.

维也纳——德国国防部长鲍里斯·皮斯托里乌斯（Boris Pistorius）周三在联邦议院国防委员会听证会后告诉记者，议员们对其部门创纪录的2027年预算请求表现出“很大共识”，同时他反驳了有关德国购买过多旧式硬件而非新技术的批评。

皮斯托里乌斯正请求议会批准明年近1400亿欧元（1600亿美元）的国防预算，其中包括来自该部核心预算的1097亿欧元——较2026年增长32.7%——以及从即将到期的“联邦国防军特别基金”（Sondervermögen Bundeswehr）中提取的约300亿欧元；该基金是2022年俄罗斯袭击乌克兰后设立的预算外特别基金。

周三的委员会会议是联邦议院最终投票前持续审查的一部分；最终投票预计于11月27日在议院三读中进行，此前预算委员会已于11月12日举行协调会议。

在闭门会议后发言时，皮斯托里乌斯驳斥了一些议员和评论人士提出的指控，即采购计划偏向旧技术而非现代化。他指出，Leopard 2A8坦克是“高科技”系统，而非遗留装备，并宣布该部将启动其有史以来首个专项资助计划，面向从事国防相关技术（包括人工智能和无人系统）研究的民用大学和研究机构。

关于法德“主要地面作战系统”（Main Ground Combat System），皮斯托里乌斯承认该项目的原始设计可能无法以当前形式存续。一天前，德国和法国发布联合声明称，该项目将转向追求“平台无关技术”，而非主战坦克。皮斯托里乌斯表示，鉴于他形容为与四五年前明显不同的威胁环境，柏林和巴黎需要“在未来几周内”就转向“一个不同且经重组调整的项目”达成一致。这一联合下一代坦克概念可追溯至2012年。

尽管右翼的德国选择党（AfD）、绿党和极左翼的左翼党（Die Linke）一致反对——他们称该支出计划在财政上鲁莽或不够透明——执政联盟仍拥有通过预算所需的票数。

利努斯·赫勒（Linus Höller）是《防务新闻》（Defense News）欧洲通讯员和开源情报（OSINT）调查员。他报道塑造欧洲和世界的军火交易、制裁和地缘政治。他拥有大规模杀伤性武器防扩散、恐怖主义研究和国际关系硕士学位，并以四种语言工作：英语、德语、俄语和西班牙语。

items.title: Europe’s push to reduce US reliance is reshaping the defense space market
items.author: Rudy Ruitenberg
items.summary: Spooked by U.S. restrictions on satellite data access during recent crises, European countries are scrambling to catch up on sovereign capabilities.
items.body:
PARIS — Demand for sovereign satellite capabilities is growing in Europe as governments seek greater control over access to relevant infrastructure.

The push comes after restrictions by the United States on satellite access in Ukraine and the Middle East over the past two years underscored the risk of dependence, executives and policy makers said at an industry conference here last week.

“Sovereignty” was a recurring theme at the World Space Business Week, held from Sept. 14 to 17 in Paris, and the two-day Space Defense & Security Summit side event.

U.S. firms touted their ability to build satellites in Europe or operate free from International Traffic in Arms Regulations, while European companies highlighted their ability to provide local clients with complete satellite systems.

“The drive to sovereignty, we all have customers that want to go there,” said Noam Segal, the chief executive officer of Israeli firm ImageSat International, or ISI. “Any of the defense customers we are dealing with can find themselves in a geopolitical situation in which one of the suppliers will not be able to deliver. I think this is the driver.”

The war in Ukraine has highlighted both the importance of satellite data on the modern battlefield and the reliance of Western militaries on U.S. suppliers for critical space capabilities. Restrictions on Starlink access in Ukraine, a halt in U.S. intelligence sharing with Ukraine in March 2025 and imagery restrictions over the Middle East in 2026 are pushing European countries to seek sovereign alternatives.

The lesson from Ukraine has been to show how critical space has become for defense, as well as “the importance of indeed not being reliant on solutions you don’t control,” said Guillaume de la Brosse, head of the defense policy and innovation unit at the European Commission, the European Union’s executive arm.

He said there is a “clear imperative” to accelerate development of sovereign space-based capabilities in Europe, meaning a minimum backbone of public assets owned by either the EU or member states, and an EU-based industry able to provide sovereign services “that we can control all the time.”

“Sovereignty very much matters, this is what we’ve learned from Ukraine,” De la Brosse said. “That does not preclude the fact that we need cooperation, whatever happens, but that as a pre-requirement has sovereignty. It’s good to cut dependencies where we need to cut dependencies, and that’s very much the agenda of the upcoming years.”

Recent history showed space sovereignty is the only ultimate guarantee of having the freedom to “assess and act when conflict breaks out,” said Jean-Baptiste Paing, a deputy director at France’s Directorate General for Armament whose responsibilities include intelligence and space operations. He cited the difficulty obtaining commercial satellite communications over Afghanistan and, more recently, access to commercial imaging during the various crises in the Middle East.

The emergence of New Space, the shift from a government-dominated to a private space industry that has cut the cost of launchers and satellites, is allowing European governments to establish space sovereignty even with relatively limited budgets, executives said.

The number of intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance satellites for defense purposes, “a key priority for most nations,” is expected to increase more than fourfold through to 2035, according to industry consultancy Novaspace, which organized the conferences.

New Space provides “an incredible opportunity” for countries that didn’t have a space industry to develop their own sovereign capabilities, said Vincent Dedieu, the CEO of Sodern, a unit of France’s ArianeGroup. He said Sodern has been working with countries such as Poland, Bulgaria and Finland, which are taking advantage of New Space to catch up in both defense and commercial space.

The fact that customers are now able to own space assets at a “completely different cost point” from the past means the push for sovereign capabilities “is a strong trend that’s going to be there for the future,” according to Segal at ISI.

There is a “seismic shift” in how industry and governments deal with space capabilities, said Julia Gottfriedsen, chief technology officer at German thermal-imaging startup Constellr. She cited the example of Germany buying data from ICEYE and Rheinmetall for its brigade in Lithuania, through a service-level agreement that shifted the risk for data supply to the companies.

“So this is pretty modern and new, while in parallel, of course, the governments are also looking into procuring their own infrastructure,” Gottfriedsen said.

Executives at U.S.-based geospatial intelligence firms such as Planet Labs, BlackSky and Vantor all noted that their satellites can be delivered ITAR-free, with several highlighting their European presence or ability to manufacture their satellites outside the Untied States.

HawkEye 360 CEO John Serafini said partnerships with Italy’s Leonardo and Czechia’s ERA and having a Luxembourg subsidiary means he’s confident that “even as a U.S. company,” the firm can meet the requirement of European militaries “regardless of how those customers want the sovereignty delivered to them.”

Planet Labs cut the ribbon on a new facility in Berlin this week, and co-Founder and Chief Strategy Officer Robbie Schingler said the company’s first German-built Pelican satellite is set to come off the production line by the end of the year and sent into orbit on a German-built Isar Aerospace rocket launched from Norway “sometime early next year.”

Meanwhile, Finland’s ICEYE is taking sovereignty “to a whole different level” to fulfill a German order for a 40-satellite constellation, setting up a manufacturing site in western Germany controlled by a German-owned entity and keeping the entire supply chain within the country, according to CEO Rafal Modrzewski. That does require a sufficiently large order to justify the investment, he said.

For European customers that own and operate a smaller number of ICEYE satellites, such as Sweden, Finland, Poland and the Netherlands, the company is now offering a software layer that allows countries to “federate their assets at the tactical level” and borrow each other’s capabilities to cover areas of interest, Modrzewski said.

One element of sovereignty is assurance and control, another is choice, said Schingler at Planet Labs. The federation approach allows countries to network their systems for an ad hoc mission, “and that choice also gives a lot of sovereignty,” he said.

The European Commission is pushing for international cooperation to remain the way of doing things in space, including through discussions with NATO about space security, even if “that cooperation is very much challenged, and there is a need for Europeans to do much more, investing in their freedom of action,” De la Brosse said.

He said that as EU members invest heavily in space, one challenge is to avoid “renationalization of space policies,” and the commission is using the EU budget to provide an incentive to member states to coordinate investments and pool space resources rather than develop constellations without taking other member states into account.

Germany’s plan to invest a “massive” €35 billion in sovereign military space capabilities by 2030 may raise concern among some EU members that the country will “fly solo,” but the investment is a legitimate sovereign choice, said Paing at the DGA.

“I cannot speak for sovereignty myself without recognizing the same capacity in other countries, and I think it should be seen more as a model to follow for others rather than something to be afraid of,” Paing said. “That being said, I believe that this investment should nevertheless be put at the service of building a stronger Europe.”

Sovereignty also includes the ability to get satellites into orbit, executives said, with several remarking on the scarcity of launch slots. Nicolas Lefort, the head of new markets at MBDA, said France’s Toutatis project to bring a maneuverable satellite into low-Earth orbit is still waiting for a launcher.

François Lombard, the head of connected intelligence at Airbus Defence and Space, said he’s optimistic about new European players offering launchers capable of carrying one-ton payloads into LEO, citing a recent successful launch by Germany’s Isar Aerospace, as well as ArianeGroup’s MaiaSpace coming to the market “pretty soon.”

“In that case, European alternatives, which is good,” Lombard said. “There are a few satellites we cannot launch from other continents, so it’s important that we have also the sovereign access to space for this class of satellites in a competitive manner.”

Rudy Ruitenberg is a Europe correspondent for Defense News. He started his career at Bloomberg News and has experience reporting on technology, commodity markets and politics.

巴黎——随着各国政府寻求对相关基础设施的使用拥有更大控制权，欧洲对自主卫星能力的需求正在增长。

高管和政策制定者上周在此间举行的一场行业会议上表示，这一推动力源于过去两年美国对乌克兰和中东卫星使用施加的限制，这些限制凸显了依赖他国的风险。

9月14日至17日在巴黎举行的世界太空商业周，以及为期两天的配套活动太空防务与安全峰会，“主权”是一个反复出现的主题。

美国公司宣扬其能够在欧洲建造卫星，或不受《国际武器贸易条例》约束地运营；而欧洲公司则强调其有能力为当地客户提供完整的卫星系统。

“追求主权的动力——我们都有想要朝这个方向走的客户，”以色列公司ImageSat International（简称ISI）首席执行官诺姆·西格尔（Noam Segal）说。“我们所接触的任何防务客户都可能陷入这样一种地缘政治处境：其中一个供应商将无法交付。我认为这就是驱动因素。”

乌克兰战争既凸显了卫星数据在现代战场上的重要性，也凸显了西方军队在关键太空能力上对美国供应商的依赖。对乌克兰境内Starlink使用的限制、2025年3月美国暂停与乌克兰的情报共享，以及2026年对中东地区的图像限制，正推动欧洲国家寻求自主替代方案。

欧盟执行机构欧盟委员会防务政策与创新部门负责人纪尧姆·德·拉布罗斯（Guillaume de la Brosse）表示，乌克兰危机的教训表明太空对防务已变得何等关键，同时也显示了“不依赖你无法控制的解决方案确实十分重要”。

他说，加速发展欧洲自主天基能力存在“明确的紧迫性”，这意味着至少要有一个由欧盟或成员国拥有的公共资产骨干，以及一个总部位于欧盟、能够提供“我们始终能够控制”的自主服务的产业。

“主权至关重要，这是我们从乌克兰身上学到的，”德拉布罗斯（De la Brosse）说。“这并不排除我们无论如何都需要合作，但前提是主权。在我们需要切断依赖的地方切断依赖是好事，而这正是未来几年的议程。”

近期历史表明，太空主权是拥有在“冲突爆发时进行评估并采取行动”自由的唯一终极保障，法国军备总局（Directorate General for Armament）副局长让-巴蒂斯特·潘（Jean-Baptiste Paing）说，其职责包括情报与太空行动。他举例说，在阿富汗上空获取商业卫星通信十分困难，而更近一些时候，在中东的各种危机期间获取商业成像数据也同样困难。

业内人士表示，“新太空”（New Space）的兴起——即从政府主导转向私营航天产业，从而降低了运载火箭和卫星的成本——正使欧洲各国政府即便在预算相对有限的情况下也能建立太空主权。

据组织这些会议的行业咨询公司Novaspace称，用于国防目的的情报、监视与侦察卫星数量——“大多数国家的关键优先事项”——预计到2035年将增长四倍以上。

新太空为那些原本没有航天产业的国家提供了发展自身主权能力的“难以置信的机遇”，法国阿丽亚娜集团（ArianeGroup）旗下Sodern公司首席执行官樊尚·德迪厄（Vincent Dedieu）说。他说，Sodern一直在与波兰、保加利亚和芬兰等国合作，这些国家正利用新太空在国防和商业航天领域迎头赶上。

ISI的塞加尔（Segal）认为，客户如今能够以与过去“完全不同的成本水平”拥有太空资产，这意味着对主权能力的追求“是一个强劲的趋势，未来将持续存在”。

德国热成像初创公司Constellr首席技术官尤利娅·戈特弗里德森（Julia Gottfriedsen）说，产业界与政府在处理太空能力的方式上出现了“剧变”。她举例说，德国通过一项服务级别协议，为驻立陶宛的旅从ICEYE和莱茵金属（Rheinmetall）购买数据，该协议将数据供应的风险转移给了企业。

“所以这相当现代、相当新，而与此同时，政府当然也在考虑采购自己的基础设施，”戈特弗里德森说。

美国地理空间情报公司 Planet Labs、BlackSky 和 Vantor 的高管均指出，他们的卫星可以不受 ITAR 限制地交付，其中几家还强调自身在欧洲的存在，或在美国境外制造卫星的能力。

HawkEye 360 首席执行官约翰·塞拉菲尼 (John Serafini) 表示，与意大利的 Leonardo 和捷克的 ERA 建立合作伙伴关系，并在卢森堡设有子公司，意味着他有信心，该公司“即使作为一家美国公司”，也能满足欧洲军方的要求，“无论这些客户希望主权以何种方式交付到他们手中”。

Planet Labs 本周在柏林为新设施举行了剪彩仪式。联合创始人兼首席战略官罗比·欣格勒 (Robbie Schingler) 表示，该公司首颗德国制造的 Pelican 卫星将于今年年底下线，并于“明年年初某个时候”由从挪威发射的德国制造 Isar Aerospace 火箭送入轨道。

与此同时，芬兰的 ICEYE 正将主权“提升到一个完全不同的层次”，以履行德国一份由 40 颗卫星组成的星座订单。据首席执行官拉法尔·莫德泽夫斯基 (Rafal Modrzewski) 称，该公司正在德国西部设立一个由德资实体控制的制造基地，并将整个供应链留在德国境内。他说，这确实需要足够大的订单来证明这笔投资的合理性。

莫德泽夫斯基表示，对于拥有并运营少量 ICEYE 卫星的欧洲客户，例如瑞典、芬兰、波兰和荷兰，该公司现在提供一层软件，使各国能够“在战术层面将其资产联邦化”，并相互借用能力来覆盖关注区域。

Planet Labs 的欣格勒表示，主权的一个要素是保障与控制，另一个要素是选择。联邦式方式使各国能够为临时任务将其系统联网，“而这种选择也赋予了大量主权，”他说。

德·拉布罗斯 (De la Brosse) 表示，欧盟委员会正推动将国际合作继续作为太空领域的行事方式，包括与北约就太空安全进行讨论，即便“这种合作正面临很大挑战，欧洲人也需要做得更多，投资于自身的行动自由”。

他说，随着欧盟成员国在太空领域大举投资，一个挑战是避免“太空政策再国家化”，欧盟委员会正利用欧盟预算激励成员国协调投资、汇集太空资源，而不是在不顾及其他成员国的情况下发展星座。

德国计划到2030年前向主权军事太空能力投资“巨额”350亿欧元，这可能引发一些欧盟成员国担忧该国将“单飞”，但DGA的潘（Paing）表示，这项投资是合法的主权选择。

潘（Paing）说：“如果不承认其他国家也具备同样的能力，我就不能自己谈主权；我认为这更应被视为其他国家效仿的榜样，而不是令人恐惧的事情。”“话虽如此，我认为这项投资仍应服务于建设一个更强大的欧洲。”

高管们表示，主权还包括将卫星送入轨道的能力，有几位高管提到发射名额稀缺。MBDA新市场主管尼古拉·勒福尔（Nicolas Lefort）表示，法国旨在将一颗可机动卫星送入低地球轨道的Toutatis项目仍在等待运载火箭。

空中客车防务与航天公司互联情报负责人弗朗索瓦·隆巴尔（François Lombard）表示，他对欧洲新兴企业提供能够将one-ton有效载荷送入LEO的运载火箭感到乐观，并提到德国Isar Aerospace最近的发射成功，以及ArianeGroup的MaiaSpace“很快”将进入市场。

隆巴尔说：“那样的话，就有欧洲的替代方案，这是好事。”“有少数卫星我们无法从其他大陆发射，因此，我们以有竞争力的方式为这类卫星拥有主权进入太空的能力也很重要。”

鲁迪·鲁滕贝格（Rudy Ruitenberg）是《防务新闻》驻欧洲记者。他的职业生涯始于彭博新闻社，在报道技术、大宗商品市场和政治方面拥有经验。
zhParas: 巴黎——随着各国政府寻求对相关基础设施的使用拥有更大控制权，欧洲对自主卫星能力的需求正在增长。
高管和政策制定者上周在此间举行的一场行业会议上表示，这一推动力源于过去两年美国对乌克兰和中东卫星使用施加的限制，这些限制凸显了依赖他国的风险。
9月14日至17日在巴黎举行的世界太空商业周，以及为期两天的配套活动太空防务与安全峰会，“主权”是一个反复出现的主题。
美国公司宣扬其能够在欧洲建造卫星，或不受《国际武器贸易条例》约束地运营；而欧洲公司则强调其有能力为当地客户提供完整的卫星系统。
“追求主权的动力——我们都有想要朝这个方向走的客户，”以色列公司ImageSat International（简称ISI）首席执行官诺姆·西格尔（Noam Segal）说。“我们所接触的任何防务客户都可能陷入这样一种地缘政治处境：其中一个供应商将无法交付。我认为这就是驱动因素。”
乌克兰战争既凸显了卫星数据在现代战场上的重要性，也凸显了西方军队在关键太空能力上对美国供应商的依赖。对乌克兰境内Starlink使用的限制、2025年3月美国暂停与乌克兰的情报共享，以及2026年对中东地区的图像限制，正推动欧洲国家寻求自主替代方案。
欧盟执行机构欧盟委员会防务政策与创新部门负责人纪尧姆·德·拉布罗斯（Guillaume de la Brosse）表示，乌克兰危机的教训表明太空对防务已变得何等关键，同时也显示了“不依赖你无法控制的解决方案确实十分重要”。
他说，加速发展欧洲自主天基能力存在“明确的紧迫性”，这意味着至少要有一个由欧盟或成员国拥有的公共资产骨干，以及一个总部位于欧盟、能够提供“我们始终能够控制”的自主服务的产业。
“主权至关重要，这是我们从乌克兰身上学到的，”德拉布罗斯（De la Brosse）说。“这并不排除我们无论如何都需要合作，但前提是主权。在我们需要切断依赖的地方切断依赖是好事，而这正是未来几年的议程。”
近期历史表明，太空主权是拥有在“冲突爆发时进行评估并采取行动”自由的唯一终极保障，法国军备总局（Directorate General for Armament）副局长让-巴蒂斯特·潘（Jean-Baptiste Paing）说，其职责包括情报与太空行动。他举例说，在阿富汗上空获取商业卫星通信十分困难，而更近一些时候，在中东的各种危机期间获取商业成像数据也同样困难。
业内人士表示，“新太空”（New Space）的兴起——即从政府主导转向私营航天产业，从而降低了运载火箭和卫星的成本——正使欧洲各国政府即便在预算相对有限的情况下也能建立太空主权。
据组织这些会议的行业咨询公司Novaspace称，用于国防目的的情报、监视与侦察卫星数量——“大多数国家的关键优先事项”——预计到2035年将增长四倍以上。
新太空为那些原本没有航天产业的国家提供了发展自身主权能力的“难以置信的机遇”，法国阿丽亚娜集团（ArianeGroup）旗下Sodern公司首席执行官樊尚·德迪厄（Vincent Dedieu）说。他说，Sodern一直在与波兰、保加利亚和芬兰等国合作，这些国家正利用新太空在国防和商业航天领域迎头赶上。
ISI的塞加尔（Segal）认为，客户如今能够以与过去“完全不同的成本水平”拥有太空资产，这意味着对主权能力的追求“是一个强劲的趋势，未来将持续存在”。
德国热成像初创公司Constellr首席技术官尤利娅·戈特弗里德森（Julia Gottfriedsen）说，产业界与政府在处理太空能力的方式上出现了“剧变”。她举例说，德国通过一项服务级别协议，为驻立陶宛的旅从ICEYE和莱茵金属（Rheinmetall）购买数据，该协议将数据供应的风险转移给了企业。
“所以这相当现代、相当新，而与此同时，政府当然也在考虑采购自己的基础设施，”戈特弗里德森说。
美国地理空间情报公司 Planet Labs、BlackSky 和 Vantor 的高管均指出，他们的卫星可以不受 ITAR 限制地交付，其中几家还强调自身在欧洲的存在，或在美国境外制造卫星的能力。

items.title: Germany wants to manufacture American PAC-3 interceptors to help meet global demand
items.author: Sebastian Sprenger
items.summary: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has lobbied U.S. defense leaders to allow the production of PAC-3 MSE interceptor missiles in Germany.
items.body:
COLOGNE, Germany — German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has lobbied U.S. defense leaders to allow the production of PAC-3 MSE interceptor missiles in Germany, arguing an additional production site would help alleviate a glaring shortfall in the global supply chain for the vital air-defense weapons.

Pistorius’ comments in Berlin on Wednesday offer more details about an agreement struck with his U.S. counterpart, Pete Hegseth, at the Pentagon last week.

The German defense minister said the spirit of that accord reflects Berlin’s willingness to manufacture all elements of the Patriot value chain — PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors, launchers and all — in Germany, plus whatever other American weaponry is in short supply among allies.

Germany’s MBDA already makes PAC-2 interceptors, a Raytheon product. The more advanced, and more expensive, PAC-3 MSE interceptors, on the other hand, are made by Lockheed Martin, which has a longstanding cooperation agreement in Germany with Rheinmetall, including in the missile sector.

Whether PAC-3 production in Germany or elsewhere in Europe will come to pass is largely a matter of the U.S. government and Lockheed Martin playing along. Details would likely also depend on the scope of work happening abroad.

The performance characteristics of Patriot interceptors are a closely guarded secret, as that information could allow adversaries to build countermeasures into their attack missiles. There is also a business decision wrapped up in the export of Patriot production, as the equipment has been a decades-old cash cow for the manufacturers and the U.S. government alike.

Ukrainian leaders said in July they were promised by U.S. President Donald Trump that they would be able to make Patriot interceptors under license in Ukraine, though the details of that arrangement remain unclear.

Patriot interceptors are a key defense against Russian missiles that have been battering Ukrainian cities.

Sebastian Sprenger is associate editor for Europe at Defense News, reporting on the state of the defense market in the region, and on U.S.-Europe cooperation and multi-national investments in defense and global security. Previously he served as managing editor for Defense News. He is based in Cologne, Germany.

德国科隆——德国国防部长鲍里斯·皮斯托里乌斯（Boris Pistorius）已游说美国防务领导人允许在德国生产PAC-3 MSE拦截导弹，称增设一个生产基地将有助于缓解这一关键防空武器全球供应链中显而易见的短缺。

周三在柏林，皮斯托里乌斯（Pistorius）的表态披露了更多细节，涉及上周他与美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞思（Pete Hegseth）在五角大楼达成的一项协议。

该德国国防部长表示，该协议的精神反映了柏林方面愿意在德国制造“爱国者”价值链的所有环节——包括PAC-2和PAC-3拦截导弹、发射装置及全部相关组件——以及盟国中短缺的任何其他美国武器。

德国的MBDA已经在生产PAC-2拦截导弹，这是雷神（Raytheon）的产品。另一方面，更先进也更昂贵的PAC-3 MSE拦截导弹则由洛克希德·马丁（Lockheed Martin）制造，该公司与莱茵金属（Rheinmetall）在德国有长期合作协议，包括在导弹领域。

PAC-3能否在德国或欧洲其他地方投产，很大程度上取决于美国政府和洛克希德·马丁是否配合。具体细节还可能取决于海外承担的工作范围。

“爱国者”拦截导弹的性能特征属于严格保守的秘密，因为这类信息可能让对手在攻击导弹中内置对抗措施。出口“爱国者”生产还牵涉商业决策，因为该装备数十年来一直是制造商和美国政府的摇钱树。

乌克兰领导人7月表示，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）向他们承诺，他们将能够按许可在乌克兰生产“爱国者”拦截导弹，不过该安排的具体细节仍不清楚。

“爱国者”拦截导弹是防御俄罗斯导弹的关键手段，这些导弹一直猛烈打击乌克兰城市。

塞巴斯蒂安·施普伦格（Sebastian Sprenger）是《国防新闻》（Defense News）欧洲部副主编，负责报道该地区国防市场状况，以及美欧合作和国防与全球安全领域的多国投资。此前他曾担任《国防新闻》执行主编。他常驻德国科隆。

items.title: US Navy destroyers tested in Middle East as demands mount
items.author: Natalie Oliverio
items.summary: The concentration of Navy destroyers in the Middle East raises questions about meeting sustained operational demand.
items.body:
Navy destroyers are concentrated in the Middle East as U.S. forces conduct operations against Iran, according to U.S. Central Command — a move that puts renewed operational demands on a fleet that has experienced prolonged maintenance periods.

As of Sept. 14, two Navy guided-missile destroyers were operating in the Red Sea and another 13 were in the Arabian Sea, according to the U.S. Naval Institute’s fleet tracker, which uses both Navy and public data.

The Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Stout also departed Naval Station Norfolk on Monday to begin deployment operations after months of training, maintenance and certification events, according to Naval Surface Force Atlantic.

The demand facing the class has been significant, even before the start of the Iran war.

The USS Carney spent 235 days deployed from September 2023 to May 2024 and conducted 51 engagements against Houthi-launched weapons, according to the Navy. The campaign demonstrated what operations around one of those chokepoints can demand from destroyers.

When USS Carney returned in May 2024, then-Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Lisa Franchetti told the crew that the last time the Navy had directly engaged an enemy to that degree was during World War II.

The renewed demand for destroyers in the Middle East comes as the Navy’s maintenance system has struggled to keep the fleet on schedule.

U.S. Fleet Forces Command declined to discuss its current destroyer readiness posture, current operations or potential effects on future deployment schedules, citing operational-security and classification guidelines. The command also declined to provide historical aggregate data on destroyer operational tempo.

According to a December 2025 Congressional Budget Office analysis of Navy maintenance data, the Arleigh Burke-class destroyer overhauls that began between 2011 and 2024 took an average of 26% longer than the Navy’s final schedules estimated.

The 225 DDG-51 overhauls CBO analyzed also required 8% more labor than scheduled.

CBO projected that DDG-51 destroyers will spend an average of more than nine years, or about 27% of their planned service lives, in maintenance. That is more than twice the roughly four years envisioned in the Navy’s 2012 class maintenance plans.

The federal budget agency identified several factors contributing to longer maintenance periods, including the aging fleet, postponed maintenance, late inspections and contract awards, unexpected additional work, delays in parts and materials and modernization work.

The average age of the DDG-51 fleet rose from 10 years in 2011 to 20 years in 2024.

The Government Accountability Office has found broader problems across the Navy’s conventional surface fleet.

In a January 2025 review, GAO found that the Navy requested nearly $24.9 billion for combat-surface-ship maintenance from fiscal 2020 through 2023 and reported that nearly $25.9 billion was appropriated. The Navy reported obligating 99.7% of that funding by the end of fiscal 2023. Yet, GAO found that the service continued to face shortages of spare parts, insufficient qualified maintenance personnel and a continuing need to defer maintenance.

CBO’s analysis covers maintenance events beginning in 2011 and points to longstanding factors, including the age of the destroyer fleet and postponed work.

Natalie Oliverio is an independent journalist and Navy veteran who covers military and veterans’ issues. Drawing on her experience as a talent executive and mentor, she writes about the policies, people and programs shaping the military community.

据美军中央司令部称，随着美军对伊朗开展行动，海军驱逐舰正集中部署在中东——此举给一支长期经历维护期的舰队带来了新的作战需求。

截至9月14日，根据美国海军学会（U.S. Naval Institute）的舰队追踪数据，两艘海军导弹驱逐舰正在红海行动，另有13艘在阿拉伯海；该追踪数据同时使用海军数据和公开数据。

据大西洋海军水面部队称，Arleigh Burke-class导弹驱逐舰USS Stout也于周一驶离诺福克海军基地，在历经数月训练、维护和认证活动后开始部署行动。

该级舰面临的需求一直十分巨大，甚至早在伊朗战争开始前就是如此。

据海军称，USS Carney从2023年9月至2024年5月期间部署了235天，并对胡塞武装发射的武器进行了51次交战。这场行动表明，在这些咽喉要道之一周边作战会对驱逐舰提出怎样的要求。

当USS Carney于2024年5月返回时，时任海军作战部长 Adm. 莉萨·弗兰凯蒂（Lisa Franchetti）告诉舰员，海军上一次如此程度地直接与敌人交战还是在第二次世界大战期间。

中东对驱逐舰的新需求出现之际，海军的维护体系一直难以让舰队按计划运行。

美国舰队部队司令部以行动安全和保密准则为由，拒绝讨论其当前驱逐舰战备态势、当前行动或对未来部署计划的潜在影响。该司令部还拒绝提供有关驱逐舰作战节奏的历史汇总数据。

根据美国国会预算办公室（CBO）2025年12月对海军维修数据的分析，2011年至2024年间启动的Arleigh Burke级驱逐舰大修，平均耗时比海军最终进度表估算的长26%。

CBO所分析的225次DDG-51大修，所需工时也比计划多8%。

CBO预测，DDG-51驱逐舰平均将在维修上花费九年以上，约占其计划服役寿命的27%。这比海军2012年舰级维修计划所设想的约四年多出一倍以上。

这家联邦预算机构指出，导致维修周期延长的因素有多个，包括舰队老化、维修推迟、检查与合同授予延迟、计划外的额外工作、零部件和材料延误以及现代化改装工作。

DDG-51舰队的平均舰龄从2011年的10年上升到2024年的20年。

美国政府问责局（GAO）发现，海军常规水面舰队存在范围更广的问题。

在2025年1月的一份审查报告中，GAO发现，海军在2020财年至2023财年为主战舰艇维修申请了近249亿美元，并报告称实际拨款近259亿美元。海军报告称，截至2023财年末已承付其中99.7%的资金。然而，GAO发现，该军种仍面临备件短缺、合格维修人员不足以及持续需要推迟维修的问题。

CBO的分析涵盖2011年开始的维修活动，并指向长期存在的因素，包括驱逐舰舰龄和推迟的工作。

娜塔莉·奥利韦里奥 (Natalie Oliverio) 是一名独立记者兼海军退伍军人，报道军事与退伍军人事务。她凭借作为人才高管和导师的经验，撰写有关塑造军人社区的政策、人物和项目的内容。

items.title: DM Airmen participate in Coyote Storm 26.2 to reinforce AEW 2.0 concepts
items.author: Capt. M. Anna Turpin
items.summary: The multi-day training event operationalized Air Expeditionary Wing 2.0 concepts across cross-functional disciplines, including field medicine, combat search and rescue, and command and control.
items.body:
Published Sept. 22, 2026

By Capt. M. Anna Turpin

355th Wing Public Affairs

Airmen from the 355th Wing strengthened their ability to operate in contested environments during Coyote Storm 26.2 at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base , Sept. 14-17. Coyote Storm 26.2 was a training exercise focused on improving flexibility and readiness through the Air Expeditionary Wing 2.0 concept. AEW 2.0 training requires that preparation for deployments happens long before members go into theater and ensures that they have the time to train together across disciplines.

作者：Capt. M. Anna Turpin

第355联队公共事务办公室

9月14日至17日，第355联队的空军人员在戴维斯-蒙森空军基地举行的“郊狼风暴”26.2演习中，增强了在对抗环境中作战的能力。“郊狼风暴”26.2是一场训练演习，重点是通过“空中远征联队2.0”概念提高灵活性和战备水平。AEW 2.0训练要求，部署准备工作要远在人员进入战区之前就进行，并确保他们有时间跨专业一起训练。
